name: Westerkeersluis
en: The Westerkeersluis (bridge 346) is a bascule bridge in Amsterdam-West. The bridge spans the Westerkanaal and is part of the Centrumring S100. It connects Van Diemenstraat with Tasmanstraat. North of the bridge, the wooden lock gates of the Westerkanaal flood barrier (lock 205) between the city and the IJ are visible.

name: Westertoren
en: The Westertoren in Amsterdam is the tower of the Westerkerk, at Prinsengracht 279 by the Westermarkt in Amsterdam-Centrum. The tower is owned by the city of Amsterdam. It was restored from February 2023 until early 2025.

name: Westerwijk
en: Westerwijk or Wester-wijk is a building in Amsterdam with houses, office space and two rooms. The building was built after a tender in June 1925 in 1925/1926 on the Admiraal de Ruyterweg to the design of F.B. Jantzen in the style of the Amsterdam School. The construction cost amounted to just under 80,000 guilders at the time.

name: Westhaven
en: The Westhaven is a port in the Western Port Area in Amsterdam and was built as part of the General Expansion Plan of 1934. en: Westkanaaldijk is a district in the north of the Lindenholt district in the Dutch city of Nijmegen. On January 1, 2023, the district had 5 residents, distributed over 5 houses, on an area of 1.22 km².

name: Westlandgracht
en: The Westlandgracht is a surface water, a street and until 1962 the name of a district and is named after the Westland, the area west of Delft and south of The Hague. name: Westlandgrachtsluis

name: Westplein

name: Westpoortweg
en: The Westpoortweg is an important continuous connection between Amsterdam Westpoort and the North Sea Canal and further towards Velsen-Zuid. en: The Westzeedijk is part of Schielands Hoge Zeedijk, the dike that was built in the 13th century to protect the area between Gouda, Leiden and Rotterdam from flooding. name: Weteringpoort
en: The Weteringpoort was one of the eight Amsterdam city gates that were built during the Third and Fourth Extensions of the city. The Weteringpoort, which was part of the fortifications of Amsterdam, was one of the smaller city gates together with the Raampoort and Zaagmolenpoort.

en: The Wezerhaven is a small docking port in Rotterdam's Europoort on the Caland Canal. Exxon Mobil Chemical Holland is located on the south side of the port and Caldic Chemie on the west side.

name: Wibautstraat
en: The Wibautstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost, between the Rhijnspoorplein and the Prins Bernhardplein and named after former alderman Floor Wibaut.

name: Wiegbrug
en: The Wiegbrug (bridge no. 173) is a movable bridge over the Kostverlorenvaart in Amsterdam-West, connecting the De Clercqstraat with the Admiraal de Ruijterweg. Its name refers to the type of bridge built here in 1904, a rolling bascule bridge.

name: Wijkerbrug
en: The Wijkerbrug in the Dutch town of Voorburg is a lift bridge over the Vliet dating back to 1891. During construction, the bridge was built as a fixed bridge. In 1919, the bridge was converted into a lift bridge. The bridge is a national monument.

name: Wijnhaven
en: The Wijnhaven is a harbor in the center of Rotterdam. The Wijnhaven is connected to the Oude Haven and the Leuvehaven. On the Wijnhaven stand the White House and the Marine Museum. The André van der Louw Bridge runs over the Wijnhaven. On the harbor are the Maasboulevard, Boompjes, Wijnhavenpunt, Scheepsmakerskade and the Wijnkade.

name: Wijttenbachstraat
en: The Wijttenbachstraat is a street in the Dapperbuurt in Amsterdam-Oost, between the corner Oosterpark-Linnaeusstraat and the railway viaduct near Pontanusstraat. name: Wil de Graaffbrug
en: The Wil de Graaffbrug (bridge 393) is a pedestrian bridge in Amsterdam-West. The bridge is located in the northeast of Erasmus Park and spans the Erasmusgracht, which lies just outside the park. The bridge lies in line with the Lof der zotheidbrug (bridge 394). The bridge dates back to 1970, when the park was completely redesigned at what was then great cost.

name: Wilhelminahaven
en: The Wilhelminahaven in the Dutch municipality of Schiedam is a port that was built between 1914 and 1921 on the northern side of the Nieuwe Maas. The port is located west of Vijfsluizen (Wiltonhaven), and east of the Spuihaven in Schiedam-Zuid.

name: Wilhelminakade
en: The Wilhelminakade is a street on the left bank of the Maas in Rotterdam. It has a rich history and in the first years of the 21st century there was much talk of high-rise buildings being built.

name: Wilhelminakerk
en: The Wilhelminakerk is a church building in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The church building was built around 1931 in the Schildersbuurt on the corner of Hobbemastraat and Paulus Potterstraat. The design in the style of the Amsterdam School comes from the architect H.F. Mertens. The building is valued as a municipal monument.

name: Wilhelminapark
en: The Wilhelminapark is a city park in the Dutch city of Utrecht. It is recognized as a national monument as one of the first parks in the Netherlands. The park is centrally located in Utrecht-Oost and east of Oudwijk. The surrounding neighborhood is called the Wilhelminaparkbuurt while a street along the park is also called Wilhelminapark.

name: Willem de Zwijgerkerk
en: The Willem de Zwijgerkerk is a Protestant church on Olympiaweg in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is a "neighborhood church" of the Protestant Church (PKN) in Amsterdam.

name: Willemsbrug
en: The Willemsbrug (bridge 151) is a bridge in Amsterdam-West over the Singelgracht between the Haarlemmerplein and the Nassauplein. This bascule bridge is named after the nearby Willemspoort. The construction of a bridge at this location became necessary after the construction of the Westerkanaal in 1877.

name: Willemsbrug

name: Willibrorduskapel
en: The Willibrorduskapel is a Catholic chapel in The Hague, located on the first floor of the Willibrordushuis at Oude Molstraat 35. The chapel is a municipal monument and was built in 1928 in the style of the Delft School, designed by the Hague architect Jos Duynstee, for the Sisters of Love from Tilburg. name: Wiltonhaven
en: The Wiltonhaven is a port in Schiedam on the Nieuwe Maas. Wilton-Fijenoord was based in this port, which was completed in 1924. In 2003, Damen took over this shipyard and it is now called Damen Shiprepair Rotterdam. North of it is the site of Huisman, while Mammoet has its headquarters on the west side of the port in the Vijfsluizerhaven.

name: Wim Ibobrug
en: Wim Ibobrug (bridge 1774) is a bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. The bridge was built as a connection between the dead-end roads Grasweg and Distelweg. It spans the Tolhuiskanaal. The bridge was built in the early 1990s and is almost entirely made of concrete.

name: Wim Suurbierbrug
en: The Wim Suurbierbrug (bridge 2239) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is one of the traffic bridges (the others are for slow traffic) that forms the connection within the Park de Meer neighborhood within the Watergraafsmeer, which rose from the ground here between 1998 and 2002.

name: Yaa Adu-Ampomabrug
en: The Yaa Adu-Ampomabrug, called the Reigersbospadbrug until 2023, is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Zaagpoort

name: Zaandijksspoorbrug
en: The Zaandijkspoorbrug is a railway bridge in Amsterdam-West. This railway bridge is a viaduct, or a tunnel, under the Oude Lijn between the Westerpark to the south and the Spaarndammerbuurt to the north. The all-concrete structure was built around 1979 to provide a better connection between the aforementioned park and neighborhood.

name: Zaanlijn
en: The Zaanlijn is the Uitgeest-Amsterdam section of the Den Helder-Amsterdam railway. It runs through the Zaanstreek and takes its name from the fact that much of the line runs parallel to the river Zaan.

name: Zandbrug
en: The Zandbrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the Utrecht city center. The late medieval bridge spans the Oudegracht. North of the Zandbrug is the access to the Stadsbuitengracht and the Vecht river with the Weerdsluis at the Bemuurde Weerd. Directly adjacent to the south side of the bridge are workshop basements and yards.

name: Zandhoeksbrug

en: The Zeeburgerdijk is a dike in Amsterdam-Oost. The Zeeburgerdijk extends along the Hoogte Kadijk and continues beyond the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal into the Diemerzeedijk. The former district of Zeeburg took its name from the Zeeburgerdijk and the Zeeburgereiland.

name: Zeilbrug
en: The Zeilbrug or Zeilstraatbrug (bridge no. 348) is a bridge over the Schinkel in Amsterdam. The bridge connects Zeilstraat and Hoofddorpweg and forms a connection between Oud-Zuid and the Hoofddorpplein neighborhood. Various documents from the municipality of Amsterdam only mentioned bridge 348; Zeilbrug was apparently not an official name.

name: Zeilstraat
en: The Zeilstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, between the Amstelveenseweg and the Schinkel. The Zeilstraat is known as a busy, main shopping street. It extends along the Koninginneweg.

name: Zevenblad
en: Zevenblad is a perennial plant from the Apiaceae family. The plant grows in shady places in hedges, gardens, roadside verges and field edges in moist or fertilized soil. The plant is also called hen comb, gardener's grief and heers.

name: Zevenhuizerplas
en: The Zevenhuizerplas is a Dutch lake artificially created by sand mining east of the Rotte River. It serves as a recreation lake and together with the surrounding area forms a recreation area. name: Zevenmanshaven
en: The Zevenmanshaven is a port in Vlaardingen. The port, like the Vulcaanhaven, is privately owned and is in the hands of the company Northcoast. The port is connected to the Nieuwe Maas. The Zevenmanshaven is located on the west side of Vlaardingen and owes its name to the former Zevenmanspolder.

name: Zijkanaal F
en: Zijkanaal F has been a canal in the Dutch province of North Holland since 1873. It is a branch of the North Sea Canal. From Halfweg, the North Sea Canal could be reached via the side canal F. This side canal was also an important drainage of the Halfweg steam pumping station of the High Authority of the Rhine-Westphalia to the North Sea Canal.

name: Zijkanaal H
en: The Zijkanaal H is a side channel of the North Sea Canal and connects the Barndegat on the border of Amsterdam and Zaandam to the North Sea Canal. The canal was put into use in 1876 simultaneously with the North Sea Canal. It is, viewed from IJmuiden, the eighth side channel.

name: Zijkanaal I
en: The Zijkanaal I (with the letter "I") is a waterway in Amsterdam-North. It forms the connection between the IJ in Amsterdam and the former Oostzaner Overtoom near Oostzanerwerf. name: Zocherstraat
en: The Zocherstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West. name: Zonnewendebrug
en: The Zonnewendebrug (bridge 2106) is a structure in Amsterdam-Centrum. The name refers to June 21 (21-06) on which the solstice takes place annually.

en: The Zorgvliedsluis or Zorgvliedschutsluis is a lock in the Nieuwe Wetering near the Zuidelijke Wandelweg in Amsterdam. On the east side of the lock lies a branch of the Nieuwe Wetering that has open connection with the Amstel at the Zorgvliedbrug.

name: Zouthavenbrug
en: The Willem Breukerbrug (bridge 2326) is a structure in Amsterdam-Centrum. Until 10 January 2024 it was called the Zouthavenbrug.

name: Zoutkeetsbrug

en: The Zuider Amstelkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid. The canal was dug as part of the Plan Zuid by architect H.P. Berlage and is part of the connection between the Amstel and the Schinkel. It forms the separation between Stadionbuurt and Apollobuurt and the Prinses Irenebuurt.

name: Zuidergasfabriekbrug

name: Zuiderzeeweg
en: The Zuiderzeeweg is the name of a number of Dutch roads, including in Amsterdam and Middenmeer. The name refers to the former Zuiderzee. The Zuiderzeeweg in Amsterdam connects Amsterdam-Oost with Amsterdam-North.

name: Zuidplein
en: The Zuidplein in Amsterdam-Zuid is the forecourt of Amsterdam Zuid station. The square is located in the Zuidas area. On the other side of Station Zuid is Gustav Mahlerplein. name: Zwarte Water
en: The Zwarte Water is an ancient watercourse in the Dutch city of Utrecht that flows into the Vecht River. The watercourse is located near Lauwerecht. At the height of the Vecht, the national monument Lauwerecht Bridge spans the Zwarte Water as a watercourse. The street on the north side is called Zwartewater and it continues into the Vogelenbuurt.

name: Plantage Middenlaan 10-12
en: Plantage Middenlaan 10-12 in Amsterdam are two buildings on the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. The two properties were probably built at the same time to a design by Georgius Breuker. He did not come from a building background, but worked his way up to carpenter and bricklayer in Amsterdam.

name: Plantage Middenlaan 48
en: Plantage Middenlaan 48 is a building from the last quarter of the nineteenth century on the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designated a municipal monument in 1991. In the 1870s there was intensive building in the 19th-century ring around Amsterdam, and the city's built-up area had also reached the Plantage district.

name: Plantage Middenlaan 4a
en: Plantage Middenlaan 4A in Amsterdam is a building on the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building was erected in the Plantage, an area that was booming with development around 1879.

name: Poeldijkstraat 7-253
en: Poeldijkstraat 7-253 in Amsterdam is a flat of townscape significance on the Poeldijkstraat, Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is locally known as the August Povelflat.

name: Polanentheater
en: The Polanentheater is a theatre on the Polanenstraat, Spaarndammerbuurt, Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Poldergemaal Nico Broekhuysen
en: The Poldergemaal Nico Broekhuysen is a pumping station in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, close to Park de Kuil. Its primary purpose is to pump excess water from the northern part of the Osdorper Binnenpolder.

name: Polderhuis (Rustenburgerstraat)
en: The Polderhuis in the Pijp district of Amsterdam-Zuid is a workers' house built in 1865, commissioned by Jan van Bemmel. At that time the area still belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, and the surroundings consisted mainly of grassland, market gardens and luxury country estates on the Amstel for wealthy Amsterdammers.

name: Politiebureau Raampoort
en: Politiebureau Raampoort, also known as bureau Raampoort, is a 19th-century former police station on the Singelgracht in Amsterdam, on the corner of the Marnixstraat and the Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat. The building dates from 1888 and was designed by Willem Springer. It was designated a national monument in 2001.

name: Politiebureau Sloten
en: Politiebureau Sloten is a former police station on the Sloterweg, by the Dorpsplein, in the village of Sloten, now part of Amsterdam. It was the smallest police station in the Netherlands and has been a protected municipal monument since 1980. It was built in 1866 by the municipality of Sloten, which remained independent until 1921.

name: Pontsteigergebouw
en: The Pontsteigergebouw, also known as the Pontsteiger or Miljoenengebouw, is a residential tower in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. The building forms part of the Houthavens area development. The complex lies on the IJ, where the ferry to the NDSM site and the Distelweg departs from the pontoon jetty built in 1957 near the Tasmanstraat.

name: Portrettenhuisje
en: The Portrettenhuisje is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Post CS-gebouw
en: The Post CS-gebouw, also known as the Stationspostgebouw, was a building in Amsterdam on the Oosterdokseiland near Centraal Station. It was a surviving part of a demolished complex of buildings that housed a postal sorting centre. The building was about 50 metres high.

name: Prinsengracht 808
en: Prinsengracht 808 is a combined office, residential and shop building on the corner of the Amsterdam Prinsengracht and the Utrechtsestraat. It was built on commission from the Onderlinge Levensverzekeringsmaatschappij “'s-Gravenhage” (the tiled plateau above the entrance refers to it), to a design by A.D.N. and J.G. van Gendt.

name: Prinsenhof (Amsterdam)
en: The Prinsenhof is a building at Oudezijds Voorburgwal 195-199 in Amsterdam. Over time the building has had various functions.

name: Prinses Irenestraat 19
en: Prinses Irenestraat 19 in Amsterdam is a building complex in the Beatrixpark in Amsterdam-Zuid, but with an address on the Prinses Irenestraat. The complex is known as Convict en kapel (Convict and chapel).

name: Prinses Irenestraat 59
en: Prinses Irenestraat 59 in Amsterdam, known for short as PI59, is an office building on the Prinses Irenestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Queens Towers
en: The Queens Towers are three office towers in Amsterdam, dating from 2000 and designed by architect Carel Weeber of De Architekten Cie. The Wilhelminatoren, Julianatoren and Beatrixtoren together form the complex. The office space is mainly rented by the UWV.

name: Raadhuis van Amstelveen
en: The Raadhuis Amstelveen is the town hall of the municipality of Amstelveen in the Dutch province of North Holland. It is located at Laan Nieuwer-Amstel 1, on the Poel near the old village.

name: Raamdwarsstraat 7
en: Raamdwarsstraat 7 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (no. 4755). The four-storey building under a roof stands out because of its height, partly because the neighbouring building at Raamdwarsstraat 9 has only two storeys under a roof.

name: Raamplein 1
en: Raamplein 1 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (518264).

name: Raamstraat 13
en: Prinsengracht 394 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (4772).

name: Raamstraat 2
en: Raamstraat 2 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (47777). The building in Amsterdam-Centrum stands on the corner with the Prinsengracht and forms a unit with Prinsengracht 410.

name: Raamstraat 23
en: Raamstraat 23 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (4774).

name: Raamstraat 6
en: Raamstraat 6 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (4779). It is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Raamstraat 7
en: Raamstraat 7 in Amsterdam is a building with national monument status (4770).

name: Rapenburgerplein 1
en: Rapenburgerplein 1 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Rapenburgerplein and the Foeliedwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Rapenburgerplein 100
en: Rapenburgerplein 100 in Amsterdam is a building on the edge of the Rapenburgerplein, Amsterdam-Centrum. Over the span above the transition between the Nieuwe Herengracht and the Schippersgracht there has always been a lock- or bridge-keeper's cabin. It grew along with the renewals of the Scharrebiersluis. At first there stood a sort of shelter.

name: Rapenburgerplein 6
en: Rapenburgerplein 6 in Amsterdam is a building on the Rapenburgerplein, Amsterdam-Centrum. The Rapenburg island dates from the late 16th century, when three islands were added to the city. After reclamation it was built on, demolished and rebuilt. A gable stone dated anno 1726 marks the last major rebuilding then.

name: Rapenburgerplein 81-83
en: Rapenburgerplein 81-83 is a monumental building in Rapenburg in Amsterdam-Centrum, on the corner of the Rapenburgerplein and the Nieuwe Herengracht on one side and the Rapenburg street on the other.

name: Rechthuis Watergraafsmeer
en: The Rechthuis of Watergraafsmeer stands on the Middenweg, near the Ringdijk in Amsterdam-Oost. The house was built in 1777 to replace the original 17th-century building. Until 1 May 1906 the municipal government of Watergraafsmeer met here, and the building was rented from the Watergraafsmeer water board.

name: Reggestraat 18
en: Reggestraat 18 in Amsterdam is a building on the Reggestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Reguliersbreestraat 1
en: Reguliersbreestraat 1 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the Muntplein, where the Singel meets the Amstel. The Regulierspoort over the Singel, from the 16th century, gave Amsterdammers the opportunity to venture out into the countryside.

name: Reguliersgracht 111-115
en: Reguliersgracht 111-115 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands in the façade wall between the junctions with the Falckstraat and the Weteringschans. The building also has an entrance on the Weteringschans, number 259.

name: Reguliersgracht 120
en: Reguliersgracht 120 in Amsterdam is a building on the Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Reguliersgracht 130
en: Reguliersgracht 130 is a building on the Reguliersgracht, at the corner of the Fokke Simonszstraat, in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Remise Lekstraat
en: The Remise Lekstraat, also known as Remise Kromme Mijdrechtstraat or Remise Amsteldijk, is an Amsterdam tram depot with the address Amsteldijk 153 in the Rivierenbuurt. It was built in 1927–29 by the Dienst der Publieke Werken for the Gemeentetram Amsterdam and is still in use by the GVB tram operation.

name: Renaultgebouw
en: The Renaultgebouw is a monumental building in Amsterdam-Oost, Watergraafsmeer. It has three addresses: Pauwenpad 1-3, Wibautstraat 224 and Prins Bernardplein 173-175. It was built in 1958 and 1959 on the Mr. Treubplein for the car manufacturer Renault (Règie Nationale des Usines Renault Frankrijk).

name: Richard Wagnerstraat 32-34
en: Richard Wagnerstraat 32-34 in the Dutch capital Amsterdam is a church building on the Richard Wagnerstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Rijkskantoorgebouw voor het Geld- en Telefoonbedrijf
en: The Rijkskantoorgebouw voor het Geld- en Telefoonbedrijf in Amsterdam is a historic and architecturally significant building with a rich history.

name: Rijksmonument 335325
en: Rijksmonument 335325 comprises a block of dwellings near the Brink and its side streets in Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. It relates to the addresses and extensions at Veeteeltstraat 127-145. The block was designated a national monument on 20 October 1988, forming part of the larger Brink monument complex (national monument 335305).

name: Rijksmonument 335342
en: Rijksmonument 335342 comprises a gallery running parallel to the south side of the Brink, Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. The covered gallery forms the link between two buildings on the Brink. On one side is the former Verenigingsgebouw, itself national monument 335330, and on the other the former Leeszaal en Bibliotheek, national monument 335336.

name: Rijksmonument 335347
en: Rijksmonument 335347 comprises a building block on the edge of the Brink, Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. It includes the buildings at Brink 1 and 2, Landbouwstraat 51-57, Brinkstraat 82-88 and 151-157, and Veeteeltstraat 106-116. It forms part of the Brink monument complex (national monument 335305).

name: Rijksmonument 335357
en: Rijksmonument 335357 comprises a block of dwellings on the north side of the Brink and side streets in Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. It relates to the addresses Brink 4-22. The block was designated a national monument on 20 October 1988, forming part of the larger Brink monument complex (national monument 335305).

name: Rijksmonument 335363
en: Rijksmonument 335363 is a small block of dwellings with a corner shop on the Landbouwstraat, Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. It relates to Landbouwstraat 72-78. The small block was added to the monuments register on 20 October 1988. The Landbouwstraat is a street that crosses the Brink from north-east to south-west.

name: Rijksmonument 335369
en: Rijksmonument 335369 is a small block of dwellings with a corner shop on the Veeteeltstraat, Betondorp, Amsterdam-Oost. It relates to Veeteeltstraat 118-120. The small block was added to the monuments register on 20 October 1988. The Veeteeltstraat is a street that crosses the Brink from east to west.

name: Rijnstraat 24-30
en: Rijnstraat 24-30 is a strip of buildings on the Rijnstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a municipal monument since 1980 (number 200877). The street wall from Rijnstraat 24 to 58 consists of several municipal monuments, interrupted by the entrance to the IJselstraat.

name: Rijnstraat 36-54
en: Rijnstraat 36-54 is a strip of buildings on the Rijnstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a municipal monument since 1980 (number 200093). The street wall from Rijnstraat 24 to 58 consists of several municipal monuments, interrupted by the entrance to the IJselstraat.

name: Ringdijk 57
en: Ringdijk 57, Amsterdam is a building with an outbuilding on the Ringdijk in Amsterdam-Oost, Watergraafsmeer. Both buildings have been national monuments since 3 November 1970.

name: Robert Scottstraat 28-34
en: Robert Scottstraat 28-34 in Amsterdam is a building on the Robert Scottstraat in Amsterdam-West. The Robert Scottstraat consists mainly of walk-up flats from around 1950. The street had already received its name in 1939, but the Second World War halted construction. This also meant that schools had to be built after the war to educate the children.

name: Robert Scottstraat 7
en: Robert Scottstraat 7 in Amsterdam is a building block on the Robert Scottstraat, Amsterdam-West. It was built as a monastery and presbytery for the adjoining Sint-Josephkerk. The buildings are connected by a corridor.

name: Rokin 111
en: Rokin 111 in Amsterdam is a relatively large office building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was added to the register of national monuments on 11 December 2001. All buildings between Rokin 95 and 199 are either national or municipal monuments.

name: Rokin 115
en: Rokin 115 in Amsterdam is a building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum. Since March 2004 it has been a municipal monument. The Rokin has been part of the old centre of Amsterdam for centuries; it is the continuation of the Amstel. Over the centuries almost everything has disappeared, and old buildings have repeatedly been demolished and new ones erected.

name: Rokin 17
en: Rokin 17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum. As of 16 March 2004 it is a municipal monument.

name: Rokin 65
en: Rokin 65 in Amsterdam is a building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Rokin 72

name: Rokin 9-15
en: Rokin 9-15 is a building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum. On 16 March 2004 the building became a municipal monument (201028).

name: RoXY
en: The RoXY was a nightclub in Amsterdam from 1987 to 1999, which enjoyed international fame for its theatrical and glamorous style.

en: Runstraat 33 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Runstraat and the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Ruysdaelkade 2-4
en: The Ruysdaelkade 2-4 complex, also known as Rioolgemaal F (sewage pumping station F), consists of buildings on the Ruysdaelkade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of four municipal monuments on the quay, not counting the Moppesgebouw. The complex is also known in the cadastre as Stadhouderskade 46. The Polderhuis previously stood on this site.

name: Ruysdaelkade 215
en: Ruysdaelkade 215 is a school building on the Ruysdaelkade, on the bank of the Boerenwetering, in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is a municipal monument.

name: Sacramentskerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Heilig Sacramentskerk is a church building at Kometensingel 152 in Tuindorp Oostzaan in Amsterdam-Noord. It was built in 1952 as a Roman Catholic church. It is an example of a church in the style of the Bossche School, designed by architects Evers and Sarlemijn.

name: Samos (gebouw)
en: Samos is a building with 87 dwellings in Amsterdam-Oost, colloquially called De Tweeling. It is one of the largest buildings in the neighbourhood, on the northern edge of the Amsterdam Science Park. It was designed by 24H Architecten, where at the time Maartje Lammers and Boris Zeisser formed an architects' duo.

name: Sara Burgerhartstraat 1-3
en: Sara Burgerhartstraat 1-3, Amsterdam is a (school) building in Bos en Lommer in Amsterdam-West. In the period after the Second World War, great efforts went into implementing Cornelis van Eesteren's General Extension Plan. Housing estates were built quickly and, after a few years, followed by the necessary schools.

name: Sara Burgerhartstraat 5
en: Sara Burgerhartstraat 5, Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam-West. In the period after the Second World War, housing construction was fully committed to implementing Cor van Eesteren's General Extension Plan. Housing estates were built rapidly and, after a few years, followed by the necessary schools.

name: Sarphatistraat 13
en: The building at Sarphatistraat 13 is a building on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was built to a design by architect J.C. Teunissen on the site previously occupied by the private clinic of gynaecologist Arthur Maurits Mendes de Leon (Sarphatistraat 13-15). That building had all sorts of ornamentation.

name: Sarphatistraat 4
en: The building at Sarphatistraat 4 is a stately mansion on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The house was designed and built on commission from August Hendrichs, a prominent Amsterdammer. The architect was Theo Asseler, nephew of Theo Molkenboer. He designed a building in the neo-Renaissance style, which is partly freestanding.

name: Sarphatistraat 47-55
en: Sarphatistraat 47-55 in Amsterdam is a relatively wide building on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was built in the section between the Amstel with the Hogesluis and the Weesperplein.

name: Sarphatistraat 5
en: The building at Sarphatistraat 5 consisted of a mansion on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designed by Eduard Cuypers, nephew of Pierre Cuypers of the Rijksmuseum. Eduard Cuypers had a building erected in the neo-Venetian Renaissance style. It had both balconies and loggias (internal balconies).

name: Sarphatistraat 66
en: Sarphatistraat 66 is a building on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the section of the street east of the Amstel. That section, built on the former defensive redoubt, was filled in building by building in the 1870s.

name: Sarphatistraat 8
en: The building at Sarphatistraat 8 is a stately building on the Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. Space was created on the site when the famous (dance venue) and notorious (Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels spoke here in 1872) “Lokaal Dalrust”, including its dwellings, was demolished in 1875/1876. In the years that followed, two buildings were erected.

name: Scheldeplein 1-5
en: Scheldeplein 1-5 in Amsterdam is a complex on the Scheldeplein in Amsterdam-Zuid. The building has wings on the Geleenstraat and Geulstraat. Farmland with an agricultural designation lay here for centuries. The ever-expanding development for the growing population of the municipality of Amsterdam put an end to that.

name: Schellingwouderkerk
en: The Schellingwouderkerk is the village church of the dike village of Schellingwoude in Amsterdam-Noord. The church building does not stand along the Schellingwouderdijk, but slightly lower, behind it, on the Wijkergouw.

name: Schiller Hotel
en: The Schiller Hotel (official name NH Schiller) is a four-star hotel on the Rembrandtplein in central Amsterdam. It belongs to the series of grand hotels built during Amsterdam's so-called “Second Golden Age”. The present building opened in 1913 and was designated a national monument in 2001.

name: Schipholtoren
en: Schiphol Airport has two control towers in use: the large control tower at Schiphol-Centrum ('Toren-Centrum') and a smaller tower ('Toren-West') by the Polderbaan. Toren-Centrum is the larger. On its top floor, up to 15 air traffic controllers and assistants can work at the same time.

name: Schottenburch
en: Schottenburch is a warehouse at Kromboomssloot 18-20 in the Nieuwmarkt district of Amsterdam-Centrum. It is known as the “oldest surviving warehouse in Amsterdam”. It is certainly one of the oldest warehouses in the city.

name: Schutterstoren (Amsterdam)
en: The Schutterstoren is a tower block in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It forms part of the new-build project 'Meer en Oever', together with 't Waterfort and Het Bastion. This project was initiated by Projectbureau Vernieuwing Osdorp.

name: Ship Chandlers Warehouse
en: Ship Chandlers Warehouse is the oldest shop in Amsterdam and is located at Geldersekade 8, close to the Schreierstoren. It is the only building in Amsterdam that still has its original 17th-century leaded glass windows on all floors.

name: Sibbelwoningen
en: The Sibbelwoningen, or Sibbelpanden, are located on the Hoogte Kadijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. The forty small buildings have been entered in the register of monuments as separate national monuments since 17 January 1984; however, contrary to what the name suggests, they do not form a monument complex.

name: Silodam
en: The Silodam is a breakwater and street in the western harbour area of Amsterdam. The approximately 300-metre-long breakwater juts out into the IJ. Along the Silodam stand two former grain silos, which now serve as apartment buildings, including the Stenen Silo, a national monument.

name: Singel 250
en: De Singel 250 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum on the corner of the Singel and the Raadhuisstraat. It has been a national monument in Amsterdam since September 2001. Before that Raadhuisstraat was laid out, the Warmoesgracht was filled in around 1895.

name: Sint Elisabeth Gesticht
en: Het Sint Elisabeth Gesticht is the name of a national monument at Mauritskade 25-27 and 's-Gravesandestraat 1-37 in Amsterdam-Oost. The building was designed in July 1886 by master builder Adrianus Bleijs.

name: Sint Jorishof (Amsterdam)
en: The Sint Jorishof (originally the Sint Jorisgasthuis) was Amsterdam's first leper hospital. Lepers were housed in this medieval building. The hof lay on the Kalverstraat, on the corner with the Heiligeweg, between the Olieslagerssteeg and the then Sint Jorissteeg. Originally this location lay just outside the city.

name: Sint Lucas Andreas Ziekenhuis
en: The Sint Lucas Andreas Ziekenhuis is a former Christian hospital in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The hospital arose from a merger between the Sint Lucas Ziekenhuis and the Andreas Ziekenhuis on 1 January 1996. Both of these predecessors have long histories of their own.

name: Sint-Annakerk (Amstelveen)
en: The Sint-Annakerk is a former Roman Catholic church building in the Dutch city of Amstelveen. It lies at the junction of the A9 and the Amsterdamseweg. The building, church and presbytery, was erected from spring 1927 to a design by J.P.L. Hendriks and H.C.M. van Beers. The site at that time still belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Sint-Augustinuskerk (Amsterdam-Buitenveldert)
en: The Sint-Augustinuskerk is a Roman Catholic church on the corner of the Amstelveenseweg and the Kalfjeslaan in Buitenveldert, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Sint-Augustinuskerk (Amsterdam-Noord)
en: The Sint-Augustinuskerk is a former Roman Catholic church on the Nieuwendammerdijk in Nieuwendam, Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Sint-Franciscus van Saleskerk (Lijnden)
en: The Sint-Franciscus van Saleskerk is a former Roman Catholic church building in Lijnden in the Dutch province of North Holland, on the corner of the Schipholweg and the Hoofdweg. It was built in 1859 to a design by Theo Molkenboer as a hall church, and was the first Catholic church in the Haarlemmermeerpolder.

name: Sint-Laurentiuskerk (Weesp)
en: The Sint-Laurentiuskerk is a former Roman Catholic church on the Herengracht 16 in Weesp. The building is a municipal monument and now houses the Wispe Brewery with an associated catering business. The Grote Kerk of Weesp was originally also dedicated to Saint Laurence and Mary Magdalene, but after the Reformation passed to the Protestants.

name: Lauriergracht 15-17
en: Lauriergracht 15-17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The canal and the surrounding buildings date from the early 17th century, when Amsterdam was building its Derde Uitleg. The original buildings were partly demolished in the following centuries and replaced by new construction.

name: Lauriergracht 4-6
en: Lauriergracht 4-6 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The canal and the surrounding buildings date from the early 17th century, when Amsterdam was building its Derde Uitleg. The original buildings were partly lost over the following centuries and replaced by new construction.

name: Lauriergracht 41-45
en: Lauriergracht 41-45 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. It forms part of the complex of the RK Gesticht van de Voorzienigheid, a shelter for destitute girls. The complex extends over much of the southern building line of the canal between the Konijnenstraat and Hazenstraat.

name: Laurierhof
en: The Laurierhof is a hofje (almshouse courtyard) in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam-Centrum. It is one of the largest building blocks in that district. In 1977 the hofje’s street name was taken from the laurel, fitting the sequence Lauriergracht, Laurierstraat, Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat and Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat.

en: Laurierstraat 101 in Amsterdam is a building on the Laurierstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a corner building on the Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat.

name: Laurierstraat 8
en: Laurierstraat 8 in Amsterdam is a building on the Laurierstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. Until the 1940s the building had the house number 18.

name: Leesmuseum (Amsterdam)
en: The Leesmuseum in Amsterdam was a reading society and gentlemen’s club that existed from 17 November 1800 to 1 April 1930. In the second half of the 18th century the first lending libraries and reading societies were founded. By around 1800 there were already about a hundred across the country.

name: Leeuwenburg (Amsterdam)
en: The Leeuwenburg office complex is a building in the Dutch capital Amsterdam. From 1998 to September 2022 part of the Hogeschool van Amsterdam was housed there.

name: Leidsegracht 106
en: Leidsegracht 106 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (no. 3387). The building forms a whole with Raamdwarsstraat 11, which also has a registration number (4757).

name: Leidsegracht 108
en: Leidsegracht 108 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum on the edge of the Jordaan. There has been building here for centuries. Daniël Stalpaert, the city master mason, already drew a building here on his map of 1662. The Leidsegracht, then called De Leydesche Graft, still formed the southern boundary of the city’s built-up area.

name: Leidsegracht 68
en: Leidsegracht 68 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Prinsengracht and the Leidsegracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Leidsegracht 70
en: Leidsegracht 70 and Prinsengracht 424 in Amsterdam form a combined building with the status of national monument (3378).

name: Leliegracht 25
en: Leliegracht 25 in Amsterdam is a national monument in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is locally known as the Potgieterhuis, named after Everhardus Johannes Potgieter, who lived here from 1855 to 1875.

name: Lepelkruisstraat 14-52
en: Lepelkruisstraat 14-52 is a building on the Lepelkruisstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lijnbaan van de Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie
en: The Lijnbaan van de Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie, also called the Oost-Indische Lijnbaan or Compagnieslijnbaan and later known as the Suikerhuis, is a building from 1660 on the Oostenburgergracht in Amsterdam.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 166
en: Lijnbaansgracht 166 is a building on the Lijnbaansgracht in the Jordaan of Amsterdam-Centrum. According to the monuments register the building was constructed in the 18th century, probably at its beginning. It has been listed in that register since 14 July 1970. The reason is that it is a warehouse with a pointed gable.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 18A-C
en: Lijnbaansgracht 18A-C is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. The property lies on the east bank of that Lijnbaansgracht at the height of the Palmgracht. The building was declared a national monument in 1970 for its straight eaves line and its “antique” division into nine small windows.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 246
en: Lijnbaansgracht 246 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the Lijnbaansgracht just south of where the canal emerges from its culvert under the Stadsschouwburg and the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen. The property has the appearance of a 17th-century merchant’s house, but probably dates from the 18th century.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 247
en: Lijnbaansgracht 247 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 254
en: Lijnbaansgracht 254 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. The office/house lies on the Lijnbaansgracht between the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen and the point where the quay meets the Korte Leidsedwarsstraat. It looks onto the rear facade of the Barlaeus Gymnasium at Weteringschans 29/Weteringschans 31.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 255
en: Lijnbaansgracht 255 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. The property lies on the Lijnbaansgracht between the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen and the point where the quay meets the Korte Leidsedwarsstraat. The building looks onto the rear facade of the Barlaeus Gymnasium at Weteringschans 29/Weteringschans 31.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 274
en: Lijnbaansgracht 274 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the Spiegelpleintje, at the junction of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Korte Leidsedwarsstraat. The neighbour to the south is Lijnbaansgracht 275.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 282-283
en: Lijnbaansgracht 282-283 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the stretch of the Lijnbaansgracht between the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen and the Spiegelgracht. In front of the doors is the extension of the Spiegelpleintje.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 287
en: Lijnbaansgracht 287 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 93-94
en: Lijnbaansgracht 93-94 comprises two houses on the Lijnbaansgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. In the 1930s the badly dilapidated properties in the Amsterdam inner city were cleared. The chief inspector of Building and Housing Supervision, Eelke van Houten, saw many historic facades lost.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 99
en: Lijnbaansgracht 99/Bloemgracht 288-298 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the corner of the Lijnbaansgracht quay and the northern quay of the Bloemgracht. Buildings on the Bloemgracht next to it mostly fall within the national monument category.

name: Lijnwerkplaats Amsterdam Zaanstraat
en: De Lijnwerkplaats Amsterdam Zaanstraat is a maintenance workshop of the Nederlandse Spoorwegen for servicing electric passenger rolling stock in Amsterdam-West. The arrival of the electric buffer rolling stock ‘Materieel ’24’ in the late 1920s and early 1930s created a need for more workshop capacity.

name: Linnaeushof 43-44 (Amsterdam)
en: Linnaeushof 43-44, Amsterdam is a building on the Linnaeushof in Amsterdam-Oost. The Linnaeushof lay in an area that belonged to the municipality of Watergraafsmeer until 1921. Houses, the Hofkerk and schools were built around the courtyard. Almost the last building, a convent of the Zusters van het Arme Kind Jezus, was completed in 1931.

name: Linnaeushof 45-46 (Amsterdam)
en: Linnaeushof 45-46, Amsterdam is a site with two school buildings on the Linneaushof in Amsterdam-Oost. The buildings share a common entrance gate on the south side of the courtyard. Above the gate, in a restrained tile panel, the name of the school complex reads: “St-Lidwina Leerschool Anno 1927”.

name: Linnaeushof 47-48 (Amsterdam)
en: Linnaeushof 47-48 in Amsterdam is a building on the Linnaeushof in Amsterdam-Oost. From 23 April 1931 to April 1932 a Catholic school was built here, in a Catholic enclave in the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

name: Linnaeusstraat 2C (Amsterdam)
en: Linnaeusstraat 2C in Amsterdam is a building on the Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Loods 6
en: Loods 6 is a former building of the Koninklijke Nederlandse Stoomboot-Maatschappij (KNSM) on the KNSM-eiland in Amsterdam-Oost. Today it is a multi-tenant building for the creative sector, with some commercial spaces. The Kompaszaal in the building is listed in Amsterdam’s ‘Top-100 lijst van jonge monumenten’.

name: Louis Couperusstraat 133 (Amsterdam)
en: Louis Couperusstraat 133, Amsterdam is a building on the Louis Couperusstraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Louwesweg 1
en: The building Louwesweg 1, better known as the ACTA building, is a high-rise complex on the Louwesweg in Amsterdam Slotervaart. The complex was completed between 1966 and the early 1970s as a dental clinic.

name: Luchtmeetstation Nieuwendammerdijk
en: The Luchtmeetstation Nieuwendammerdijk in Amsterdam is an air-monitoring station on the Nieuwendammerdijk in Amsterdam-Noord. The Nieuwendammerdijk is a centuries-old flood defence that protects the village of Nieuwendam from the water of the IJ. The dike is lined with small dike houses, a number of which are municipal or national monuments.

name: Lucky Luyk
en: The Lucky Luyk, or Lucky Luijk, was the name of a squatted building at Jan Luijkenstraat 3 in the Museumkwartier in Amsterdam. It is a Jugendstil building and national monument, built in 1908–1909 to designs by the architects J.P.F. van Rossem and W.J. Vuyk, known as the architects of the Koninklijk Theater Carré.

name: Lutmastraat 258-266
en: Lutmastraat 258-266 in Amsterdam is a terrace of houses on the Lutmastraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Lutmastraat 263-269
en: Lutmastraat 263-269 is a terrace of houses on the Lutmastraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Maarten Lutherkerk (Weesp)
en: The Maarten Lutherkerk is a building in Weesp in the Dutch province of Noord-Holland, built in 1818 as a church building for the Evangelical-Lutheran Church in Weesp. Since 1657 the Lutheran church in Weesp had a church building, which was replaced in 1818 by the present hall church. The brick building with tall pointed-arched windows has a curved pediment.

name: Maggifabriek (Amsterdam)
en: The Maggifabriek was a factory of Maggi’s Producten Maatschappij NV, based for 60 years at Haarlemmerweg 317–321 and 331–333 on both sides of the Van Slingelandtstraat in Amsterdam-West. Today the original office building from 1921, the factory, warehouse, offices and two upper-floor dwellings are a national monument.

name: Maranathakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Maranathakerk is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Marcanti College
en: The Marcanti College is a secondary school in Amsterdam-West.

name: Maritzstraat 1-47
en: Maritzstraat 1-47 in Amsterdam forms the eastern building line of the Maritzstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. It forms part of five building blocks that originally had a certain unity.

name: Marnixbad
en: The Marnixbad was a swimming pool in Amsterdam-Centrum, located at the junction of the Marnixstraat and the Marnixplein. The original design was probably supplied by architect Jan Leupen.

name: Marnixstraat 150
en: Marnixstraat 150, Amsterdam is a building on the Marnixstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Marnixstraat 234-244
en: Marnixstraat 234-244 is a complex of houses in Amsterdam-Centrum. Here the Marnixstraat forms the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht, and the houses are separated from the water by tram tracks, cycle paths and the carriageway. At the end of the 19th century the vegetable and fruit market (Appeltjesmarkt) was located nearby.

name: Marnixstraat 317
en: Marnixstraat 317 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum, wedged between the Marnixstraat and the Lijnbaansgracht. The building, in 19th-century Dutch Neo-Renaissance style, has its rear facade directly on the water of the Lijnbaansgracht. It has a U-shape (front facade and two side wings).

name: Mauritskade 55 GH
en: Mauritskade 55 GH in Amsterdam is a commercial building on the Mauritskade in Amsterdam-Oost. The Mauritskade, a quay of the Singelgracht, forms the northern boundary of the Oosterpark here. On the quay and more or less within the park stand a number of buildings that are either municipal or national monuments.

name: Mauritskade 57 (Amsterdam)
en: Mauritskade 57, Amsterdam is a building with an address on the Mauritskade in Amsterdam, but it essentially lies against or in the Oosterpark. It was erected on the newly cleared part of the Oosterbegraafplaats, which still had to be cleared of bones and so on.

name: Mauritskade 61
en: Mauritskade 61 is a building from 1908 on the edge of the Oosterpark in Amsterdam-Oost. The property, designed in transitional architecture by Bernard Springer of the Public Works department, was built for scientific institutes of the University of Amsterdam.

name: Maxis Muiden
en: Maxis Muiden is a former hypermarket of the Maxis chain and is now a shopping centre in Muiden, in the municipality of Gooise Meren in the Dutch province of Noord-Holland. The complex lies between the Muidertrekvaart and the Diemerzeedijk, on the border with Diemen.

name: MediArena
en: MediArena is a building from 2010 in Amsterdam-Duivendrecht with offices and television studios. It was designed for the media company Endemol by architect Cees den Ouden of the firm OeverZaaijer.

name: Meetstation Jan van Galenstraat (Amsterdam)
en: The Meetstation Jan van Galenstraat is a measuring station and artwork in Amsterdam-West.

name: Molenpad 10-16
en: Molenpad 10-16 in Amsterdam is a building on the Molenpad in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Molenpad 15-17
en: The building Molenpad 15-17 is a former school building in Amsterdam-Centrum, on the corner of the Prinsengracht and the Molenpad. It was known as Prinsengracht 663 and 665, but after the new building of 1883 it received an entrance door on the Molenpad. The Prinsengracht has no house numbers 663 and 665 in 2017.

name: Molukkenstraat 200
en: Molukkenstraat 200, Amsterdam is a monumental building on the Molukkenstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. It differs architecturally from the other buildings on the street. The street has been lined with houses since the early 20th century, with shops on the east side and some on the west.

name: Museum Het Broekerhuis
en: Museum Het Broekerhuis was a museum from 1882 to 1887 at Amstelveenseweg 122 in Amsterdam, showing the contents of the Broekerhuis in Broek in Waterland, collected by Aaltje Fregeres (1810–1900). Her collection drew many tourists, but because of her age she sold it in 1880 to the N.V.

name: Muziektent (Vondelpark)
en: The Muziektent Vondelpark is a small structure in Amsterdam-Zuid. On 1 November 1996 it was entered in the monuments register as a separately named part of the national monument Vondelpark.

name: Nassaubioscoop
en: The Nassaubioscoop (also known as the Centrum Bioscoop and Thalia Theater) is a former cinema on the Lijnbaansgracht in the Jordaan in Amsterdam. Much has been published about theatres in Amsterdam. In 1996 Richard van Bueren published Saturday night at the movies: het grote Amsterdamse bioscopenboek, 2 delen. Oss, Amsterdam, 1996.

name: Nassaukade 17 (Amsterdam)
en: Nassaukade 17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nassaukade in Amsterdam-West. The property dates from 1881 and was designed by the carpenter, contractor and architect Johannes Engelfriet (Rotterdam, 1851 – there, 1934). He lived there with his family for a few months before moving back to Rotterdam, partly because of a bankruptcy.

name: Nederlands Instituut voor Nijverheid en Techniek
en: The Nederlands Instituut voor Nijverheid en Techniek (or NINT) opened on 21 May 1952 on the Rozengracht in Amsterdam. The NINT’s mission was ‘to increase attention for industry and labour, so that people are helped to choose a study and profession in the industrial sector’.

name: Nederlands Israëlietisch Seminarium
en: The Nederlands Israëlietisch Seminarium (NIS) is an educational institution in Amsterdam for Jewish teachers and rabbis.

name: Nederlands Israëlitisch Meisjesweeshuis
en: The Nederlands Israëlitisch Meisjesweeshuis was an orphanage at Rapenburgerstraat 171 (and later also number 169) in the former Amsterdam Jewish quarter.

name: Neptunus (gebouw)
en: Neptunus is an office building in Amsterdam-Centrum between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Spuistraat. It was erected in 1914–1915 as the office of ‘De Vereeniging van Nederlandsche gezagvoerders en stuurlieden ter koopvaardij’. Neptunus is the god of the sea (or of waves, and so on).

name: Nhow Amsterdam RAI
en: nhow Amsterdam RAI is a hotel beside the RAI complex on the Zuidas in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Nicolaas Witsenkade 38
en: Nicolaas Witsenkade 38 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Nicolaas Witsenkade in Amsterdam, part of the quays of the Singelgracht.

name: Nicolaas Witsenkade 39-45
en: Nicolaas Witsenkade 39 to 45 in Amsterdam-Centrum comprises several buildings on the Nicolaas Witsenkade. The Nicolaas Witsenkade is a quay of the Singelgracht between the Weteringplantsoen and the Westeinde. The complex also includes Huidekoperstraat 32, with its entrance around the corner.

name: Nieuw Engeland (Amsterdam)
en: Nieuw Engeland (also known as the New England Building) is a building on the corner of Koningsplein 2–6 and Singel 468 in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Nieuwe Herengracht 143
en: Nieuwe Herengracht 143 is a former residential home and former squat in Amsterdam. The national monument is a double house with a sandstone facade, opposite the Wertheimpark.

name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht 37
en: Nieuwe Keizersgracht 37 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwe Keizersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument (2768) since 1970.

name: Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1
en: Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1 in Amsterdam is a national monument on the Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum, on the corner of the Marnixstraat. The building, originally a gymnasium, housed the youth theatre De Krakeling from 1978 to 2020. A plaque commemorating the Second World War hangs on the facade.

name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht 64
en: Nieuwe Prinsengracht 64 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwe Prinsengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Nieuwe Spiegelstraat 64
en: Nieuwe Spiegelstraat 64 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat. It has been a national monument since 1970. It dates from the second half of the 17th century, when Amsterdam incorporated more farmland for housing. The monuments register keeps the description brief: “Building with neck gable from the 17th century”.

name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 1
en: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 1 in Amsterdam is a two-part building on the Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The street on Uilenburg is centuries old, as are a few of the buildings.

name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 57-59
en: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 57-59 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on Uilenburg, in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Nieuwendammerdijk 285
en: On the Nieuwendammerdijk 283-285, in the Amsterdam district of Nieuwendam, stands a timber house with a matching neck gable. The property is protected as a national monument and is owned by the Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser.

name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 104-108
en: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 104-108 is a building on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has a rear facade on the Spuistraat, where house numbers 65 to 69 would have been located.

name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 277
en: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 277 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument (number 518474) since 22 April 2002.

name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 282
en: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 282 and 282a in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Nieuwmarkt 25
en: Nieuwmarkt 25 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building with a ground floor at Nieuwmarkt 25 and upper floors at Sint Antoniesbreestraat 1. It has been a national monument since 27 August 1970, described as ‘corner house with a carved sandstone top’. A kind of cartouche under the eaves line bears the date 1724.

name: Nöggerath Theater
en: The Nöggerath Theater was one of Amsterdam’s first cinemas. Since 1986 it has been part of the Tuschinski complex. The cinema opened on 7 September 1907 at Reguliersbreestraat 34 as the Bioscope-Theater, founded by Anton Nöggerath Sr. (1859–1908), director of the Filmfabriek F.A. Nöggerath.

name: Noordzeeweg 4
en: Noordzeeweg 4 in Amsterdam is a building on the Noordzeeweg in Amsterdam-Westpoort. The Noordzeeweg lies in the Westelijk Havengebied, a district not known for its fine architecture. It is a large business area linked to the port of Amsterdam.

name: Odeon (Amsterdam)
en: The Odeon building is a national monument on Singel 460 in Amsterdam-Centrum. During the 17th and 18th centuries the property was a merchant’s house. In the 19th century it took on a cultural function, and today it houses various entertainment venues.

name: Onderstation Westerpark
en: Onderstation Westerpark is a former substation in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. The substation on the Houtmankade 334 was designed around 1915 by the Dienst der Publieke Werken, commissioned by the Gemeente-Electriciteitswerken, a forerunner of the Amsterdam GEB.

name: Onze-Lieve-Vrouw van Zeven Smartenkerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Onze-Lieve-Vrouw van Zeven Smartenkerk is a former Roman Catholic church building on the Aalbersestraat 224 in the Amsterdam district of Geuzenveld. The parish of Onze-Lieve-Vrouw van Zeven Smarten was founded in 1954 for the then new Geuzenveld district. The building pastor was Father M. Nillesen. For the first years two emergency churches were used.

name: Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Geboortekerk (Halfweg)
en: The Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Geboortekerk is a Roman Catholic church on the Doctor Schaepmanstraat 7 in Halfweg. Until 1929 the parish met in a church in the middle of the village centre, which was cut through by the national road Amsterdam–Haarlem.

name: Oost-Indisch Pakhuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Oost-Indisch Pakhuis, originally called the Nieuwe Magazijn and since 1997 Pakhuis Oostenburg, is a former warehouse of the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie on the Oostenburgervoorstraat in Amsterdam.

name: Oranjekerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Oranjekerk is a Protestant church building in Amsterdam, near the Sarphatipark in the De Pijp district, built in 1902–’03. It was consecrated on 11 September 1903. The architect was C.B. Posthumus Meyjes Sr. In the early 1990s there were plans to demolish the church and replace it with new construction.

name: Orato
en: Orato (meaning ‘visible’ or ‘view’) is a building on the H.J.E. Wenckebachweg in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Oudeschans 17A-23B
en: Oudeschans 17A-23B in Amsterdam is a structure on the Oudeschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Oudeschans 3
en: Oudeschans 3 in Amsterdam is a structure on the street and canal Oudeschans in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the opposite side of the canal from the Montelbaanstoren.

name: Oudeschans 35
en: Oudeschans 35 in Amsterdam is a structure on the Oudeschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Oudeschans 39
en: Oudeschans 39 in Amsterdam is a building on the Oudeschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Overtoom 197-205 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 197-205, Amsterdam is a complex of buildings on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West.

name: Overtoom 241 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 241 in Amsterdam, known as Villa Betty, is a national monument in Amsterdam-West (Oud-West). It lies in a garden between the Overtoom and the Vondelpark, closer to the park than to the road. It was built of brick from October 1877 on a natural stone plinth.

name: Overtoom 249-253 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 249-253, Amsterdam is a complex of buildings on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West.

name: Overtoom 33 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 33, Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. In the late 19th century the Amsterdamsche Omnibus Maatschappij was based here, with stables for the horses of the horse tram. When the city gradually switched to the electric tram, the stable space became redundant.

name: Overtoom 373CD (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 373-CD, Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West.

name: Overtoom 39-41 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 39-41, Amsterdam is a complex of buildings on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West.

name: Overtoom 45 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 45, Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. Buildings had stood on this spot for centuries, but they had to be repeatedly demolished and rebuilt. This also happened when the municipality of Amsterdam absorbed land from Nieuwer-Amstel here and built it up.

name: Pakhuis de Zwijger
en: Pakhuis de Zwijger is a former cold-storage warehouse on the Piet Heinkade in the Oostelijk Havengebied in Amsterdam. It is a multi-tenant business building for cultural institutions.

name: Pakhuis Sparreboom
en: Pakhuis Sparreboom is a former warehouse at Keizersgracht 487 in Amsterdam, between the Leidsestraat and the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat. The national-monument property dates from the second half of the 17th century and was one of seven almost identical warehouses on the present numbers 483 to 489.

name: Pakhuis Wilhelmina
en: Pakhuis Wilhelmina is a warehouse in the Oostelijk Havengebied on the Veemkade in Amsterdam. It was built in 1892. In 1988 the building was squatted by a group of artists, which is why it has been preserved.

name: Palmgracht 41-43
en: Palmgracht 41-43 in Amsterdam is a building on the Palmgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. Standing on the corner with the Palmdwarsstraat, it has been a national monument since 27 August 1970. It has not always had this address: in 1940 the site across the Palmdwarsstraat was Palmgracht 45–47.

name: Park Centraal Amsterdam
en: Park Centraal Amsterdam (known until 1930 as café-restaurant Parkzicht, and from 1930 to 2019 as Park Hotel Amsterdam) is a hotel on the Stadhouderskade in the Dutch capital Amsterdam, on the corner of the Hobbemastraat, in the Museumkwartier. The hotel’s history goes back to the 19th century.

name: Parkrandgebouw
en: Parkrandgebouw is a block of flats in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The building stands in Geuzenveld on the Dr. H. Colijnstraat. Around 1956 several residential blocks stood here. These had been vacated by the early 21st century, along with serious concrete decay and mould caused by poor ventilation.

name: Parnassusweg 220
en: Parnassusweg 220 is a building on the Parnassusweg in Amsterdam-Zuid (neighbourhood Zuidas-Noord). The building also adjoins the Fred. Roeskestraat and the Ringweg Amsterdam (Ringweg-Zuid). On the nomination of Heemschut, the complex has been designated a municipal monument.

name: Passeerdersgracht 3
en: Passeerdersgracht 3 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (4080).

name: Paviljoen Binnengasthuisterrein
en: The Paviljoen Binnengasthuisterrein is a structure in Amsterdam-Centrum. The architect of the building, Theo Bosch, never saw the result of his design; he died before its completion.

name: Pentagon (bouwwerk Amsterdam)
en: The Pentagon is a housing complex in the Nieuwmarkt district in central Amsterdam. It is the only building on the square of the same name. It was designed by architect Theo Bosch with help from Aldo van Eyck and is regarded as a model project in Dutch urban renewal.

name: Persilhuis
en: The Persilhuis, Persilschool or Persilgebouw was a building that stood at Stadhouderskade 19–20 in Amsterdam-West. Its basis dates from 1884, when a block of shops and dwellings rose here next to the Koepelkerk. A shop floor, three residential floors and an attic were built.

name: Pieter de Hoochstraat 78
en: Pieter de Hoochstraat 78 in Amsterdam is a school building on the Pieter de Hoochstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. This was agricultural land on the southern edge of Amsterdam for centuries; in the 19th century it was mainly administered by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Pieter de Hoochstraat 80
en: Pieter de Hoochstraat 80 in Amsterdam is a former school building on the Pieter de Hoochstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Piraeus (gebouw)
en: Piraeus, initially KNSM Blok 1 and later also called Kollhoff or Kollhoffgebouw, is an apartment building on the KNSM-eiland in Amsterdam-Oost. The building is named after the Greek port city of Piraeus, which the KNSM served with a liner service.

name: Salt (gebouw)
en: Salt is a residential complex on the Haarlemmerweg in Amsterdam Oud-West. Redevelopment of an office park into a residential neighbourhood began here in the 2010s. Four residential towers were built on the narrow strip between the Haarlemmerweg (on one side) and allotment gardens and the Westerpark (on the other).

name: Sarphatipark 1-3
en: The building Sarphatipark 1-3, on the corner of Eerste van der Helststraat 65-67, stands on the corner of Sarphatipark (as a street) and Eerste van der Helststraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Sarphatipark 19-21
en: The buildings Sarphatipark 19-21 consist of two mansions on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses bear a strong resemblance to the neighbouring buildings at Sarphatipark 9-17. The two houses were built in the Eclectic style. The buildings are almost mirror images of each other.

name: Sarphatipark 23-33
en: The buildings Sarphatipark 23-33 consist of six mansions on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses bear a strong resemblance to the neighbouring buildings at Sarphatipark 19-21. The six houses were built in the Eclectic style. The buildings are sometimes mirror images of each other.

name: Sarphatipark 35-37
en: The building Sarphatipark 35-37 is a double mansion on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were built in the Eclectic style and are mirror images of each other. Notably, the balconies of the two buildings differ from each other.

name: Sarphatipark 39-41
en: The building Sarphatipark 39-41 is a double mansion on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were built in the Eclectic style and are mirror images of each other. G. Heuvelink was an estate agent in Amsterdam and lived a little further along the street, by the park.

name: Sarphatipark 43-45
en: The building Sarphatipark 43-45 is a double mansion on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were built in the Eclectic style and are mirror images of each other. That mirror effect has been partly lost, as the facade was renovated over the years.

name: Sarphatipark 47-51
en: The building Sarphatipark 47-51 consists of three mansions on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were built in the Eclectic style. Numbers 49 and 51 mirror number 47. The symmetrical principle was abandoned for the balconies.

name: Sarphatipark 5-7
en: The building Sarphatipark 5-7 stands on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. However, the construction drawing gives a different address. It indicates that the buildings were to stand on Jan Steenstraat between Van der Helstraat and Swelinckstraat.

name: Sarphatipark 53
en: The building Sarphatipark 53 consists of a single mansion on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The house was built in the Eclectic style. In that respect it continues the facade line of this luxurious stretch of De Pijp.

name: Sarphatipark 55-57
en: The building Sarphatipark 55-57 consists of a double mansion on the north side of Sarphatipark in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were designed by the architect Pieter Jacobus de Kam, who himself moved into number 55.

name: Sarphatipark 59-61
en: The building Sarphatipark 59-61 consists of a double mansion on the north side of Sarphatipark in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses were designed by M.H.G. ten Cate, who called himself an architect, and were built at his expense according to the construction drawing. They are in an Eclectic style and generously proportioned.

name: Sarphatipark 63
en: The building Sarphatipark 63 is a mansion on the north side of Sarphatipark in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by the architects Pieter Jacobus de Kam and Leendert Hartog. Little work by either survives in Amsterdam. De Kam returned to his birthplace in Zeeland, and Hartog moved to Nijmegen.

name: Sarphatipark 65
en: The building Sarphatipark 65 consists of a mansion on Sarphatipark (both street and park) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by the architect W.J. Nijman and built in the Eclectic style, a style widely used locally.

name: Sarphatipark 67
en: The building Sarphatipark 67 consists of a mansion on Sarphatipark (both street and park) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by the architect Jacob Arnold van der Sluijs Veer. His original design was for five mansions on Sarphatipark, but only part of it was carried out.

name: Sarphatipark 75-77
en: The building Sarphatipark 75-77 consists of a double mansion on Sarphatipark (both street and park) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by the architect Jacob van den Ban, who had the buildings erected in the Neo-Renaissance style.

name: Sarphatipark 85-89
en: The building Sarphatipark 85-89 consists of three mansions on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Sarphatipark 9-17
en: The buildings Sarphatipark 9-17 are five identical buildings on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. They are five mansions, some with an office in the house, to the same design (sometimes mirrored) in the Eclectic style.

name: Sarphatipark 91-97
en: The building Sarphatipark 91-97 consists of four mansions with commercial premises on Sarphatipark (both park and street) in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The house numbered 97 stands on the corner of that street with Eerste Sweelinckstraat. The houses were designed by J.A. Stokvis, who was also responsible for Sarphatipark 5-7.

name: Sarphatistraat 102-104
en: The buildings Sarphatistraat 102-104 housed the Emma Kinderziekenhuis, together with an adjoining director's residence on Sarphatistraat in Amsterdam-Centrum, until 1988. In 2016 the Spinoza Hotel opened its doors here.

name: Scala (Amsterdam)
en: Scala, formerly known as TapasTheater, is a theatre in Amsterdam-West located at Van Hallstraat 286, in the Staatsliedenbuurt. The theatre has four small auditoria in the basement and a food bar on the ground floor.

name: Schiller (café)
en: Schiller is a café on the Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam. It opened shortly after 1920 as the hotel bar of the neighbouring Schiller hotel.

name: Schipholgebouw
en: The Schipholgebouw, abbreviated SHG and also called Schiphol Hoofdgebouw, is an office building in Schiphol-Centrum, built mainly for the offices of the airport operator Schiphol Group (also known as NV Luchthaven Schiphol). The building lies near the Schiphol exit of the Rijksweg A4 (Amsterdam-Den Haag).

name: Singel 46-48
en: Singel 46-48 in Amsterdam is a building on the Singel in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Singelhoven
en: Singelhoven is a double mansion at Stadhouderskade 69-70 in Amsterdam-Zuid. The building was designed by IJme Gerardus Bijvoets in the Eclectic style. It is built symmetrically, with a white central section containing two entrance gates, flanked by darkly painted facade sections on the left and right.

name: Sinne
en: Sinne is a restaurant in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. It has held a Michelin star since 2015. GaultMillau awarded the restaurant 14 out of 20 points in 2016. The owners of Sinne are Suzanne Sluijter and Alexander Ioannou, sommelier and head chef respectively.

name: Sint Willibrordusstraat 1-13
en: Sint Willibrordusstraat 1-13 in Amsterdam is a row of buildings on Sint Willibrordusstraat in the Willibrordusbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. The row comprises two municipal monuments (nos. 222070 and 222071).

name: Sint-Bonifatiuskerk (Zaandam)
en: The Sint-Bonifatiuskerk in Zaandam is a Neo-Gothic Roman Catholic church in Zaandam, built between 1899 and 1900. It is distinguished by a squat square tower and an exceptionally intact, colourful Neo-Gothic interior. The church forms part of a larger complex that also includes a presbytery.

name: Sint-Jozefkerk (Zaandam)
en: The Sint-Jozefkerk in Zaandam is a Roman Catholic church in the Kogerveld district of Zaandam, in the Dutch municipality of Zaanstad. The church stands beside Zaandam Kogerveld station. It is used by the Sint-Jozef parish in Zaandam.

name: Sint-Urbanuskerk (Nes aan de Amstel)
en: The Sint-Urbanuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in Nes aan de Amstel. It is a Neo-Gothic cruciform basilica with a square tower at the crossing. It was the first independent design by the architect Joseph Cuypers, son of Pierre Cuypers, who was also responsible for many churches in the Amstelland.

name: Spaarndammerhart
en: The Spaarndammerhart (also known as De Verbinding) is a two-part apartment complex on the Krommeniestraat in the Spaarndammerbuurt of Amsterdam-West (Oud-West). The Krommeniestraat changed its appearance twice dramatically during its existence. In the 1970s the street was largely demolished and replaced by a school building.

name: Spijker (bar)
en: De Spijker, or Spijkerbar, is a gay bar at Kerkstraat 4 in the centre of Amsterdam. Initially it catered to leather men, but since the 2010s it has attracted a mixed LGBT clientele. Over the years the venue has also had a darkroom, a restaurant and a small theatre.

name: Staalhof (Amsterdam)
en: The Staalhof was a 17th-century complex of buildings on the corner of the Staalstraat and the Groenburgwal in Amsterdam. It is best known for Rembrandt's painting De Staalmeesters, which hung here until 1771. The Staalhof was the centre of the cloth industry, the textile industry that dominated the area around the building.

name: Stadhouderskade 1
en: Stadhouderskade 1 is a symmetrically designed office building between the Stadhouderskade and the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-West. Built in 1922-1923 on the commission of the Public Works Department (PW), it was the head office of the Gemeentetram.

name: Stadhouderskade 115
en: Stadhouderskade 115 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is built in the shape of a 'taartpunt' (wedge-shaped point), as the form is known locally. The corner where Stadhouderskade, Gerard Doustraat and Nicolaas Berghemstraat meet is not a right angle but an obtuse one.

name: Stadhouderskade 116-122
en: Stadhouderskade 116-122 is a complex on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp.

name: Stadhouderskade 123-124
en: Stadhouderskade 123-124 originally comprised two mansions on the Stadhouderskade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid, on the corner with Van Woustraat. Photographer Jacob Olie recorded the situation in 1891. The buildings then stood apart from the development on Van Woustraat.

name: Stadhouderskade 125-127
en: According to the construction drawing of 1882, Stadhouderskade 125-127 originally comprised three mansions on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Stadhouderskade 128
en: Stadhouderskade 128 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The mansion was built to a design by Nicolaas Vos, an estate agent by background but also an architect. He designed the building for Mr K. van den Eijnden, a hospitality entrepreneur, who also had Stadhouderskade 129 built.

name: Stadhouderskade 129
en: Stadhouderskade 129 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by Nicolaas Vos, an estate agent by background but also an architect. He designed the building for Mr K.

name: Stadhouderskade 130-134
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 130-134 is a residential block of five mansions on the Stadhouderskade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of the few examples of terraced houses (wel met kasten van huizen) on the Stadhouderskade. These terraced houses are large. Built in the Eclectic style, they contain all kinds of stylistic features.

name: Stadhouderskade 135-136
en: Stadhouderskade 135-136 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by estate agent, carpenter, builder and architect Fredrik Hendrik Koekkoek. The style is sober Eclectic, with hardly any decoration, the exceptions being the garlands at the cornice.

name: Stadhouderskade 137-139
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 137-139 consists of three equivalent buildings on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The three buildings were designed by Jan Willem Hartgerink and Hendrik Dirks Kramer, who almost single-handedly built up this stretch of the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadhouderskade 145-146
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 145-146/Hemonystraat 1 consists of three buildings on the corner of the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht and Hemonystraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The architect or architects of this complex of three houses are as yet unknown. They are built in the Eclectic style, which was widely used on the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadhouderskade 155
en: The building Stadhouderskade 155 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The former mansion was built to a design by Jan Willem Hartgerink and Hendrik Dirks Kramer, who built up almost this entire stretch of the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadhouderskade 157
en: The building Stadhouderskade 157 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The former mansion was built to a design by Christiaan Posthumus Meyjes senior. The style is Eclectic, although features from the Louis XVI style can also be found.

name: Stadhouderskade 160
en: The building Stadhouderskade 160 is the last building on the Stadhouderskade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It stands on the corner with the Amsteldijk, but is accessible only through the entrance on the Stadhouderskade. Evidently an entrance on the Amsteldijk had been considered, as its numbering there only begins with number 6 as of 2015.

name: Stadhouderskade 29
en: The buildings Stadhouderskade 29 and 29a are located on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. In the 19th century the Rinckers iron foundry stood here, whose buildings were rather rickety. Moreover, residents of this new part of Amsterdam complained about the smell from the company, which caused nuisance as far as the Vondelpark.

name: Stadhouderskade 3
en: Stadhouderskade 2-3 and Overtoom 1 is a building on the corner of the Stadhouderskade and Overtoom in Amsterdam. It is known as the 'Auroragebouw', named after the life insurance company Aurora, which was based here (then still house number 1A). The money insurer B. Franco Mendes was also briefly based in the old building.

name: Stadhouderskade 30
en: The building Stadhouderskade 30 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was probably built to a design by Willem Langhout, who built and designed several other buildings in the neighbourhood. The house has four storeys and an attic floor.

name: Stadhouderskade 40-41
en: The building Stadhouderskade 40-41 consists of a grand villa designed by the architect Jean Servais, on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht, P.C. Hooftstraat and Jan Luijkenstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, Museumkwartier.

name: Stadhouderskade 47-49
en: The building Stadhouderskade 47-49/Ruysdaelkade 3-5 is a block of houses on the corner of the Stadhouderskade and the Ruysdaelkade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The richly decorated building with balconies consists of several mansions side by side. On that corner it is built in a symmetrical form.

name: Stadhouderskade 52-53
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 52-53 consists of two mansions on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in the Museumkwartier, Amsterdam-Zuid. The two houses, identical in their front elevations, were probably built to a design by Nicolaas van der Linden.

name: Stadhouderskade 54
