en: The building Stadhouderskade 54 is a mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in the Museumkwartier, Amsterdam-Zuid. The four-storey house with an attic was probably built to a design by Nicolaas van der Linden.

name: Stadhouderskade 56-57
en: The building Stadhouderskade 56-57 consists of two mansions on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in the Museumkwartier, Amsterdam-Zuid. The houses, of four storeys and an attic, were probably built to a single design by Nicolaas van der Linden.

name: Stadhouderskade 58-59
en: The building Stadhouderskade 58-59 consists of two mansions on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in the Museumkwartier, Amsterdam-Zuid. Nicolaas van der Linden had bought a number of plots on the Stadhouderskade, probably as an estate agent.

name: Stadhouderskade 60-60a
en: The building Stadhouderskade 60-60a is a monumental building from 1880 on the Stadhouderskade in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid, and a municipal monument. The house at number 60, in an Eclectic style with Neo-Romanesque and Neo-Renaissance elements and a stepped gable, was originally the clubhouse of the Amsterdam Sint-Vincentiusvereniging.

name: Stadhouderskade 62-63
en: The building Stadhouderskade 62-63/Frans Halsstraat 1-3 originally consisted, on paper, of five houses on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht corner of Frans Halsstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. IJme Gerardus Bijvoets designed five houses here in symmetrical form for the Kloppers brothers.

name: Stadhouderskade 64
en: The building Stadhouderskade 64 is a mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by the architect IJme Gerardus Bijvoets, who designed several other buildings on the spot. Notably, the building is almost entirely rendered.

name: Stadhouderskade 65-66
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 65-66 is a double mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by the architect IJme Gerardus Bijvoets, who designed several other buildings in the area. In his design he made use of the Eclectic style.

name: Stadhouderskade 68
en: The building Stadhouderskade 68 is a former mansion on the Stadhouderskade in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by IJme Gerardus Bijvoets in the Eclectic style. The building is symmetrical, with a white central section flanked by darkly painted facade sections on the left and right.

name: Stadhouderskade 71
en: The building Stadhouderskade 71 is a former mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed by IJme Gerardus Bijvoets in the Eclectic style. The building forms part of a complex of four buildings, which together are built symmetrically.

name: Stadhouderskade 74
en: The building Stadhouderskade 74 was a mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. The mansion originally served only as a residence and was designated Stadhouderskade 51N. The construction drawing is dated 22 August 1878 and bears the signature of the owner and estate agent P. J.

name: Stadhouderskade 77
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 77 on the corner of Ferdinand Bolstraat 2-6 comprises four buildings on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht, at the corner of Ferdinand Bolstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. Its location on Ferdinand Bolstraat places it opposite the former Heineken Brewery.

name: Stadhouderskade 80
en: The complex Quartier Latin consists of an office and houses on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is located on the corner of Stadhouderskade 80 and Eerste van der Helststraat number 1-a. The name alluded to the nickname De Pijp received, after the Quartier Latin in Paris.

name: Stadhouderskade 82-83
en: The building Stadhouderskade 82-83 consists of two houses on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. The two houses were built around 1882 to a design by Frederik Lodewijk Janssen senior. He had married in 1881 and started his family here.

name: Stadhouderskade 84
en: Stadhouderskade 84 is a plot on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp.

name: Stadhouderskade 85
en: Stadhouderskade 85 is a plot on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp.

name: Stadhouderskade 87-88
en: Stadhouderskade 87-88 is a double house on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The dwellings are apparently mirror images of each other, but they differ in detail.

name: Stadhouderskade 89-90
en: Stadhouderskade 89-90 is a double house with shop on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The buildings are apparently mirror images of each other, but differ in detail.

name: Stadhouderskade 91
en: Stadhouderskade 91 is a house with shop on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The building was built detached from its neighbours, in an Eclectic style, of which there are thirteen to the dozen on the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadhouderskade 92
en: Stadhouderskade 92 is a house with shop on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The original layout of Stadhouderskade 92 was a basement, beletage, upper floor and attic. The layout has since been adapted to its use. The building is a striking presence on the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadhouderskade 93-94
en: The complex Stadhouderskade 93-94 is a house with shop on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp.

name: Stadhouderskade 97
en: Stadhouderskade 97 is a dwelling on the Stadhouderskade, the southern bank of the Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. It is a fairly straightforward house built in the Eclectic style, a style that is relatively common on the Stadhouderskade.

name: Stadshartkerk
en: Stadshartkerk Amstelveen is the name of a Christian church in Amstelveen. The church has existed since November 2004 and is a replanting and continuation of the local Gereformeerde Kerk vrijgemaakt (GKV), which was dissolved in October of that year. Under the leadership of Tim Vreugdenhil, the Stadshartkerk was then developed.

name: Station Aalsmeer
en: Station Aalsmeer is a former terminus station on the Haarlemmermeer railway lines: Aalsmeer - Amsterdam Willemspark, Aalsmeer - Haarlem and Aalsmeer - Nieuwersluis-Loenen, built by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij (HESM). The station building, designed by J.G.

name: Station Amsterdam Museumplein
en: Station Amsterdam Museumplein was a planned railway station, intended as the Amsterdam (provisional) terminus of the Schiphol line.

name: Station Hoofddorp (Haarlemmermeerspoorlijnen)
en: The first Station Hoofddorp was a railway station in Hoofddorp in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer in the Dutch province of North Holland.

name: Stompe Toren (Spaarnwoude)
en: The Stompe Toren in the North Holland village of Spaarnwoude is a church tower of medieval origin, next to a small church dating from the 18th century. It is the oldest monument in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer. The chapel (c. 1063) and church (from c. 1225) on this site were dedicated to Saint Gertrude.

name: Summertime (Amsterdam)
en: Summertime is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuid. The complex consists of two building volumes which together take the form of an hourglass. The northern part stands between Gustav Mahlerlaan (house numbers 637-841) and George Gershwinlaan. The southern part stands between George Gershwinlaan (house numbers 351-537) and De Boelegracht.

name: Swaenenburgh
en: Swaenenburgh is an estate in 's-Graveland in the Dutch province of North Holland.

name: Technisch College Amsterdam
en: The Technisch College Amsterdam, abbreviated TeC Amsterdam, is a Dutch school of secondary vocational education with a Christian character. The school is housed in a three-storey building on the Vlaardingenlaan in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, located between the head office of the DWI and Henk Sneevlietweg metro station.

name: Teleport Tower
en: The Teleport Tower is an office building in Amsterdam. It stands right alongside the A10 and the N200. Construction of the Teleport Tower was completed in 2000, with a height of 65 metres and 17 storeys. Many small tenants are based in the building as sub-tenants of Regus. From the tower there is a view over Amsterdam and its surroundings.

name: Terrace Tower
en: Terrace Tower is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: The Duchess (restaurant)
en: The Duchess is a restaurant on the Spuistraat in Amsterdam, which held a Michelin star from 2018 to 2024 inclusive.

name: The Empire
en: The Empire was one of the oldest well-known gay cafés in Amsterdam. The establishment was located at Nes 17 and was first mentioned in 1911. The café was later known, among other names, as Maxim and Bob's-Bar Bodega, and continued to attract a homosexual clientele until the late 1930s.

name: The Lady (gebouw)
en: The Lady (De dame) is a building from 2024 on the P.C. Hooftstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. The P.C. Hooftstraat was built up at the end of the 19th century with houses in the style of the day. After a century, a number of these were found no longer able to meet the needs of new users.

name: The Sharing Tower
en: The Sharing Tower, formerly De Oliphant, is an office building in Amsterdam. It is a distinctive Y-shaped building with a transparent facade and a recognisable vertical geometry. The building is 65 metres high and has 17 storeys. It offers 16,000 m² of lettable floor space, with the possibility of extending to more than 20,000 m².

name: The Upside Down Amsterdam
en: The Upside Down Amsterdam is an Instagram museum where visitors can pose against a variety of backdrops for playful photos for social media. It is the third Instagram museum in Amsterdam after WONDR and Youseum. It distinguishes itself by incorporating social engagement into its programme.

name: Theater Amsterdam
en: Theater Amsterdam is a theatre in Amsterdam. For now it is the only theatre in Amsterdam designed for productions that run for as long as audiences remain interested. On 8 May 2014 the theatre opened with the production Anne, after Anne Frank's diary.

name: Theater De Omval
en: Theater De Omval is a theatre, cinema, library, music school and hospitality venue in the municipality of Diemen. The theatre opened its doors in 1996.

name: Torpedo Theater
en: The Torpedo Theater is a theatre in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat 87-89
en: The complex Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat 87-89 is a building of forty dwellings on the Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The official numbering is Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat 87-95. The dwellings were built by the Vereeniging Salerno to a design of January 1872 by Jan Leliman in the Eclectic style.

name: Tweede Jan Steenstraat 112-114
en: The building Tweede Jan Steenstraat 112-114 consists of two houses on the Tweede Jan Steenstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat 94-96
en: The building Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat 94-96 stands on the Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is the second-to-last building on the street before it crosses the Amsteldijk. It stands at an angle to Amsteldijk 25, which is also a monument.

name: Tweede van Swindenstraat 7-13
en: Tweede van Swindenstraat 7-13 in Amsterdam is a building on the Tweede van Swindenstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. The street was built up at the end of the 19th century, in the era of so-called revolution building. In the 1970s and 1980s part of that development fell victim to urban renewal.

name: Twiskemolen
en: The Twiskemolen is an octagonal, reed-thatched ground-sail windmill between Landsmeer and Oostzaan, where the boundary between the two villages runs through the middle of the mill, in the Het Twiske recreation area. It has a sail span of 24.00 metres. The mill was erected here in 1974, after first standing in Barsingerhorn to drain the Hooglandspolder.

name: UNStudio Tower
en: UNStudio Tower is a building on the Zuidas in Amsterdam, on the corner of Gustav Mahlerlaan and Parnassusweg. The building has 21 storeys and a height of 85 metres. It is the last building in the Mahler4 block and, like the others, is named after its designers, here UNStudio. The building is also known as the RBS Tower.

name: Utrechtsedwarsstraat 4
en: Utrechtsedwarsstraat 4 in Amsterdam is a building on the Utrechtsedwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Utrechtsedwarsstraat 6-8
en: Utrechtsedwarsstraat 6-8 is a building on the Utrechtsedwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The upper dwellings received house number 6; number 8 is the storage space.

name: Van Baerlestraat 27
en: Van Baerlestraat 27 is a building on the Van Baerlestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, on the edge of the Museumkwartier. Between 1901 and 1977 the building housed the head office of the Rijkspostspaarbank. From 1985 the Sweelinck Conservatorium settled in the building, where it remained until 2008.

name: Vanderveen
en: Vanderveen was a restaurant in Amsterdam that opened in November 2018. When the Michelin stars for 2023 were awarded, it received one star.

name: Vereniging Nederlandse Verkeersvliegers
en: The Vereniging Nederlandse Verkeersvliegers, or VNV, is the trade union and professional association for Dutch pilots who are or were active in civil aviation. It currently represents the pilots of KLM, Transavia, Martinair, TUI fly, easyJet and CHC HN. Its membership rate is high.

name: Vinkenstraat 39
en: The building Vinkenstraat 39, also known as Vinkenstraat 39-41, is a building on the Vinkenstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. In 1872 the 'Vereeniging tot verbetering der kleine kinderbewaarplaatsen' (a day nursery) opened a first branch here. Care for children could be provided from 7 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.

name: Weesperzijde 79D
en: Weesperzijde 79D in Amsterdam is a building on the Weesperzijde in Amsterdam-Oost. Development along the Weesperzijde was largely built house by house during periods of urban expansion, and those periods can still be seen in the architecture used.

name: West-End (Amsterdam)
en: The West-End, later the Ambassade, was a cinema in the Amsterdam district of De Baarsjes. The cinema opened in 1933 on the Jan Evertsenstraat near the Krommert, at what was then the far western edge of the city. It is not known whether the name West-End refers to the London nightlife district of the same name. The cinema was initiated by REMA N.V.

name: Westerkade 1-9
en: Westerkade 1-9/Marnixstraat 215-231 is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Centrum. The complex is wedged between the Westerkade (to the east, here the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht) and the Marnixstraat (to the west).

name: Westzijderkerk (Zaandam)
en: The Westzijderkerk in Zaandam stands on the Westzijde, one of the two streets along the Zaan. It is a cruciform church built between 1638 and 1640 and enlarged between 1671 and 1680. In 1647 a farmer and his pregnant wife were buried in the church; both had been killed by a mad bull.

name: Weteringkerk
en: The Weteringkerk is a church building on the Veluwelaan in Amsterdam-Zuid. The building, at the time announced as the Nieuwe Weteringkerk, was built in 1968/69.

name: Weteringschans 77
en: Weteringschans 77 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the east side of the Weteringschans in Amsterdam. Its rear facade faces the Zieseniskade, the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht here. When built in 1881 it formed an architectural whole with Weteringschans 79.

name: Willemsparkweg 15
en: Willemsparkweg 15, Amsterdam is a building on the Willemsparkweg in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is joined to Willemsparkweg 13, and the two were built around 1886 to a design by the architect Hendrik Jan Wigman. Wigman was active in the neighbourhood; his work can also be found at Willemsparkweg 29-35 (Huis Galesloot), which is a municipal monument.

name: Windroosplein 73
en: Windroosplein 73 in Amsterdam is a building on the Windroosplein, Wittenburg, in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Wittenburg peninsula, which is reachable only via the quay of the Wittenburgergracht, is centuries old.

name: Windroosplein 75-77
en: Windroosplein 75-77 in Amsterdam is a building on the Windroosplein, Wittenburg, Amsterdam. The Wittenburg peninsula, which is reachable only via the quay of the Wittenburgergracht, is centuries old.

name: Wingerdweg 110
en: Wingerdweg 110 is a building on the Wingerdweg in Amsterdam-Noord. The small building on the edge of the Noorderpark was erected there as an office and park-keeper's cottage for the Plantings Department of the Public Works. It probably dates from the time the Florapark was laid out, around 1920.

name: Wingerdweg 28-34
en: Wingerdweg 28-34 is a complex on the Wingerdweg in Amsterdam-Noord. It is a former school building, built on commission from the Public Works Department. The architect of the whole was Nicolaas Lansdorp, working under Wichert Arend de Graaf. In 1926 two schools were housed in the building: the Resedaschool (32-34) and the Wingerdschool (28-30).

name: Wingerdweg 52
en: Wingerdweg 52 is a building on the Wingerdweg in Amsterdam-Noord. It lies on the edge of the Florapark and Noorderpark. With the urban expansion of Amsterdam-Noord the question arose whether a hospital would be necessary. A councillor therefore asked whether such an institution would prove viable to operate.

name: Winkelcentrum Diemerplein
en: Winkelcentrum Diemerplein is a shopping centre in the centre of Diemen in the Dutch province of North Holland. The shopping centre, located on the square of the same name, was built in the 1960s. Besides shops, it also contains housing.

name: Wooncoöperatie De Warren
en: Wooncoöperatie De Warren is the first self-build housing cooperative realised in Amsterdam. In April 2018 it won the tender for the pilot housing cooperative, issued by the Municipality of Amsterdam. The building was completed in early 2023 on Centrumeiland, a new part of IJburg.

name: Y-Towers
en: Y-Towers is a building complex under construction in the Overhoeks district of Amsterdam. The complex consists of a base with hotel and congress facilities of the Maritim chain and two towers: a hotel tower 114 metres high and the residential tower Yvie, 106 metres high. Construction began in 2017 and was due to be completed in 2023.

name: Zaanstad (gebouw)
en: Zaanstad (officially West-Kantoor) is a building in Amsterdam-West. It was designed by Willem Dudok, who was already retired at the time, and Robert Magnée. It is one of the tallest buildings in the area. The building was erected at the initiative of a property developer who wanted to place an office building on a site that was easy to reach.

name: Zoutkeetsgracht 2-110
en: Zoutkeetsgracht 2-110 is a complex of dwellings dating from 1975/1976, on the Zoutkeetsgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The northern facade of that canal is almost entirely 20th-century development built on three old warehouses, which are, after all, national monuments.

name: Zoutkeetsplein 1-7
en: Zoutkeetsplein 1-7, Barentzstraat 317-335, Zoutkeetsgracht 346-370 is a building complex in Amsterdam-West. It is a composite building with its front on the Zoutkeetsplein. The square came into being as early as the 17th century, but only received its name in 1913.

name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is a Dutch Old Catholic church building on Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam. The church, presbytery and lecture room form a single ensemble and were designed by Johan W.F. Hartkamp jr., a pupil of Hendrik Petrus Berlage.

name: Sint-Ritakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Roman Catholic Sint-Ritakerk on Hagedoornplein 2 in Amsterdam-Noord was built in 1921–22 to a design by A.J. Kropholler. It is a broad basilica-type church with an apse and tower, in a traditionalist design with rationalist details.

name: Sint-Rosaklooster
en: The Sint-Rosaklooster was a Roman Catholic sisters’ house at Wingerdweg 4 in Amsterdam-Noord. It was built in 1926–27 to a design by A.J. Kropholler in a traditionalist style. The building comprises a sisters’ house with a chapel and is linked to the cloister courtyard.

name: Sint-Urbanuskerk (Bovenkerk)
en: The Sint-Urbanuskerk is a Roman Catholic church on Noorddammerlaan in Bovenkerk, in the municipality of Amstelveen in North Holland. On Saturday evening, 15 September 2018, the church was severely damaged by a fierce blaze. The tower survived. Reconstruction and alteration of the church building were soon decided upon.

name: Sint-Urbanuskerk (Ouderkerk aan de Amstel)
en: The Sint-Urbanuskerk is a Roman Catholic church of 1867 in Ouderkerk aan de Amstel in the Dutch province of North Holland. The church stands on the south-western side of Ouderkerk, by the Kerkbrug over the small river Bullewijk, on the edge of the Rondehoep polder.

name: Skydome (Amsterdam)
en: Skydome is a tower block on KNSM-eiland in the Oostelijk Havengebied in Amsterdam-Oost. The 63-metre residential tower, dating from 1996, was designed by Wiel Arets.

name: Spaklerweg 24
en: Spaklerweg 24, Amsterdam, is a building on Spaklerweg, Amsterdam-Oost. It has been a national monument since 2003. It was built as a house for the (chief) overseer of the Zuidergasfabriek, which had its grounds here. The building stood, as it were, pinned to the industrial estate, separated by a street.

name: Spiegelgracht 27
en: Spiegelgracht 27 is a building on the edge of Amsterdam-Centrum. The corner house stands on the corner of Spiegelgracht and Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat.

name: Spiegelgracht 38
en: Spiegelgracht 38 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the corner of Lijnbaansgracht and Spiegelgracht. It once also had a house number on Lijnbaansgracht, but this has lapsed. The building has been a national monument since 1970.

name: Spinnekop (Amsterdam)
en: Spinnekop is a block of flats in the Molenwijk neighbourhood, Oostzanerwerf district, in Amsterdam-Noord. According to the Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen, Spinnekop is not a street name but the name of a landscape area. It is surrounded by a parkland setting, which as a whole is called Molenwijk.

name: Spinoza Lyceum
en: The Spinoza Lyceum is a secondary school in Amsterdam, named after the philosopher Baruch Spinoza, a pantheist who sought his answers in the connection or relationship of humanity and nature, alongside or with the divine. Since 1957 the Spinoza Lyceum has been based at Peter van Anrooystraat 8 in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Splendor (muziekgebouw)
en: Splendor is a music venue in the Uilenburg district in the centre of Amsterdam, housed in a monumental building constructed in the style of the Amsterdam School.

name: Spui 10
en: Spui 10 was originally a shop and department store on the Spui in Amsterdam. The building, in the eclectic style, was built in 1891–1892 to a design by architect Eduard Cuypers. It has four storeys (ground floor, mezzanine, and two floors under a roof) on a square ground plan.

name: Spuistraat 289 (Amsterdam)
en: Spuistraat 289 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Spuistraat 53 (Amsterdam)
en: Spuistraat 53 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Stadhouderskade 5
en: Stadhouderskade 5 and 6 is a building on Stadhouderskade in Amsterdam, also known as ‘Atlanta’. The brick-red building has seven storeys and a spear-shaped tower.

name: Stadhouderskade 7
en: Stadhouderskade 7 (sometimes including 9) is a building on Stadhouderskade in Amsterdam. It was built to a design by the architect Foeke Kuipers, of Frisian origin. He designed it for the Algemene Maatschappij voor Jongemannen (AMVJ) and its Hotel Centraal. After the AMVJ had left, the entire building was given a hospitality use.

name: Stadionkade 113
en: Stadionkade 113 is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuid. On Stadionkade, at a bend in the Zuider Amstelkanaal, stands a relatively large school building, in use by the Olympiaschool in 2019. The municipality awarded the work on 29 June 1931; the school officially opened a year and a half later, though not all rooms were yet in use.

name: Stadsloket Zuidoost
en: The Stadsdeelkantoor Zuidoost, also known as Stadsloket Zuidoost, is a striking building in the Amsterdam-Zuidoost district. The office, on Anton de Komplein, was completed in 2006 to a design by ADP Architecten.

name: Staringplein 9 (Amsterdam)
en: Staringplein 9 in Amsterdam-West is a structure in the Overtoomse Sluis district.

name: Stenen Silo
en: The Stenen Silo is a former grain silo on Silodam in Amsterdam. The 19th-century silo was declared a national monument in 1996. It is officially called Korthals Altes, after Jan Philip Korthals Altes, municipal councillor and director of the N.V. Maatschappij tot Exploitatie van Graansilo’s en Pakhuizen.

name: Stoomgemaal Halfweg
en: Museum Stoomgemaal Halfweg is a steam pumping station dating from 1852, located in Halfweg, North Holland, on the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder. It is the oldest and largest still-working paddle-wheel steam pumping station in the world.

name: Telecomtoren Zuidas
en: The Telecomtoren Zuidas is a microwave link tower on the Zuidas in Amsterdam. The tower was built to establish inter-local telephone connections and is owned by Cellnex Netherlands B.V. (formerly Alticom Datacenters). Cellnex took over this tower, together with 24 other telecom and data towers, from KPN (formerly PTT).

name: Teslatoren
en: The Teslatoren is a residential tower on the corner of Middenweg and Kruislaan in Amsterdam-Oost, built in 1998.

name: The Curve (Amsterdam)
en: The Curve is an office building in the North Holland city of Amsterdam, in the Amsterdam-Noord borough. It is unlike any other building in the area, which was previously dominated by the buildings of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij.

name: The George (Amsterdam)
en: The George is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuid, Buitenveldert, Zuidas. It was designed by Liesbeth van der Pol, Pieter Lievense, Johan Rombouts and Niek Slijkerman of DOK architecten, who thereby contributed a small part to the completion of the Zuidas, in this case between George Gershwinstraat and the drainage channel Boelegracht.

name: The International (Amsterdam)
en: The International is a golf club in Badhoevedorp, in the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer, north-east of Schiphol.

name: The Whale (Amsterdam)
en: The Whale (also known as The Sfinx or Sphinx) is a building in Amsterdam-Oost. It was built in the 1990s during the redevelopment of the Oostelijk Havengebied in Amsterdam. Almost everything connected with port works disappeared, and a residential neighbourhood was built on the Sporenburg peninsula.

name: Thonikgebouw
en: Thonikgebouw is a building on the north-eastern projecting corner of Wibautstraat and Grensstraat, Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Tolhuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Tolhuis in Amsterdam-Noord stands at Buiksloterweg 7, by the Buiksloterweg ferry, now also known as the ‘Tolhuispont’. The Buiksloterveer was already mentioned in 1308, shortly after Amsterdam came into being, and probably existed earlier. In 1556 the city bought the ferry but leased it out again, which allowed it to set conditions.

name: Tolhuisweg 1 (Amsterdam)
en: Tolhuisweg 1 in Amsterdam is a monumental building in Amsterdam-Noord. It was designed by architect Arthur Staal and was to house the occupational health service of Koninklijke Shell. Staal designed several buildings for Shell in this neighbourhood. The building dates from 1957.

name: Tolstraat 21-53
en: Tolstraat 21–53 and Pieter Aertszstraat 22–28 in Amsterdam are a row of portiek (shared-entrance) dwellings on the corner of Tolstraat and Pieter Aertszstraat in the ‘Van der Helstpleinbuurt’, Amsterdam-Zuid. The complex was built in two phases in the Nieuwe Pijp.

name: Toren van Ransdorp
en: The Toren van Ransdorp is a monumental, unfinished, richly detailed Late Gothic tower of 1525 in Ransdorp in Amsterdam-Noord. It is the tower of the Ransdorp church and is 32 metres high. From the flat top there is a view over the expansive polder land of Landelijk Noord.

name: Tramremise Koninginneweg
en: The Tramremise on Koninginneweg 29 in Amsterdam-Zuid is a building from 1893, built as a depot for the horse trams of the AOM. The architect was A.L. van Gendt; the building specification shows that he had help with the design from P.H. van Gendt. At the time of construction it stood free of surrounding development, in a meadow.

name: Transformatorhuisje (Halfweg)
en: The transformer station on Schoolstraat 18 in Halfweg was built around 1915 on commission from the Kennemer Electriciteit-Maatschappij (KEM). The architect Han van Loghem designed a good deal for that company, but certainly designed a unique example for Halfweg. There is no other structure with this appearance in the surroundings.

name: Tuinstadhuis
en: The Tuinstadhuis is an office building in Amsterdam in the Slotermeer district, originally the head office of the NVV and, since 1990, a borough office.

name: Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat 18
en: Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat 18-AB in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 43
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 43 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 45
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 45 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 50
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 50 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 52
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 52 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 56
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 56 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 58
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 58 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 64
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 64 is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 8
en: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat 8 is a building on Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Oosterparkstraat 246
en: Tweede Oosterparkstraat 246 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Oosterparkstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. The area was still barely laid out when a Roman Catholic enclave took shape in this part of the Oosterparkbuurt. First came the Sint-Bonifatiuskerk and its presbytery, and shortly afterwards the Catholic school at Eikenplein 1–5.

name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 14
en: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 14 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Rozendwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It bears a strong resemblance to Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 16; together they are the only national monuments in the street.

name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 16
en: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 16 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede Rozendwarsstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. Together with Tweede Rozendwarsstraat 14, it is one of the only two national monuments in the street.

name: Tweede van Swindenstraat 208
en: Tweede van Swindenstraat 208 in Amsterdam is a building on Tweede van Swindenstraat, Dapperbuurt, Amsterdam-Oost. After 1882 there was intensive work on an extension to the Dapperbuurt, which included a primary school.

name: Tweede van Swindenstraat 26
en: Tweede van Swindenstraat 26/Pieter Nieuwlandstraat 3 in Amsterdam is a relatively modern complex on Tweede van Swindenstraat and Pieter Nieuwlandstraat in the Dapperbuurt, Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat 133
en: Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat 133 is a building on Wittenburg, one of the Eastern Islands in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is known as the Markerhuisje or Groenlandhuisje.

name: Valkenburgerstraat 202-210
en: Valkenburgerstraat 202–210 in Amsterdam is a building on Valkenburgerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Valley (Amsterdam)
en: Valley (English for ‘valley’) is a residential and office tower on the Zuidas in Amsterdam. The complex consists of three towers occupying a plot on Beethovenstraat, opposite the head office of ABN AMRO.

name: Van Breestraat 71-77 (Amsterdam)
en: Van Breestraat 71–77 in Amsterdam is a complex of buildings on Van Breestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has been a municipal monument since 31 January 2012. The site, formerly a peat-meadow area, belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1889.

name: Van der Boechorststraat 26
en: Van der Boechorststraat 26, better known as Paviljoen Buitenveldert, is a building on Van der Boechorststraat in Amsterdam-Buitenveldert. The basic design of the building comes from Gerrit Rietveld, who worked on it as architect from 1963 until his death in June 1964.

name: Van der Pekblokken
en: The Van der Pekblokken in Amsterdam consist of two residential complexes in the Indische Buurt, Amsterdam-Oost. The complexes have the addresses Molukkenstraat 66–72, Balistraat 128–144 and Eerste Atjehstraat 135–151.

name: Van Eeghenstraat 103
en: Van Eeghenstraat 103 in Amsterdam is a building on Van Eeghenstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. Van Eeghenstraat is a street full of mansions, built of brick and natural stone, generally with a great deal of ornament. Within this, the building at number 103 stands out considerably.

name: Van Houtenkerk
en: The Van Houtenkerk is a church building in the North Holland town of Weesp. It is also known as the ‘chocolate church’, since it was built on commission from the ladies J.S. and H.C. van Houten of the chocolate factory. It was built on the site of a demolished Van Houten villa on the Oudegracht.

name: Variété Flora
en: Variété Flora was an Amsterdam theatre founded in 1892 by the German entrepreneur and film pioneer Anton Nöggerath (1859–1908). It was located at Amstelstraat 26 and later 20–22–24–26–28 in Amsterdam, and ultimately had more than 1000 seats.

name: Velodrome Amsterdam
en: Velodrome Amsterdam is one of the three covered cycling tracks in the Netherlands. The track was built in 1972 at Sportpark Sloten. It is 200 metres long, has a maximum banking angle of 47° and is made of wooden slats. The municipality of Amsterdam has been the sole manager since 2016, assisted by a large group of volunteers.

name: Verrijzenis van Onze Heer Jezus Christuskerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Verrijzenis van Onze Heer Jezus Christuskerk is a Roman Catholic church on Louis Bouwmeesterstraat in Amsterdam. It was built in 1959–1961 in the Slotervaart district to a design by architect Gerard Holt. It is a modernist church with a free-standing bell tower.

name: Victoria (bioscoop)
en: The Victoria was the name of two cinemas run by Gerardus van Royen in Amsterdam: first on the Nieuwendijk from 1920 to 1922, and later on the Sloterkade in the Amsterdam Hoofddorppleinbuurt from 1934 to 1976. Rotterdam also had a cinema called Victoria.

name: Vijzelgracht 1
en: Vijzelgracht 1 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It stands on the corner of Vijzelgracht and Prinsengracht, on Vijzelgracht opposite Vijzelgracht 2a.

name: Vijzelstraat 81
en: Vijzelstraat 81 in Amsterdam is a corner building on Vijzelstraat 81 and Keizersgracht 660 in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Villa Heineken
en: Villa Heineken is a villa on the corner of Tweede Weteringplantsoen and Nicolaas Witsenkade, Amsterdam-Centrum. The former residence looks out over the small park Tweede Weteringplantsoen and the Singelgracht, on the far side of which stands the former Heineken Brewery.

name: Villa Lebbink
en: Villa Lebbink is a building at Apollolaan 166 in Amsterdam-Zuid. The building, with an attached garage and built brick garden wall, was designed by architect Jo Mulder. He also designed terraced houses for workers from the port in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Viñoly
en: The Viñoly tower on Gustav Mahlerplein is part of the Mahler4 complex on the Zuidas in Amsterdam. It was the first realised design in Europe by the South American architect Rafael Viñoly. The 95-metre-high office tower is constructed with a steel skeleton and a concrete core for stability.

name: Vondelpark 1
en: Vondelpark 1 is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid, Oud-Zuid. The small building is one of eight buildings in the Vondelpark that actually have an address in that park. It is the former supervisor’s house, dating from around 1867, and was built on commission from the ‘Vereeniging tot aanleg van een rij- en wandelpark te Amsterdam’.

name: Vondelpark 4
en: Vondelpark 4 is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid, Oud-Zuid. It is one of the eight buildings that actually have an address in that park. It was built on commission from the Vereeniging tot oprichting van een Rij- en Wandelpark, later the Vondelpark, to provide the necessary drainage in the area of the Overtoom and the Kattensloot.

name: Vondelstraat 51 (Amsterdam)
en: Vondelstraat 51, or Huize Johanna, is a monumental house on Vondelstraat in Amsterdam-West.

name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 1
en: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 1 in Amsterdam is a building on the street Voormalige Stadstimmertuin in Amsterdam-Centrum. The city timber yards mentioned, along with the boatbuilders’ yard, moved from 1898 and 1899 to a complex on Van Reigersbergenstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 2
en: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 2 in Amsterdam is a building on the street Voormalige Stadstimmertuin in Amsterdam-Centrum. The city timber yards mentioned, along with the boatbuilders’ yard, moved from 1898 and 1899 to a complex on Van Reigersbergenstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Vredenburgh (Amsterdam)
en: Vredenburgh is a national monument in Amsterdam, on the Vredenburgersteeg at the northern tip of the Oudezijds Eiland in central Amsterdam. Its oldest parts date from the 15th century.

name: Waalkerk
en: The Waalkerk was a Reformed church building with 1400 seats on Waalstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built in 1936 in the Rivierenbuurt, which had only just been completed. The church was demolished in 1989 and replaced by an apartment complex.

name: Watertoren Entrepot-West
en: Watertoren Entrepot-West in Amsterdam is a tower block designed by architect Hans van Beek and Frans Dirks of the firm Atelier PRO. It stands on the C. van Eesterenlaan, in the former borough of Zeeburg in Amsterdam-Oost. The residential tower has 20 storeys and is 60 metres high.

name: Weesper Automaten Kabinet
en: The Weesper Automaten Kabinet (or Automaten Kabinet Weesp) is a museum in Weesp specialising in historical automata. It is housed in the centre of Weesp, on the Middenstraat, one of the oldest streets in the town. It was founded by Jelle Zijlmans, who is also its owner.

name: Weesperflat
en: The Weesperflat on Weesperstraat in Amsterdam is a large building for student housing, owned by housing association De Key. It lies close to the Waterlooplein, the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam and the H’ART Museum (formerly the Hermitage).

name: Westbatterij
en: The Westbatterij lies on the western bank at the mouth of the Vecht in Muiden. A fortification was already established on this site in 1427, and it was further expanded over time. Above all, the sea lock and the introduction of inundation as a key means of defence greatly strengthened Muiden.

name: Westbeat
en: Westbeat is an apartment and business complex in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is located at Delflandlaan 2 and Rijnlandlaan 3–199. The latter road received its name during the preparations for the complex’s construction (2015) and is a parallel road to the Cornelis Lelylaan.

name: Westerdoksdijk 40
en: Westerdoksdijk 40 in Amsterdam is a building on Westerdoksdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was built between the street on the dyke and the IJ. During construction, rails from the marshalling yard still ran between the street and the building, leading to and from the storage sheds on Stenen Hoofd.

name: Westerstraat 202 (Amsterdam)
en: Westerstraat 202, Amsterdam, is a structure on Westerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building is an anachronism on two sides. Because of its 20th-century architecture it stands out from the rest of the surrounding buildings; in the façade is a gable stone referring to 1770.

name: Westgate II
en: Westgate II is an office building in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, in the Riekerpolder district. The roughly 50-metre-high, H-shaped building stands on the Adam Smithplein, but its addresses are on Thomas R. Malthusstraat (house numbers 1–65). It fills the western side of the square and houses about 30,000 m² of floor space.

name: Weteringschans 104
en: Weteringschans 104 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 106
en: Weteringschans 106 is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 108
en: Weteringschans 108 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 187
en: Weteringschans 187 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 197
en: Weteringschans 197–199 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum. On the drawing board it was given the name Casa Luna.

name: Weteringschans 225
en: Weteringschans 225 in Amsterdam is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 241
en: Weteringschans 241 is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 243
en: Weteringschans 243 is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 245
en: Weteringschans 245 in Amsterdam is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 253
en: Weteringschans 253 in Amsterdam is a mansion on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 257-259
en: Weteringschans 255–259 and Reguliersgracht 138–142 form a complex of mansions on the corner of Weteringschans and Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. In the past, address changes took place here, so the numbering has shifted.

name: Weteringschans 26-28
en: Weteringschans 26 and 28 in Amsterdam are two office buildings on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum. In Amsterdam the buildings are known by the nickname ‘Peper-en-Zout’ (Pepper and Salt).

name: Weteringschans 261
en: Weteringschans 261 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 263
en: Weteringschans 263 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 31
en: Weteringschans 31 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. The school building is on Weteringschans in Amsterdam. It is bounded on the north side by the national monument Weteringschans 29, the Barlaeus Gymnasium. On the opposite side of Weteringschans stands Paradiso, also a national monument.

name: Weteringschans 79
en: Weteringschans 79 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the east side of Weteringschans in Amsterdam, in a short street leading to the Spiegelgracht. The rear and/or side façade of the building faces onto the Zieseniskade. When built in 1881 it formed one architectural whole with Weteringschans 77.

name: Weteringschans 92
en: Weteringschans 92 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 93
en: Weteringschans 93 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was built by, or on the initiative of, the then contractor F.L. Janssen. It was built without a house number and dates from early 1899, when the Building Inspectorate found that it had been built in line with the guidelines issued (13 February 1899).

name: Weteringschans 94
en: Weteringschans 94 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 96
en: Weteringschans 96 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Wielingen (kraakpand)
en: The Wielingen was the name of a squatted building in Amsterdam-Zuid. The name was taken from the Wielingenstraat on which the building stood, which is named after the Wielingen, a main channel in the Westerschelde.

name: Witsenhuis
en: The Witsenhuis is the former studio of Willem Witsen at Oosterpark 82 in Amsterdam. The first floor of the Witsenhuis, named after him, is in its original state. The remaining floors are made available to writers as temporary living space.

name: Woestduinkerk
en: The Woestduinkerk, renamed Jacobuskapel in 1996, was a church building on Woestduinstraat in the Hoofddorppleinbuurt in Amsterdam.

name: Woongebouw Wertheim
en: Woongebouw Wertheim is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Centrum. In the 1990s a complex with a business on the ground floor and dwellings above stood on the corner of Plantage Middenlaan and Plantage Parklaan. The complex was in poor condition, which is why the existing buildings were demolished.

name: Xavier (Amsterdam)
en: Xavier is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is named after site X on which it was built. The complex of 159 apartments consists of one building volume divided into several heights. The front on the Gustav Mahlerlaan is a high-rise with 21 storeys.

name: Zeemanlaboratorium
en: The Zeemanlaboratorium is a former physics laboratory on the Plantage Muidergracht, number 4, in the Dutch city of Amsterdam.

name: Zeemanshuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Zeemanshuis, or Zeemans-huis, is a building at Kadijksplein 17–18 in Amsterdam-Centrum. The rectangular building has side façades on the Nieuwevaart/Prins Hendrikkade and Hoogte Kadijk. It is a sober building in the eclectic style.

name: Ziekenhuis Amstelland
en: Ziekenhuis Amstelland, known as Ziekenhuis Amstelveen from 1978 to 2005 and abbreviated ZHA, is a medical institution (hospital) in the town of Amstelveen in the Dutch province of North Holland.

name: Zonder titel (Per Kirkeby)
en: On the Hildo Kropplein in Amsterdam-Oost stands an untitled artwork by the Danish artist Per Kirkeby. The work is best described as ‘Bakstenen beeld met vijver’ (Brick sculpture with pond). Kirkeby became known for his brick sculptures.

name: Zonnehuis
en: The Zonnehuis (the façade reads ’t Zonnehuis) is a building at Zonneplein 30 in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Zorro (gebouw)
en: Zorro is a building in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The tower block, also called the Ecutoren, was built from 1995 to 1999 to a design by Tangram Architecten (Bart Mispelblom Beyer and Charlotte ten Dijke). The Ecuplein, from which it takes its name, is an open space in the Middelveldsche Akerpolder district.

name: Zuidelijk Citroëngebouw
en: The Zuidelijk Citroëngebouw, or Citroëngarage, is a building that was originally a garage and showroom on the Stadionplein in Amsterdam. It served as the head office of Citroën Nederland until 2014. It was built from 1930 to 1931 to a design by Jan Wils.

name: Zuidelijk ventilatiegebouw IJ-tunnel
en: The Zuidelijk Ventilatiegebouw IJ-tunnel is a structure in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is one of the two ventilation towers that keep the air in the IJ-tunnel fresh; the southern one stands at Piet Heinkade 2, next to the Oosterdoksdoorgang. The idea of ventilation towers was new in Amsterdam.

name: Zuiderbad
en: The Zuiderbad is an indoor swimming pool in Amsterdam-Zuid at Hobbemastraat 24A–26. It lies on the corner of Hobbemastraat and Hobbemakade, diagonally behind the Rijksmuseum. The Zuiderbad has been protected as a national monument since 1996.

name: 212 (restaurant)
en: 212 is a restaurant in Amsterdam run by head chefs Richard van Oostenbrugge and Thomas Groot. The establishment has held two Michelin stars since 29 March 2021.

name: Achtergracht 11F
en: Achtergracht 11-F in Amsterdam is a small building on the Achtergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. Buildings along that canal were given municipal or national monument status in the 20th century. These are mainly converted warehouses (Pakhuis January to Pakhuis November) or mansions.

name: Afzelia (gebouw)
en: Afzelia is an apartment building on Wiborgeiland 201–281 in the Houthavens in the Westelijk Havengebied of the Dutch capital Amsterdam. The Houthavens long formed, quite literally, the timber harbour of Amsterdam. It was an area with much water and mooring jetties.

name: Akropolistoren
en: Akropolistoren, or Akropolis, is an apartment complex in Amsterdam. It was designed by the architectural firm Studioninedots for the north-western tip of the Sportheldenbuurt on Zeeburgereiland.

name: Albert Cuypstraat 182
en: The property Albert Cuypstraat 182 is a building on Albert Cuypstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of three municipal monuments on that street. The symmetrical building stands out, in size, robustness and solidity, from its neighbours and from the opposite side of Albert Cuypstraat.

name: Albert Cuypstraat 241
en: The property ‘Albert Cuypstraat 241’ is a building on Albert Cuypstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of three municipal monuments on that street. It was built as a primary school on the corner of Albert Cuypstraat and Eerste Sweelinckstraat.

name: Albert Cuypstraat 88
en: The building at Albert Cuypstraat 88 is a structure on Albert Cuypstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The building, about 5 metres wide and 15 metres deep, was built to a design by Publieke Werken van Amsterdam. It was intended to serve as an additional fire station to the one on Ferdinand Bolstraat 8.

name: Albrecht Dürerstraat 36 (gymnastieklokaal)
en: Albrecht Dürerstraat 36 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (512947).

name: Sint-Petrus'-Bandenkerk (Diemen)
en: The Sint-Petrus'-Bandenkerk is a church at Hartveldseweg 25 in Diemen, North Holland. The three-aisled hall church of 1910 has an almost rectangular ground plan and a saddle roof fitted with steekkappen (half-hipped ends).

name: Sloterweg 1210-1212
en: Sloterweg 1210-1212 in Amsterdam is a two-part building on Sloterweg in Sloten, in the Amsterdam Nieuw-West borough.

name: Smaragdplein 3-5
en: Smaragdplein 3-5 in Amsterdam is a building on Smaragdplein, Diamantbuurt, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Spaklerweg 26-28
en: Spaklerweg 26-28, Amsterdam, is a building on Spaklerweg, Amsterdam-Oost. It has been a national monument since 2003. It was built as a house for the director and deputy engineer of the Zuidergasfabriek, which had its grounds here. The building stood, as it were, pinned to the industrial estate, separated by a street.

name: Stadhouderskade 140-141
en: Stadhouderskade 140-141 consists of two equal buildings on Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. Both were designed by Jan Willem Hartgerink and Hendrik Dirks Kramer, who between them almost completed this stretch of Stadhouderskade. Hartgerink and Kramer used the eclectic style.

name: Toldwarsstraat 1-7
en: Toldwarsstraat 1-7 in Amsterdam is a building of relatively large volume on Toldwarsstraat in the 'Van der Helstpleinbuurt', Amsterdam-Zuid. Its side façades received the addresses Pieter Aertszstraat 62-64 and Tolstraat 57-59. Tolstraat was built up westwards from the Amstel and Amsteldijk.

name: Tolstraat 136-142
en: Tolstraat 136-142 in Amsterdam is a building block on Tolstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. The block is a municipal monument (222102). The plot, with 19th-century architecture, is overshadowed by the neighbouring Tolstraat 160 of light-coloured concrete and the much lighter-coloured Asschergebouw by Gerrit van Arkel (two national monuments).

name: Tommaso Albinonistraat 200-204
en: Tommaso Albinonistraat 200-204 in Amsterdam is a 55-metre-high building on Tommaso Albinonistraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Zuidas district.

name: Tuinstraat 100-102
en: Tuinstraat 100-102 is a complex on Tuinstraat, Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum. It consists of two buildings with an open space between them. The separation from 'the street' is a wall.

name: Tuinstraat 137-141
en: Tuinstraat 137-141 in Amsterdam is a building on Tuinstraat, Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat 43-53
en: Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat 43-53 in Amsterdam is a small block of residential and shop units on Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat in Amsterdam-West. The block still has structures on its wings, at Eerste Helmersstraat 82-84 and Tweede Helmersstraat 123.

name: Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat 2-86
en: The complex Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat 2-86/Eerste van der Helststraat 1 is a building with sixty dwellings on the corner of Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat and Eerste van der Helststraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. The building stands out in the neighbourhood because of its size.

name: Van der Helstplein 7-17
en: Van der Helstplein 7-17 is a complex of buildings on Van der Helstplein in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has been a national monument since 6 December 2004. By the 1910s the municipal built-up area of Amsterdam had reached the Rustenburgerstraat. To the south of it lay a watercourse, which was soon filled in.

name: Voorburgstraat 2-242
en: Voorburgstraat 2-242 in Amsterdam is a townscape-defining block of flats on Voorburgstraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is known locally as the Elisabeth Steinflat.

name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 4-6
en: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin 4-6 in Amsterdam is a building on the street Voormalige Stadstimmertuin in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Vosmaerstraat 1-321
en: Vosmaerstraat 1-321 in Amsterdam is a building on Vosmaerstraat in Amsterdam-West, a municipal monument since 14 April 2009. The street was named in 1911 and built up afterwards. Its even-numbered north side received portiek dwellings; the odd-numbered south side became a 'Gesticht voor jongens' (boys' institution).

name: Vossiusstraat 21-32
en: Vossiusstraat 21-32 in Amsterdam is a block of buildings on Vossiusstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. Vossiusstraat, named after Gerardus Vossius by council resolution of 19 November 1879, was initially only a short lane. It was laid out in a strip south of the later Vondelpark.

name: Weteringschans 126-128
en: Weteringschans 126-128 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum. For centuries this was agricultural land, but Amsterdam expanded strongly in the 19th century. On the site between the Weteringplantsoen and the Paleis voor Volksvlijt, the Schans was also incorporated for housing construction.

name: Weteringschans 193-195
en: Weteringschans 193-195 in Amsterdam is a double building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 219-223
en: Weteringschans 219-223 in Amsterdam is a triple building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 227-229
en: Weteringschans 227-229 is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 231-233
en: Weteringschans 231-233 is a residential building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 247-251
en: Weteringschans 247-251 is a set of three mansions on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 72-74
en: Weteringschans 72-74 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Weteringschans 88-90
en: Weteringschans 88-90 in Amsterdam is a building on Weteringschans in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: WG-Plein 1-78
en: WG-Plein 1-78 in Amsterdam is a building on the WG-Plein in Amsterdam-West. The WG-Plein was laid out on the grounds of the Wilhelminagasthuis. An ophthalmic clinic had been put out to tender for that hospital as early as 1904. The clinic, discussed for a year beforehand, was also to house a sisters' house. It opened the following year.

name: Wibautstraat 220-222
en: Wibautstraat 220-222 is a building on Wibautstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. It lies east of the railway embankment on which the Spoorlijn Amsterdam–Elten was built around 1956, and was designed by the architects W.A. Ulrich and B.J.F. Kamphuis. They proposed three stacked cubes with square floors (sides 31 metres), one underground.

name: Wibautstraat 80-86
en: Wibautstraat 80-86, Eerste Oosterparkstraat 52 is a building on the south-western corner of Wibautstraat and Eerste Oosterparkstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. The architecture of the two sides has differed considerably since the 1970s. The original development on Eerste Oosterparkstraat mainly comprises dwellings from around 1900.

name: Willem Beukelsstraat 32-38
en: Willem Beukelsstraat 32-38 in Amsterdam concerns four plots on Willem Beukelsstraat in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Zon's Hofje
en: Zon's Hofje, also known as Zonshofje, is a hofje (almshouse courtyard) on the Amsterdam Prinsengracht. It was built around 1765 for Mennonite women aged 50 and over. In the course of the 19th century the complex was extended with two buildings on the Prinsengracht, both of which have several storeys.

name: Achtergracht 17-19
en: Achtergracht 17-19 in Amsterdam is a building on the Achtergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Achtergracht is a 17th-century canal within the old inner city, bounded by the Singelgracht. As on the other canals, canal houses were built here, often with a business unit, dwellings and a pakzolder (storage attic).

name: Amstel 135-141
en: Amstel 135-141 in Amsterdam is a building on the Amstel in Amsterdam-Centrum. Some of the residents have a view over the River Amstel. Amsterdam grew steadily outwards from the inside and by the late 17th century had reached this spot, just within the Weteringschans – Sarphatistraat ring.

name: Amstel Taveerne
en: Amstel Taveerne was the original name of a well-known gay café on the corner of the Amstel and Halvemaansteeg in central Amsterdam. The business opened in 1964, was renamed Amstel Fifty Four in 2007 and closed in summer 2024. It is often thought that the Amstel Taveerne was Amsterdam's oldest gay café, but that is not correct.

name: Amsteldijk 25
en: The building Amsteldijk 25 stands on the Amsteldijk in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is situated on the corner of Tweede Jan van der Heydenstraat 109. Together with the corner building on the Stadhouderskade, it is the only monument within the Oude Pijp on the Amsteldijk.

name: Amstelstein
en: Amstelstein was the nickname of the complex at Vijzelstraat 36-100 in Amsterdam, a residential and shopping gallery in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Vijzelstraat was widened in the 1920s to give traffic more room. The widening was carried out in phases, as a considerable number of buildings had to be demolished.

name: Amsterdam The Style Outlets
en: Amsterdam The Style Outlets is an outlet centre in Halfweg, between the towns of Haarlem and Amsterdam. It is the first branch of The Style Outlets in the Netherlands, and the first outlet centre in the Randstad.

name: Amsterdams Theaterhuis
en: The Amsterdams Theaterhuis is an Amsterdam theatre on the WG-terrein. Alongside a theatre school, it offers space to both amateur and professional performing artists, and its gallery seats 95 visitors. Theatergroep Toetssteen and Theatergroep De Spelers, among others, stage their productions there.

name: Amsterdamsche Schaakhuis
en: The Amsterdamsche Schaakhuis was a mind-sports centre located at Henri Polaklaan (formerly Plantage Franschelaan) 14 in the Plantage district of Amsterdam. The building was mainly used by chess clubs in Amsterdam.

name: April (café)
en: April was a gay café in Amsterdam which became world-famous for its striking interior decoration, talked-about parties and a revolving bar. Café April opened in 1981 and was located at Reguliersdwarsstraat 37 in Amsterdam. The business closed in 2010.

name: Asterdorp
en: Asterdorp in Amsterdam-Noord was an emergency village of housing for families deemed inadmissible, built in 1927. Asterdorp was built on the former industrial site in the Buiksloterham between the Asterweg and the Distelweg. The complex consisted of 132 homes, far from the inhabited world.

name: AVA-woonblok H
en: AVA-woonblok H in Amsterdam is a housing complex of workers' dwellings built by the Amsterdamsche Vereeniging tot het bouwen van Arbeiderswoningen (AVA), constructed between 1879 and 1881 in the Amsterdamse Zeeheldenbuurt. This complex was designed by city architect Bastiaan de Greef.

name: AVA-woonblok I
en: AVA-woonblok I in Amsterdam is a housing complex of workers' dwellings built by the Amsterdamsche Vereeniging tot het bouwen van Arbeiderswoningen (AVA), constructed between 1883 and 1884 in the Amsterdamse Zeeheldenbuurt. This complex was designed by city architect Bastiaan de Greef.

name: Baker McKenzie House
en: The Baker McKenzie House, until 2016 Baker & McKenzie House, is an office building on Claude Debussylaan in the Mahler4 area of the Zuidas in Amsterdam. It is used by the Dutch branch of the American law firm Baker McKenzie. The building was designed by American architect Michael Graves (1934-2015).

name: Bar Buka
en: Bar Buka is a women's café in Amsterdam, located since 2019 at Albert Cuypstraat 124 in De Pijp.

name: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46
en: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46 is a building on the southern edge of the Bijdorpplantsoen in Amsterdam-Oost. Staff housing once stood here, belonging to the Bijlmerbajes prison, which stood just to the north of the small complex.

name: Binnenhof (Amstelveen)
en: The Binnenhof in Amstelveen is a shopping centre in the centre of Amstelveen in the Dutch province of North Holland. The original shopping centre was designed by Van den Broek en Bakema.

name: Bistro de la Mer
en: Bistro de la Mer is a restaurant in Amsterdam. It received one Michelin star when the Michelin stars for 2023 were awarded.

name: Blend (gebouw)
en: Blend is a residential complex on the Haarlemmerweg in Amsterdam Oud-West. Here, from the 2010s onwards, the redevelopment of an office park into a residential neighbourhood began. Four residential towers were erected on the narrow strip between the Haarlemmerweg and the allotment gardens and Westerpark.

name: Byzantium (gebouw)
en: The Byzantium is a complex on the Stadhouderskade in Amsterdam-West. The building, in the Museumkwartier, is enclosed by the Vondelpark, the Stadhouderskade and the Tesselschadestraat. At completion, it was one of the largest buildings in the city, certainly in the neighbourhood where it was built.

name: Calandlyceum
en: The Calandlyceum is a secondary school in Amsterdam Osdorp, in the Nieuw-West borough. The school is located on the Pieter Calandlaan between Louis Davidsstraat and Hoekenes.

name: Caransa Hotel
en: The Caransa Hotel (official name NH Caransa) is a four-star hotel in the city centre of Amsterdam. The hotel is located on the Rembrandtplein.

name: Cinema International
en: Cinema International, previously Cinema West and afterwards simply Cinema, was a cinema in the Overtoomse Veld district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The cinema was located on the August Allebeplein and from 1975 bore the name Cinema International, which turned it from a neighbourhood cinema into an ordinary cinema. It closed at the end of 1999.

name: Concordia Inter Nos
en: Concordia Inter Nos was a housing association founded at the start of the 20th century in the former municipality of Sloten to build affordable and sound workers' housing in Osdorp for peat workers and farm labourers. The housing stock was transferred to the municipality of Amsterdam in 1958, after which the association was dissolved.

name: Concordia Noordwest
en: Concordia Noordwest is a complex of small houses on the corner of the Westerstraat and Lijnbaansgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum, covering addresses 327 to 405 and Lijnbaansgracht 63-65. Amsterdam has three Concordia hofjes (almshouse courtyards): two on the Westerstraat (the other being Concordia Noordoost) and Concordia Zuid on the Elandstraat.

name: Cromhouthuis
en: The Cromhouthuis is a patrician house and one of the Cromhouthuizen on the Herengracht in Amsterdam. Until 2020 the house housed the Bijbels Museum and a branch of the Amsterdam Museum. That year the building was taken over by Stadsherstel. The house was built for the Cromhout family, but nothing remains of their furnishings.

name: Cruquiusweg 83D
en: Cruquiusweg 83D is a building on the Cruquiusweg in the Eastern Docklands area of Amsterdam-Oost. It is known as the 'Insulindegebouwtje'.

name: Crystal Tower (Amsterdam)
en: The Crystal Tower is an office building in Westpoort, in the Teleport district, in Amsterdam near Sloterdijk station. At 95 m, the office tower is one of the fourteen tallest buildings in Amsterdam. On the outside, this skyline tower also served as the tower of the fictional company Sanders Inc. in the soap opera Goede tijden, slechte tijden.

name: Daalder (restaurant)
en: Restaurant Daalder is a restaurant in Amsterdam run by hospitality entrepreneur Frans van Dam, with chef and co-owner Dennis Huwaë. Under Huwaë's culinary leadership, the restaurant received a Michelin star on 29 March 2021.

name: Danscafé Havana
en: Danscafé Havana, or simply Havana, was a café-cum-club that opened in 1989 at Reguliersdwarsstraat 17-19 in central Amsterdam. The venue closed in 2002 but reopened briefly several times between 2009 and 2011.

name: Datacenter Westpoort
en: Datacenter Westpoort is a planned large data centre (hyperscale) being built on the Plimsollweg in Amsterdam, near Sloterdijk station in the Western Harbour area. The only party so far set to use the data centre is Microsoft.

name: De bonte zwaan
en: De bonte zwaan is a structure in Amsterdam, in the Houthavens.

name: De Hoop (Rietlanden)
en: De Hoop was the name of one of three timber-sawing windmills in Amsterdam that stood on the Zaagmolensloot. This ditch was a dead-end side arm of the Nieuwe Vaart, the water north of the Zeeburgerdijk, in the Rietlanden. De Hoop was built in 1660 by Vechter and Cornelisz Jansz.

name: De Juwelier (restaurant)
en: De Juwelier is a restaurant in Amsterdam. It received one Michelin star when the Michelin stars for 2022 were awarded. In 2026 the restaurant lost its Michelin star.

name: De Kandelaar (Amsterdam-Zuidoost)
en: De Kandelaar is a multifunctional association building in Amsterdam-Zuidoost, opposite Ganzenhoef metro station and next to the Cultureel Educatief Centrum (CEC Amsterdam). It houses fifteen migrant churches from Amsterdam-Zuidoost. There are five church halls, which together seat 900 worshippers.

name: De Pilsner Club (Amsterdam)
en: De Pilsener Club, better known as 'De Engelse Reet', is a historic café in central Amsterdam. The café is located on the Begijnensteeg, near the Kalverstraat and the Begijnhof, and is a typical brown café.

name: De Punt (gebouw)
en: De Punt is the nickname of a corner building at Gerard Doustraat 129-137 (odd numbers) and Quellijnstraat 152-156 in Amsterdam. The nickname arises because the streets cross at a sharp angle, which was caused by the use of two layouts during the planning of De Pijp.

name: De Spakler
en: De Spakler is a residential tower in Amsterdam-Oost, located on the Spaklerweg. The tower is around 73 metres high and therefore had to meet specific requirements for such buildings, for example for fire safety, particularly the risk of fire spreading. The tower is built from precast concrete facades.

name: De stal int Nuland
en: De stal int Nuland is a relocated façade stone on the Zuiderkerkhof, Zandstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The inscription is a contraction of 'De stal in het nieuwe land' and shows a stable in what was then still agricultural land.

name: De Vrouwe Maria
en: De Vrouwe Maria (also known as the Seskant and the Vrouwe Anna Maria) was a stellingmolen (trestle mill) on the Kwakerspoel in Amsterdam. The mill stood at the spot of today's junction of the Kinkerstraat and the Bilderdijkkade. The mill, a hexagonal bovenkruier (cap-turning windmill), was used for timber sawing.

name: Dorpskerk (Aalsmeer)
en: The Dorpskerk is a church on Dorpsstraat 11 in the North Holland town of Aalsmeer. The cruciform church has a nave intersected by three transepts.

name: Droogbak 11
en: Droogbak 11 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. The numbering of Droogbak street starts at number 1 with the Droogbak. Opposite is a façade wall with continuous (that is, odd and even) numbering up to number 17 on the corner of the Buiten Wieringerstraat. House numbers 3 and 12 are missing.

name: East House
en: East House is an apartment complex on the Markelerbergpad in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The Markelerbergpad is a kind of service road to the much wider Meibergdreef, one of the main traffic routes through Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat 120
en: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat 120 in Amsterdam is a building on the Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat in Amsterdam-West. The building also has an entrance on the Vondelstraat 72.

name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat 42
en: Eerste Van Swindenstraat 42 in Amsterdam is a building on the Eerste van Swindenstraat in the Dapperbuurt, Amsterdam-Oost. In 1891 a small children's nursery was built here. The client was the Vereeniging tot verbetering der kleine Kinderbewaarplaatsen (childcare association), led by Femina Muller. The architect Coenraad Wiegand was engaged for the project.

name: Eikenplein 2-22
en: Eikenplein 2-22 is a building on the Eikenplein in Amsterdam-Oost. It is the only building on the west side of the square; on the east side too there is only one building, a school. Eikenplein 2-22 forms a single ensemble with buildings on the Tweede (200-242) and Derde Oosterparkstraat (201-235).

name: Elandsgracht 113
en: Elandsgracht 113 is a shop with a house in the Jordaan in Amsterdam-Centrum. The corner building lies on the northern side of the Elandsgracht, filled in around 1891, and the Lijnbaansgracht. There has been building here for centuries; on Joan Blaeu's map of 1649 the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht is already almost entirely built up.

name: Energetica (museum)
en: The Energetica public centre was a museum of energy technology. The museum opened its doors in 1999 in the former Amsterdam power station of 1903. The museum covered both energy production and the use of gas and electricity.

name: Flevorama (Muiderberg)
en: The villa Flevorama in the Dutch village of Muiderberg is a monumental building on the slope of the former Zuiderzee coast.

name: Foeliestraat 2-8
en: Foeliestraat 2-8 in Amsterdam is a building on the Foeliestraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Fokke Simonszstraat 45-49
en: The building Fokke Simonszstraat 45-49 in Amsterdam is in Amsterdam-Centrum, Weteringbuurt. It dates from 1907/1908 and so did not experience the period when the street was still the Nieuwe Looiersgracht (filled in around 1875).

name: Fokke Simonszstraat 59-63
en: Fokke Simonszstraat 59-63 is a building complex on the Fokke Simonzstraat in the Weteringbuurt in Amsterdam-Centrum. Buildings have stood here for centuries, dating back to the time of the Nieuwe Looierssloot. The original buildings were demolished long ago and rebuilt. In the 21st century this history repeated itself.

name: G. Perlee Draaiorgelmuseum
en: The G. Perlee Draaiorgelmuseum is a museum in Amsterdam with a changing collection of barrel organs from the Perlee organ company. The museum is located at Westerstraat 119 in the Jordaan, where the Perlee organ company has been based since 1932. In that year the museum's namesake, Gijs Perlee, took over the company from his father-in-law Leon Warnies.

name: Garstenmolen
en: The Garstenmolen in Nigtevecht was built in 1876 on the site of an earlier mill that had burned down. Until 1960 the mill drained the Garstenpolder; afterwards the Garstenmolen was converted into a holiday home and its working machinery was removed. Until the mid-1990s the mill was capable of turning.

name: Geert Groote College Amsterdam
en: The Geert Groote College Amsterdam, colloquially called 'het Geert Groote', is a Steiner school (vrijeschool) for secondary education in Amsterdam-Zuid. Pupils can follow the vmbo, havo and vwo tracks there.

name: Gemaal De Bolstra
en: Gemaal De Bolstra is a modern pumping station from 1991 which, together with other pumping stations, is responsible for water management within the Haarlemmermeerpolder. The station is located on the Aalsmeerderdijk near Oude Meer, east of Aalsmeerderbrug.

name: Gemaal Mercatorstraat
en: Gemaal Mercatorstraat is a structure in Amsterdam-West. The pumping station, with an attached electricity building, has been placed on the corner of the Jan van Galenstraat and Mercatorstraat. It lies at the south-western tip of the Erasmuspark, although it is not really part of the park, being separated from it by a ring canal around the park.

name: Gerard Doustraat 156
en: The building Gerard Doustraat 156 is a building on the Gerard Doustraat in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of five municipal monuments on that street. The building was built to a design by architect Willem Hamer jr. He designed a building in the Neo-Renaissance style.

name: Gerard Doustraat 175-181
en: The building Gerard Doustraat 175-181 is a building on the Gerard Doustraat in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of five municipal monuments on that street. The building has a celebrated past. Its first user and owner, with its factory chimney, was the carriage factory W.H. van Eck en Zonen.

name: Gerechtshof Amsterdam
en: The Gerechtshof Amsterdam is a Dutch court of appeal that hears cases from the Amsterdam and Noord-Holland district courts on appeal. Its jurisdiction covers most of the province of North Holland (except the Gooi). It is therefore the smallest jurisdiction since the revision of the judicial map on 1 January 2013.

name: Gerrit van der Veen College
en: The Gerrit van der Veen College is a secondary school in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Gertrude (restaurant)
en: Gertrude is a restaurant on the Bosboom Toussaintstraat in the Amsterdam district of Oud-West. Gertrude opened its doors in March 2020. Its owners were Géza Weisz and Tijn Verstappen. After a year they brought in Amadou Dia as chef, who had previously cooked for restaurant Bordewijk on the Noordermarkt and Boca Cocktail Lounge in Barcelona.

name: Govert Flinckstraat 286
en: The building Govert Flinckstraat 286 on the corner of Eerste Sweelinckstraat 22 is a building at the junction of the Govert Flinckstraat and Eerste Sweelinckstraat in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is built in the Neo-Gothic style and was designed by Publieke Werken Amsterdam.

name: Graphite by Peter Gast
en: Graphite by Peter Gast is a restaurant in Amsterdam. The eatery was opened at the end of 2018 by Peter Gast and Jacqueline van Liere. The restaurant held a Michelin star from 2020 up to and including 2024. In February 2025 the restaurant closed.

name: Grote Kerk (Westzaan)
en: The Grote Kerk is a church on Kerkbuurt 37 in the North Holland village of Westzaan. The cruciform church was built in 1740-1741 with a rich façade in régence style, possibly to a design by Amsterdam master carpenter Jan van der Streng. The foundation stone was laid on 19 May 1740 and the consecration took place on 14 July 1741.

name: H.H. Cosmas en Damianuskerk (Abcoude)
en: The H.H. Cosmas en Damianuskerk is a Roman Catholic church on Kerkstraat 23 in Abcoude.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 128
en: Haarlemmerdijk 128 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Haarlemmerdijk has buildings of all periods and in all architectural styles. Max Put noted in his book Art nouveau in Amsterdam (2022) that relatively many buildings in that style can be found there.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 140
en: Haarlemmerdijk 140, Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 63
en: Haarlemmerdijk 63 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building extends into the Binnen Oranjestraat. The Haarlemmerdijk is centuries old, and much of the original building has been replaced, sometimes more than once. At the corner in question the biggest change took place around 1937.

name: Haarlemmerplein 1
en: Haarlemmerplein 1 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerplein, the longest part of the row of buildings on the Haarlemmerdijk 177-179. Haarlemmerplein 1 gives access to the homes; the addresses on the Haarlemmerdijk lead to the shopping section.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 141-179 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 141-179 in Amsterdam is a residential and shopping complex on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 87 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 87, Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 2004 it was given protected status as a municipal monument (no. 204020). The Haarlemmerstraat is a centuries-old street just north of the canal ring.

name: Hallen Theater
en: The Hallen Theater, also known as the Hallen Bioscoop, was a theatre and cinema at Jan van Galenstraat 41 in the Amsterdam-West district of Amsterdam. The theatre opened on 30 October 1936, in the presence of alderman Monne de Miranda, with the film De jongste rebel (The Littlest Rebel) starring Shirley Temple.

name: Halte Aalsmeer Oost
en: Halte Aalsmeer Oost (until 1930 Halte Oosteinde; telegraphic codes Ao and Oe respectively) is a former railway halt on the Spoorlijn Aalsmeer – Amsterdam Willemspark, built and operated at the time by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij.

name: Hemonystraat 9
en: The building Hemonystraat 9 is a building on the Hemonystraat in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of the two municipal monuments on that street; the other is at Hemonystraat 22. The building was designed as a house, probably by architect Hendrik Dirks Kramer.

name: Hervormde kerk (Ilpendam)
en: The Nederlands Hervormde Kerk is a single-aisled church on the Kerkstraat in the North Holland village of Ilpendam. The church partly dates from 1656.

name: Hervormde Kerk (Oostzaan)
en: The Hervormde Kerk (also known as the Grote Kerk) is a church on Kerkbuurt 12 in the North Holland village of Oostzaan. The cruciform church, with a wooden tower above the façade decorated with rococo scroll brackets, was built in 1760. The church was built on a terp because in earlier times it had to be usable as a place of refuge.

name: Het Huis van Aristoteles
en: Het Huis van Aristoteles was a museum in Amsterdam aimed mainly at young children. Topics included children's literature, art, cultures and science, among others. The house is named after the Greek philosopher Aristotle, who was the first to recognise the importance of the senses for the ability to learn.

name: Hollandia (Ankeveen)
en: De Hollandia is a polder windmill in the Dutch village of Ankeveen which drained the Hollandsche Ankeveense polder. As early as 1538 there was probably already a mill for this polder. The present mill was built in 1640, most likely on the site of its predecessor. Via the 's-Gravelandse vaart it pumped water out onto the Vecht.

name: Ignatiushuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Ignatiushuis is a religious formation centre of the Jesuits in Amsterdam. Since 2000 it has been located on the Beulingstraat, around the corner from the Jesuit church Krijtberg (Sint Franciscus Xaverius) on the Singel in Amsterdam's city centre.

name: Islamitisch gebeds- en bewassingruimte De Nieuwe Ooster
en: The Islamitisch gebeds- en bewassingruimte is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost on the grounds of De Nieuwe Ooster. The whole was opened on 5 June 2012 by alderman Andrée van Es of Amsterdam.

name: Israël Queridoschool
en: The Israël Queridoschool is a former school building in the West borough of Amsterdam. In 2021 the building was demolished to make way for new construction.

name: Jacob Bontiusplaats 1
en: Jacob Bontiusplaats 1 is a complex of two small buildings in Amsterdam-Centrum, on the Oostelijke Eilanden at the junction with the Oostenburgermiddenstraat. The two buildings were part of what were once the factories of Werkspoor and its successor Stork.
