The Oostelijke Eilanden were full of such factories, except for the adjoining residential neighbourhood.

name: Jacob van Lennepkade 334
en: The Jacob van Lennepkade 334 is an old building in Amsterdam-West.

name: Jan Evertsenstraat 1 (Amsterdam)
en: Jan Evertsenstraat 1, Amsterdam forms part of a building that, although it has a house number on the Jan Evertsenstraat in Amsterdam, stands physically separate from the other buildings on that street. The first even number lies diagonally across the street, and number 7 is on the other side of the Witte de Withstraat.

name: Justitieel Complex Schiphol
en: The Justitieel Complex Schiphol (JCS) is a building housing several judicial institutions. It stands on the Noord-West business park near the Dutch Schiphol airport.

name: Kantoor en rouwcentrum De Nieuwe Ooster
en: The Kantoor en rouwcentrum De Nieuwe Ooster is a building in Amsterdam-Oost. It was erected in 2010-2012, when the western part of the De Nieuwe Ooster cemetery was redeveloped according to the insights of Karres en Brands Landschapsarchitecten. A new entrance was created at Rozenburglaan 5.

name: Kapel van Sint Josephs Gezellen-Vereeniging
en: The Kapel van Sint Josephs Gezellen-Vereeniging, within the Kolping network, was a church with an entrance at Stadhouderskade 55 in Amsterdam-Zuid, De Pijp. The Sint Jozef Gezellenvereniging has been an association of fellow believers since 1868, fighting for a better lot for workers in the footsteps of the priest Adolph Kolping of Cologne.

name: Karel I sigarenfabriek (Amsterdam)
en: The later Karel I cigar factory first had its base in Amsterdam. It was located on land that the municipality of Amsterdam had annexed in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel. The small factory was based at Wiegelstraat 3 from 1900.

name: Keizer Karelweg 259-281
en: The buildings Keizer Karelweg 259-281 and Keizer Karelweg 307-329 in Amstelveen have been municipal monuments since 2009. There are only two monuments on the long Keizer Karelweg (data 2020). They are basically two identical block-of-flats buildings from the period 1957 to 1960, designed by Willem Dudok and Robert Magnée.

name: Kerk aan Zee
en: De Kerk aan Zee is a late-Gothic church building from the 15th century in the North Holland village of Muiderberg. The church was built on the Kavelberg there.

name: Klederdracht Museum Amsterdam
en: The Klederdracht Museum Amsterdam on the Herengracht was a museum showing Dutch traditional costumes. The museum closed in 2020, during the Coronavirus pandemic, due to a lack of financial resources and too few visitors.

name: Knooppunt Schiphol-Noord
en: Knooppunt Schiphol-Noord is a bus station and an important hub for public bus transport at Schiphol-Noord.

name: Koninginneweg 176
en: Koninginneweg 176 is a building on the Koninginneweg in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Willemsparkweg and the Koninginneweg together form a long street that cuts through Amsterdam-Zuid, and together they form one of the city's arterial routes towards the Ringweg-West. That road came into being around 1885, when Amsterdam was extended westwards.

name: Kromme Distelstraat 17
en: Kromme Distelstraat 17 is a corner building on the Kromme Distelstraat and Distelkade in Amsterdam-Noord. The building, with influences of the Amsterdam School style, dates from 1919.

name: Lars Amsterdam (restaurant)
en: Lars Amsterdam is a restaurant in the Netherlands, which opened in September 2018. It received a star when the Michelin stars for 2022 were awarded.

name: Lauriergracht 122
en: Lauriergracht 122 is a house on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Leidsekade 68-69 (Amsterdam)
en: Leidsekade 68 and 69 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Leidseplein 28
en: Leidseplein 28/Leidsekade 97 in Amsterdam is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam-Centrum. From its completion it has been in use by the American Hotel.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 219
en: Lijnbaansgracht 219 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum that houses the Politiebureau Lijnbaansgracht police station. In the 1970s two police stations in the area around the Rembrandtplein and the Leidseplein were considered for replacement, but both became too small.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 244
en: Lijnbaansgracht 244 is a building on the Lijnbaansgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The almost square building is located on the corner of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Leidsekruisstraat.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 256-258
en: Lijnbaansgracht 256-258 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies along the Lijnbaansgracht, between the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen and the point where the quay of that square meets the Korte Leidsedwarsstraat. The building overlooks the rear façade of the Barlaeus Gymnasium, located at Weteringschans 29/Weteringschans 31.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 259-260
en: Lijnbaansgracht 259-260/Korte Leidsedwarsstraat, unnumbered, is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 279-280
en: Lijnbaansgracht 279-280 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It consists of a double house on the Lijnbaansgracht between the Spiegelpleintje and the Spiegelgracht.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 281
en: Lijnbaansgracht 281 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It consists of a residential and shop house on the Lijnbaansgracht between the Spiegelpleintje and the Spiegelgracht.

name: Linnaeushof 31-42 (Amsterdam)
en: Linnaeusstraat 31-42 in Amsterdam is a row of homes on the Linnaeushof in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Lutmastraat 271
en: Lutmastraat 271 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lutmastraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Lycka
en: Lycka is a building in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The fifty-metre-high building consists of workspaces with social-housing apartments above. It contains several types of apartment, which is reflected in the architecture: each type of home has its own character in both material and colour.

name: Marktpleinkerk (Hoofddorp)
en: The Marktpleinkerk is a Protestant church building on the corner of Marktplein and the Hoofdweg (East side) in the village of Hoofddorp in the Dutch province of North Holland. The church was built in 1927-1929 as a Gereformeerde Kerk to a design by architect Jos de Jonge (1887-1965). It replaced a church building on the Marktplein dating from 1879.

name: Marktzicht
en: Marktzicht is a municipal monument that has housed a hospitality business for more than 150 years in the Dutch village of Hoofddorp. It stands in the middle of the Haarlemmermeerpolder on the Marktplein, next to the Polderhuis, at the junction of the Hoofdweg and Kruisweg.

name: Marnixplein 2-2B
en: The building Marnixplein 2-2B is located on the Marnixplein in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies north of the connection via bridge 128 to the Westerstraat. On the site of number 2, the Marnixplein 2C-8M housing complex was built in 1875 and 1876.

name: Marnixstraat 214-220
en: Marnixstraat 214-220 is a complex of homes in Amsterdam-Centrum. Here the Marnixstraat forms the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht; the homes are separated from the water by tram tracks, cycle paths and the carriageway. At the end of the 19th century the fruit and vegetable market (appeltjesmarkt) was located in the area.

name: Marnixstraat 222-232
en: Marnixstraat 222-232 is a complex of homes in Amsterdam-Centrum. Here the Marnixstraat forms the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht; the homes are separated from the water by tram tracks, cycle paths and the carriageway.

name: Marnixstraat 307-315
en: Marnixstraat 307-315 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is connected by a footbridge to Marnixstraat 317. The building is wedged between the Marnixstraat, the extension of the Bloemgracht and the Lijnbaansgracht. Its rear façade stands directly on the water of the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Mata Hari (rijksmonument)
en: Mata Hari is a national monument on the Amsterdam Wallen. The complex consists of several interconnected buildings at Oudezijds Voorburgwal 27 and 29, and a building at Oudezijds Achterburgwal 20-22-24. The complex owes its name to a notorious illegal gambling house, which was established here from the early 1970s.

name: Mauritskade 56 (Amsterdam)
en: Mauritskade 56 is a building with an address on the Mauritskade in Amsterdam-Oost, but in essence it lies on the Oosterpark. As early as 1928 there were plans for a second open-air school for sick children. An earlier such school had already been built on the Frederiksstraat; that building bordered the Vondelpark.

name: Middenweg 460a (Amsterdam)
en: Middenweg 460a, Amsterdam is a building on the Middenweg in Amsterdam-Oost, Watergraafsmeer. The unassuming small building stands at the southern end of the Middenweg, just before the road passes under rijksweg 10. It stands together with an electricity cabin in a green strip between the Middenweg and its service road.

name: Molenpad 6-8
en: Molenpad 6-8 is a building on the Molenpad in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Mos (restaurant)
en: Mos is a restaurant in Amsterdam run by head chef Egon van Hoof and host Henry Pattiwael van Westerloo. The eatery has held a Michelin star since 2017.

name: Mulligans Irish Music Bar
en: Mulligans Irish Music Bar is a café on the Amstel 100 in Amsterdam. The business opened in 1988 and is comparable to O'Donoghue's in Dublin, Ireland. At this location there was originally the gay café De Komedie, which in 1988 was taken over by Miriam Feuth and an Irish construction worker who acted as her business partner.

name: Museumwoning Tuindorp Oostzaan
en: Museumwoning Tuindorp Oostzaan is a house from 1922 still in its original state, at Meteorenweg 174 in Amsterdam-Noord, which has been open to the public since 2002. At the time, the Gemeentelijke Woningdienst Amsterdam built around 1350 houses in Tuindorp Oostzaan as a temporary village for workers in the shipbuilding industry.

name: Museumwoning Van Eesteren
en: The Van Eesteren Museumwoning in Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West is a stairwell-access flat (portiekwoning) at Freek Oxstraat 27. It opened when the neighbourhood turned exactly 60 years old in October 2012. The Van Eesterenmuseum, together with housing corporation De Alliantie, restored the 1953 home to its original state.

name: Nederlands Hervormde Kerk (Hoogmade)
en: The Nederlands Hervormde Kerk is a church on the Kerkstraat in the South Holland village of Hoogmade, built in 1729 and 1730. Above the west façade the church has a wooden bell turret. The entrance is formed by a natural-stone gateway bearing the date 1729 and the arms of the then lord of the manor, Cornelis Sprongh.

name: New Amsterdam (gebouw)
en: New Amsterdam is a residential tower in Amsterdam on the Zuidas. It is part of the Mahler4 development. It comprises 24 residential floors, with a gross floor area of 42,435 m² including 174 rental apartments, 20 owner-occupied apartments and 3,500 m² of commercial space, of which the top four floors are penthouses.

name: New Kit
en: New Kit is an apartment complex in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The name refers to the Opstandingskerk, which because of its shape is known colloquially as the Kolenkit (coal scuttle). The building, with its pointed church tower, has formed an eye-catching landmark at the start of the Bos en Lommerweg, west of the Bos en Lommerplein, since its completion in 1956.

name: Nicolaas Witsenkade 32
en: Nicolaas Witsenkade 32 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nicolaas Witsenkade in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Nicolaas Witsenkade, between the Tweede Weteringsplantsoen and Westeinde, is the northern quay of the Singelgracht.

name: Nieuwe Looiersstraat 68-70
en: The building Nieuwe Looiersstraat 68-70 in Amsterdam is in Amsterdam-Centrum, Weteringbuurt. It dates from around 1940. The Nieuwe Looiersstraat shows a mixture of all kinds of architectural styles; over the years the original buildings disappeared, and the subsequent buildings did not all survive the passage of time either.

name: Nieuwe Nieuwstraat 22 (Amsterdam)
en: Nieuwe Nieuwstraat 22 is a building on the Nieuwe Nieuwstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat is a little street in Amsterdam already known from maps of 1599. The original buildings disappeared over the centuries, and in the 20th century too buildings were demolished and new ones built.

name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 59-achter
en: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 59-achter in Amsterdam is a relatively small building on the grounds of Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 57-59 in Amsterdam-Centrum. Both are municipal monuments.

name: Nijlpaardenhuis
en: The Nijlpaardenhuis is a building on the grounds of Artis in which the hippopotamuses were housed until 2009. After 2009 the building was renamed Gorillahuis, but within the architecture the old name Nijlpaardenhuis is retained.

name: Noorderparkbad
en: The Noorderparkbad is a swimming pool in Amsterdam, located on the edge of the Noorderpark. It comprises both an indoor section (binnenbad) and an outdoor area with swimming basins (openluchtbad). The indoor section was built in 2013-2015 alongside the Floraparkbad, which had opened in 1975.

name: Noordervermaning (Westzaan)
en: The Noordervermaning is a former Mennonite church in the North Holland village of Westzaan. Today it is a church building of the Gereformeerde Gemeenten. The largely wooden church building dates from 1695, making it the oldest church building of that denomination. In 1976 the building was recognised as a national monument.

name: Oval Tower
en: The Oval Tower, named after its oval shape, is located in the ArenA Boulevard area in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Since 2011 the building has been largely rented by Deutsche Bank.

name: Overtoom 13-17 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 13-17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. When the building was erected in 1890/1891 there was still plenty of commercial activity along the Overtoomse Vaart with its Vondelkade. At number 13-17, the timber merchant Firma A. had been established since the mid-1870s.

name: Overtoom 21-25 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 21-25 in Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom. It is somewhat known as Huize Vondel.

name: Overtoom 429-439 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 249-253, Amsterdam is a complex of buildings on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. It has wings extending into the Saxenburger- and Reyer Anslostraat.

name: Overtoom 447 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 447, Amsterdam is a double mansion on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West.

name: Parnassusweg 280
en: Parnassusweg 280 is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Rechtbank Amsterdam (Amsterdam District Court) had outgrown its offices on the Parnassusweg in Amsterdam (the Parnas complex). Moreover, one building had a layout that no longer suited the judicial practice then in use.

name: Pauluskerk (Amsterdam)
en: De Pauluskerk is the church building of the Roman Catholic Paulus parish on Pieter Calandlaan 194 in Amsterdam-Osdorp. The first plans for the Pauluskerk date from 1961, shortly after construction began on the Tuinstad Osdorp. Construction of the church started in 1966, and the building was completed on 4 November 1967.

name: Pepper (gebouw)
en: Pepper is a residential and shopping complex on the Haarlemmerweg in Amsterdam Oud-West. Here, in the 2010s, the redevelopment of an office park into a residential district began. On the narrow strip between the Haarlemmerweg on one side and the allotment gardens and Westerpark on the other, four residential towers were erected.

name: Polderhuis (Hoofddorp)
en: The Polderhuis is a building in Hoofddorp in the Dutch province of North Holland, where the water board of the Haarlemmermeerpolder was based. The architect was Foeke Kuipers.

name: Poldermolen Nederhorst den Berg
en: The Poldermolen Nederhorst ten Berg, in the Dutch municipality of Wijdemeren, drained the formerly Stichts-Ankeveense polder. There was originally a second mill for the polder, but it disappeared between 1863 and 1894. This mill remained in operation until around 1932. In 1956 the neglected mill was bought by the current owner and restored as a house.

name: Politiebureau Flierbosdreef
en: Politiebureau Flierbosdreef is a police station on the Flierbosdreef 15-17 in the Amsterdam-Zuidoost borough. It serves as the district and neighbourhood team office for the Regiopolitie Amsterdam-Amstelland.

name: Prinsengracht 551
en: Prinsengracht 551 is a building on the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Prinsengracht 571
en: Prinsengracht 571 in Amsterdam is a building on the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Prinsengracht 927
en: Prinsengracht 927 is a building on the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. On the opposite side of the canal stands the Maison Descartes. From 1882 up to and including 1884 the Elisabeth Wolffschool, a girls' school of the fourth class, was built here; that is, for girls from well-to-do families, as it was the most expensive class.

name: Raadhuis van Westzaan
en: The Raadhuis van Westzaan is a former courthouse ('t Reghthuys) and former town hall, built in 1781-1783. The design was by Johan Samuel Creutz, one of the directors of the municipal works of Amsterdam (stadsfabriek).

name: Raamstraat 9
en: Raamstraat 9 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of a national monument (4771).

name: Rapenburgerstraat 77-81
en: Rapenburgerstraat 77-81 in Amsterdam is a residential and work building on the Rapenburgerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is often combined with Rapenburgerstraat 93-97, the same complex.

name: Reguliersgracht 109
en: Reguliersgracht 109 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Reguliersgracht. It stands in the façade wall between the crossings with the Falckstraat and the Weteringschans.

name: Reinaert de Vosstraat 27
en: Reinaert de Vosstraat 27 is a building on the Reinaert de Vosstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West. Originally built as the Rooms Katholieke Horeca- en Brood- en Banketbakkersvakschool St. Hubertus (a Roman Catholic school for the hospitality and bread and pastry trades), it has housed the Islamic Cornelius Haga Lyceum since 2019.

name: Rembrandt Park One
en: Rembrandt Park One is a business centre in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. Until 2019 the building was known as Ringpark.

name: Remise Havenstraat
en: De Remise Havenstraat is a tram depot built by the Gemeentetram Amsterdam. The complex, the first section of which came into use in 1914, is located on the Havenstraat between the Haarlemmermeerstation and the Schinkel, south of the Vlietstraat.

name: ROC van Amsterdam
en: The ROC van Amsterdam (ROCvA), full name Regionaal Opleidingencentrum van Amsterdam, is a regional training centre for mbo, vmbo and adult education in Amsterdam and surrounding areas. The ROCvA offers education at nine mbo colleges in Amsterdam, Amstelveen, Hilversum and Hoofddorp. It offers more than 300 mbo courses.

name: Rozenstraat 183
en: Rozenstraat 183 in Amsterdam is a building on the Rozenstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Rozentheater
en: The Rozentheater is a theatre located at Rozengracht 117 in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Ruysdaelkade 43
en: The building Ruysdaelkade 43 consists of a mansion on the Ruysdaelkade in De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of the four municipal monuments on the quay, not counting the Moppesgebouw. The building is a striking presence on the Ruysdaelkade. The lower house numbers consist of tall, block-like residential buildings with fixed storey and building heights.

name: Saarein
en: Café Saarein is the oldest surviving women's café in Amsterdam, located since 1978 at Elandsstraat 119 in the Jordaan.

name: Lijnbaansgracht 211-218
en: The building complex Lijnbaansgracht 211-218/Passeerdersgracht 34-38 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Passeerdersgracht, at the corner of the Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat and the Passeerdersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Pakhuizen Serdang, Langkat en Deli
en: As a continuation of the warehouses in Amsterdam's inner city, various new warehouses rose near the IJ around 1900. All of them were converted into apartments by the end of the 20th century.

name: Poortgebouw van het Begijnhof (Amsterdam)
en: The gatehouse of the Begijnhof is a gatehouse from 1907 on the Spui in Amsterdam-Centrum that forms part of the Begijnhof. It has a floor area of about 70 m² and, including the storage attic, five storeys. It was built of brick, bluestone and sandstone. The passage has a barrel-vault construction that helps carry the dwellings above.

name: Raadhuis van Ransdorp
en: The town hall of Ransdorp is a national monument in the North Holland village of Ransdorp, in the municipality of Amsterdam. The building at Dorpsweg 59 was built in 1652 and served as the meeting place of the Waterlandse Unie and as the town hall of Ransdorp until 1811. It then functioned until 1921 as the town hall of the municipality of the same name.

name: Raadhuis van Weesperkarspel
en: The town hall of Weesperkarspel stood at Hoogstraat 24 and along the Vecht, with outbuildings at Kerkstraat 2-6 in Weesp. It was the town hall of the former North Holland municipality of Weesperkarspel from 1924 to 1966.

name: Telefooncentrale Amsterdam-Slotervaart
en: The Amsterdam-Slotervaart telephone exchange (abbreviation: Asd-Slov) is a telephone exchange in the Slotervaart district of the Dutch city of Amsterdam. The building was declared a municipal monument on 2 December 2008. The exchange, at Plesmanlaan 1 on the corner with Ottho Heldringstraat 1, dates from 1958-1960.

name: Theater Frascati
en: Frascati is a theatre in the centre of Amsterdam, which has two locations in the Nes: Frascati 1, 2 and 3, and Frascati 4.

name: Watertoren (Amsterdam Nieuwer-Amstel)
en: The water tower of Nieuwer-Amstel, which stood in Amsterdam after 1896, was designed by architects H.P.N. Halbertsma and Jan Verheul and was built in 1888. The tower was 40.00 metres high and had a water reservoir of 500 m³. It stood on the Amsteldijk, slightly south of the later Berlagebrug, and was demolished in 1928.

name: Watertoren (Amsterdam Spaklerweg)
en: The water tower of the Zuidergasfabriek on Spaklerweg in Amsterdam was built in 1911. It was constructed by contractor J.L. Seeuwen, who offered the lowest price at the tender in the autumn of 1910. He built a tower about 45.00 metres high, with a granite parapet and striking red brick above it.

name: Watertoren Amstelveenseweg
en: The water tower on Amstelveenseweg in Amsterdam-Zuid was designed by architect Piet Elling and built in 1965. It is 40 metres high and has a single water reservoir of 2335 m³. The reservoir is of steel, surrounded by an aluminium casing, so the tower is clearly visible in strong sunlight.

name: Dorpskerk (Abcoude)
en: The village church of Abcoude is a Protestant cruciform church in Gothic style in the Dutch town of Abcoude. It dates mainly from the 15th and 16th centuries, but the building's history goes back further. The church building is on the national monuments register.

name: Haci Bayram Moskee (Amsterdam)
en: The Haci Bayram Mosque is a mosque in the Nieuw-West borough of Amsterdam. It is housed in a former primary school building on the Osdorperweg 384-386. The mosque serves as an Islamic house of prayer and community centre for the local Muslim community, and also hosts various religious and social activities.

name: Kantoorgebouw Van Leer
en: The former office building of Van Leer's Vatenfabrieken lies on the Amsterdamseweg in Amstelveen. It was built in 1958 to a design by Marcel Breuer as the headquarters of the company Van Leer. The building, in the area of the former hofstede (farmstead) Elsrijk, lies in a green setting.

name: Reynders (café)
en: Reynders (also spelled Reijnders) is a café at Leidseplein 6 in Amsterdam. It is the oldest surviving café on this square and was particularly known in the 1950s and 1960s as an artists' café.

name: Sifon van het Merwedekanaal
en: The Merwedekanaal siphon is an underlevel, or water transport tunnel, which runs under the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal (ARK) and connects two branches of the Merwedekanaal on the southern edge of the city of Utrecht. The current siphon has existed since 1973 and replaced an older, steel crossing.

name: Sultan Ahmet Moskee (Zaandam)
en: The Sultan Ahmet Mosque is a mosque in the Poelenburg district of Zaandam. It was designed by Bedri Sevinçsoy of Mabeg Architecten in Utrecht. The design for the Sultan Ahmet mosque had been on the table since 1992. The client was the Islamitische Stichting Nederland, based in The Hague.

name: A'DAM Toren
en: The A'DAM Toren is a 100-metre tower on the IJ waterfront in Amsterdam-Noord. It was originally designed in 1966 as the Toren Overhoeks by the Dutch architect Arthur Staal for Koninklijke Shell, and it was therefore known for many years as the Shell-toren.

name: D'Admiraal
en: D'Admiraal is a chalk and trass mill on the Noordhollands Kanaal in Amsterdam (borough of Noord). It is the last surviving example of its type. Its baard bears the year 1792, and the achterbaard reads d'admiraal.

name: De 1100 Roe
en: De 1100 Roe is a polder mill in Amsterdam that formerly stood on the Haarlemmerweg. Its name is based on its distance in roede from the Haarlemmerpoort, almost four kilometres. The mill was built in 1674 after the Haarlemmertrekvaart was dug, and served to drain the Sloter and Middelveldsche Gecombineerde Polders.

name: De Bloem
en: De Bloem, or De Blom, is a gallery mill (stellingmolen) in Amsterdam-West on the Haarlemmerweg. The mill is also known as the 400 Roe, after its distance of 400 roede from the Haarlemmerpoort, roughly one and a half kilometres.

name: Hoek van 't IJ
en: The Hoek van 't IJ lighthouse is a monumental structure east of the village of Durgerdam in the Dutch province of North Holland.

name: Vondelparkpaviljoen
en: The Vondelparkpaviljoen (also known as VondelCS) is a building in the Vondelpark in Amsterdam. It was built in 1874-1881 by the architect W. Hamer in an Italian Renaissance style, with fluted Ionic half-columns, round-arched windows and domed turrets. Ten years after its opening, a reception hall and a bowling alley were added.

name: Breitnertoren
en: The Breitnertoren, officially the 'Breitner Center', is a skyscraper in Amsterdam named after the Dutch painter George Breitner. This office tower stands on the Amstelplein, on the de Omval business park, a headland in the Amstel, south of Amstel station.

name: Burgerweeshuis (Amsterdam, IJsbaanpad)
en: The former Burgerweeshuis (orphanage) on the IJsbaanpad in Amsterdam-Zuid was built in 1958-1960 by Aldo van Eyck and is the first example of Structuralism. Van Eyck gained considerable renown at home and abroad through it.

name: Carlton Hotel (Amsterdam)
en: NH Flower Market, better known as the Carltonhotel, is a four-star hotel that opened in 1928 at the start of the Vijzelstraat in central Amsterdam.

name: Centrale Diemen
en: The Vattenfall Nederland centrale Diemen is a complex of electricity power stations in the Dutch municipality of Diemen, where district heat is also produced for Almere and Diemen. The two units have a capacity of 684 MWe (megawatts electrical) and 615 MWth (megawatts thermal).

name: Chassékerk
en: The Chassékerk is the nickname of the former Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in Amsterdam. The name Baarsjeskerk, originally proposed after the chapel of ease in use from 1917 to 1926, was dropped fairly quickly.

name: Eerste Openluchtschool voor het Gezonde Kind
en: The Eerste Openluchtschool voor het Gezonde Kind, usually shortened to Openluchtschool, is a school building from 1930, designed by the Dutch architect Jan Duiker. The complex consists of a school building on an inner courtyard and a gatehouse on the Cliostraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Gebouw Batavia
en: Gebouw Batavia is a building on the Prins Hendrikkade in Amsterdam. It is a national monument.

name: Gemeenschapsmolen
en: The Gemeenschapsmolen on the Gaasp near Driemond is a polder mill dating from 1708. It was built to drain the Gemeenschapspolder. Originally fitted with a scoop wheel, the mill was converted to an Archimedes screw in 1892. In 1926 a pumping station was installed that took over the drainage, and the upper part of the mill was sawn off.

name: Kohnstammhuis
en: The Kohnstammhuis is a striking building in Amsterdam, on the Wibautstraat near the Rhijnspoorplein. It opened in 1958 to house the Dutch Tax Authority (Belastingdienst), which occupied it until 1994. It is now used by the Hogeschool van Amsterdam, which named the building after the physicist, philosopher and educator Philip Kohnstamm.

name: Olympiahuisje
en: The Olympiahuisje (the little house at Stadionplein 18), also called the Portiershuisje or Noordelijke Dienstwoning, is a former porter's lodge on the site in Amsterdam where the 1928 Olympic Games took place. During the Games it served as a post office. Like the Olympic Stadium, it was designed by the architect Jan Wils.

name: Schiphol Plaza
en: Schiphol Plaza (officially Shopping Centre Schiphol Plaza) is a shopping centre on the landside of Schiphol Airport, open to everyone. It forms the part of the arrivals hall after passport control, comprising the four sections Aankomst 1 to 4. The departures hall is one floor higher.

name: Sint-Josephkerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Sint-Josephkerk is a former Roman Catholic parish church on the Erik de Roodestraat in Amsterdam Bos en Lommer. The building was used as a church from 1952 to 1990. It was then used as a climbing hall from 1996 to 2012. After a period of vacancy, the building was squatted and became nationally known as De Vluchtkerk.

name: Sint-Urbanuskerk (Duivendrecht)
en: The Sint-Urbanuskerk is one of the two churches in Duivendrecht. The Roman Catholic church of Saint Urban was built in 1878 in Neo-Romanesque style to a design by the architect Theo Asseler, commissioned by the building pastor Laurent. The church was consecrated on 16 July 1879 by Mgr. Snickers, the Bishop of Haarlem.

name: Vrolikstraat 8
en: Vrolikstraat 8 is a building on the Vrolikstraat in Amsterdam-Oost. It dates from the post-war reconstruction period and was placed on a list of the 100 most valuable monuments from that period in 2007. It was also added to the national monuments register in 2009. Since 2013 the Cygnus Gymnasium has been based here.

name: Westereindflat
en: The Westereindflat is a residential block on the Harry Koningsbergerstraat in the Slotermeer district (part C) of the Amsterdam Nieuw-West borough. It was built in 1956-1958 to a design by the architects Jan Rietveld and Pieter Rinze Bloemsma, for the contractor Cornelis Balke (1894-1959).

name: 's-Gravesandeplein 19 (gebouw)
en: 's-Gravesandeplein 19 in Amsterdam is a building on the 's-Gravesandeplein in the Oosterpark neighbourhood of Amsterdam-Oost. It has been a municipal monument since 3 July 2012 (number 200639).

name: 't Haantje (Weesp)
en: 't Haantje is a former grain mill on the Stammerdijk beside the Smal Weesp, in the Dutch town of Weesp (province of North Holland).

name: 't Jagershuis
en: 't Jagershuis is a former hotel and restaurant at Amstelzijde 2-4, in the part of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel that belongs to the municipality of Amstelveen. The building stands on the western bank of the Amstel, at the southern entrance to the historic village buildings.

name: 12-verdiepingenhuis
en: The 12-verdiepingenhuis, better known by the nickname De Wolkenkrabber ('The Skyscraper'), is a residential building from 1932 by J.F. Staal. It stands in a central position in the Amsterdam Rivierenbuurt, in the Plan Zuid designed by Berlage.

name: 400 Beethoven
en: 400 Beethoven is an office building on the Beethovenstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built as part of the Gershwin development area in the Zuidas. The building stands on the corner of the Beethovenstraat and the Gustav Mahlerlaan, at the head of the George Gershwinlaan. At its highest point it has fourteen storeys, with a car park beneath.

name: 900 Mahler
en: 900 Mahler is a residential tower on the Gustav Mahlerlaan in the Zuidas district of Amsterdam. The building was designed by Inbo Architecten and forms part of cluster IV of the Gershwin complex. Its architecture is inspired by New York building styles.

name: A.H. Gerhardhuis
en: The A.H. Gerhardhuis on the Slotermeerlaan in the Amsterdam district of Slotermeer is named after the freethinker and humanist Adriaan Gerhard. The building is in the modernist style of the 1950s, to a design by the architect Willem van Tijen from 1959.

name: Aalsmeerder Veerhuis
en: The Aalsmeerder Veerhuis, also known as 'Herberg De Bonte Os', is a historic building from 1634 at Sloterkade 21-22, then still in the former municipality of Sloten and now in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of the last surviving houses of the former Overtoomse Buurt.

name: Accijnshuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Accijnshuis is a monumental 17th-century building on the Oudebrugsteeg in Amsterdam, on the corner of the Beursstraat. A café is now based here.

name: Admiraal De Ruijterweg 56
en: Admiraal De Ruijterweg 56 is a building on the Admiraal De Ruijterweg in Amsterdam-West. From 1908, the NV Drukkerij Senefelder had a new printing works built here, then still in the municipality of Sloten. The design was by the architects J.W.F. Hartkamp and P.H. van Niftrik, in the style of their colleague Berlage. It became a heavy industrial complex.

name: Akermolen
en: The Akermolen is a mill stump in the Middelveldsche Akerpolder in Amsterdam-Osdorp, a remnant of a polder mill. The mill lies on the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder.

name: Albert Cuypstraat 2-6
en: Albert Cuypstraat 2-6 is a building on the Albert Cuypstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of three municipal monuments on that street. It is locally known as the Moppesgebouw. From its completion until 2005, a diamond cutter and dealer was based here.

name: Albrecht Dürerstraat 10
en: Albrecht Dürerstraat 10 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of a municipal monument (200990).

name: Amstel 344
en: The Amstel 344 complex, at the corner of Sarphatistraat 15, is an office building in Amsterdam-Centrum where the Sarphatistraat crosses the Amstel by the Hogesluis. Two buildings stood here from the late 19th century: the private clinic of Arthur Maurits Mendes de Leon and the villa of Anne Willem van Eeghen (1860-1938).

name: Amstel Tower
en: The Amstel Tower is a skyscraper in Amsterdam-Oost. It consists of a 103-metre residential tower with 192 rental apartments and a lower six-storey block that houses Meininger Hotels.

name: Amsteldijk 273
en: Amsteldijk 273 in Amsterdam is a building on the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam-Zuid. The small building was erected as a service house for the Zorgvlied cemetery, then in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, under the address Utrechtsche Zijde.

name: Amsteldijk 35
en: Amsteldijk 35 in Amsterdam is a relatively large building on the Amsteldijk, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Amsteldijk 75-78
en: Amsteldijk 75-78 is a composite building on the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam.

name: Amsteldijk 83
en: Amsteldijk 83 in Amsterdam is a corner building on the Amsteldijk and the Lutmastraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Amsteldijk 86
en: Amsteldijk 86 in Amsterdam is a building on the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam-Zuid, in the Diamantbuurt. Here a cluster of urban development arose in the then largely agricultural municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel. That district was laid out and built up in the 1990s under the direction of Dolf van Gendt.

name: Amstelkerk (Ouderkerk aan de Amstel)
en: The Amstelkerk is a Protestant church in Ouderkerk aan de Amstel in the Dutch province of North Holland. It stands on the west side of Ouderkerk, on the River Amstel, by the Kerkbrug over the Bullewijk.

name: Amstelrust
en: Amstelrust has been a farmstead in Amsterdam at Amsteldijk 319, just south of the Rozenoordbrug, since the 17th century, and is a national monument. The Amstelrust entrance gate is separately listed as a national monument.

name: Amsterdam Symphony
en: Amsterdam Symphony is a development in the Zuidas district of Amsterdam comprising two striking orange-red skyscrapers. The 105-metre residential tower has 29 storeys and the 97-metre office tower has 27. Both were designed by the Dutch architect Pi de Bruijn.

name: Anjeliersstraat 157
en: Anjeliersstraat 157 in Amsterdam is a building on the Anjeliersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Anjeliersstraat 82
en: Anjeliersstraat 82 in Amsterdam is a structure on the Anjeliersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Anthonie van Dijckstraat 1
en: Anthonie van Dijckstraat 1 in Amsterdam is a school building with municipal monument status (222131).

name: Apollo House
en: Apollo House is an office building on the Apollolaan and the Stadionweg in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has been a national monument since 2004. Built in 1937-1939 to a design by Dirk Roosenburg as the head office of the Rijksverzekeringsbank (RVB), later renamed the Sociale Verzekeringsbank, which remained here until 1990.

name: Apollolaan 1 (Amsterdam)
en: Apollolaan 1 in Amsterdam is a building on the Apollolaan in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Apollolaan 171
en: Apollolaan 171 in Amsterdam is a building on the Apollolaan in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Apostolisch Genootschap Watergraafsmeer
en: The association building of the Apostolisch Genootschap Watergraafsmeer in Amsterdam dates from 1931 and has been a municipal monument since 1992. The architectural style is late Amsterdam School. The building was renovated in 1999 and has an unusual organ made up of two parts.

name: Aquariumgebouw
en: The Aquariumgebouw is an aquarium building at Artis zoo in Amsterdam. The national monument at Plantage Middenlaan 53 was built in 1881 by the architect G.B. Salm. Salm had designed many other buildings for Artis in earlier years, together with his son Abraham Salm. The facade is in the neoclassical style.

name: Argos (bar)
en: De Argos, also known as Argos Bar, was a gay bar in central Amsterdam. It opened in 1965 as a leather and cruising bar with a darkroom at Heintje Hoekssteeg 15, moving to Warmoesstraat 95 in 1979. The bar closed in 2015. It is regarded as the oldest leather bar in Europe.

name: Arie Kepplerhuis
en: The Arie Kepplerhuis is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuid, named after Arie Keppler.

name: Arminiuskerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Arminiuskerk, named after Jacobus Arminius, is a church building in Amsterdam-West, at the corner of the Antillenstraat and Postjeskade, house number 200. Built for the Remonstrant congregation, it opened in May 1957 to a design by Karel Sijmons, who has several churches to his name.

name: Augustanakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Augustanakerk, also called the Augustanahof (after the new functions the building now houses), is a Lutheran church building in the Amsterdam district of Bos en Lommer. The building dates from 1956 and was designed by the architect Ferdinand B.

name: Aula De Nieuwe Ooster
en: The Aula van De Nieuwe Ooster is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost, partly a national monument since 12 January 2004. Built in 1938-1939 to a design by Jan Leupen, it replaced an outdated aula by Adriaan Willem Weissman. Leupen designed it in the traditionalist style with help from the Dienst der Publieke Werken.

name: Avenhornstraat 41
en: Avenhornstraat 41 in Amsterdam is a building on the Avenhornstraat in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Baarsjesweg 136
en: Baarsjesweg 136 is a building on the Baarsjesweg and the Kostverlorenvaart in Amsterdam-West. It was designated a municipal monument (200678) on 17 September 2013.

name: Bachzaal
en: The Bachzaal is a medium-sized concert hall in Amsterdam-Zuid. The hall takes its name from the Bachstraat, where it is located. The architect Piet Vorkink (1878-1960) designed the ingenious complex of which the Bachzaal forms part, in 1930.

name: Bananenbar
en: The Bananenbar is an erotic entertainment venue in De Wallen, Amsterdam. It occupies an 18th-century building on the Oudezijds Achterburgwal that is listed in the national monuments register. It was previously the so-called Boudoir of the Satanskerk.

name: Barcelona (gebouw)
en: Woongebouw Barcelona, also known as the Albertcomplex, Bruno Albert or Barcelonaplein, is an apartment building on the KNSM island in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Berghaus Plaza
en: Berghaus Plaza (also known as Berghaus) is a building on the Koningin Wilhelminaplein and the Elizabeth Anscombestraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Bethlehemkerk (Amsterdam)
en: Zwanenplein 34-36 in Amsterdam-Noord is a structure on the Zwanenplein. For many years it housed the Bethlehemkerk.

name: Bijlmersportcentrum
en: The Bijlmersportcentrum, completed in 2008, is an important part of the large-scale transformation of the Bijlmer centre and the neighbouring F-buurt in Amsterdam. This development aimed to improve the living environment in the area.

name: Billardfabriek Wilhelmina
en: Billardfabriek Wilhelmina was one of the oldest billiard table factories in the Netherlands, dating from the early 20th century.

name: Blankenstraat 2
en: Blankenstraat 2, locally known as De Engel, is a neighbourhood building on the corner of the Blankenstraat and Tweede Coehoornstraat in the Oostelijke Eilanden district of Amsterdam-Centrum. An oil factory of NV Godol stood on the site and was hit by a fire as late as 1938.

name: Blauwburgwal 15
en: Blauwburgwal 15 in Amsterdam is a building on the Blauwburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum. Buildings have stood on the site for centuries. The Blauwburgwal already existed in the late 16th century, but the house that received the address Blauwburgwal 15 is much younger.

name: Blauwburgwal 22
en: Blauwburgwal 22 is a canal house with its front facade on the Blauwburgwal and its side facade on the Herengracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Bloemgracht 56
en: Bloemgracht 56 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of a national monument (555).

name: Bloemgrachtkerk
en: Bloemgracht 98 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of a national monument (518325). It is known as the Bloemgrachtkerk, but no longer has any church function.

name: Bloemstraat 129-145
en: Bloemstraat 129-145 in Amsterdam is a building on the Bloemstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Bloemstraat 189
en: Bloemstraat 189 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of a national monument (598).

name: Bloemstraat 47-57
en: Bloemstraat 47-57 is a building on the Bloemstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Boekhuis
en: The Boekhuis, also known as the Boek, is a large office building on the Kingsfordweg, near Sloterdijk station. Designed by Abe Bonnema for Reed Elsevier, it takes the form of an open book. It is 85 metres high and has 20 storeys.

name: Boerhaaveplein 4-6
en: Boerhaaveplein 4-6 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam-Oost. The firm Wild & Hardebeck and/or Gordijnenfabriek Hardebeck and/or N.V. Hardebeck's Gordijnenfabriek had a factory building erected here on the Boerhaaveplein around 1921.

name: Boezemgemaal Halfweg
en: The Boezemgemaal Halfweg is a pumping station in the municipality of Amsterdam, in the Amsterdam Nieuw-West borough.

name: BorzoGallery
en: BorzoGallery, on the Keizersgracht in Amsterdam, specialises in modern and contemporary art, notably Nul, ZERO, minimalism and conceptual art. Jan Schoonhoven, Ben Akkerman, Jan Henderikse, Herman de Vries, Ad Dekkers, Carel Visser and Ger van Elk are represented in its collection.

name: Botenhuis Nereus
en: The Botenhuis van Nereus is a building on the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam belonging to the student rowing club ASR Nereus. It stands on the River Amstel and serves as the boathouse and clubhouse of the club. The upper floor houses a caretaker's flat.

name: BovenIJ Ziekenhuis
en: The BovenIJ Ziekenhuis is a medium-sized hospital in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Brouwersgracht 51 (Amsterdam)
en: Brouwersgracht 51 in Amsterdam is a house on the Brouwersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Brouwersgracht is a centuries-old canal. Much of its original building stock has disappeared, including the building that stood at number 51, which was built at the request of J.J.F.

name: Brouwersgracht 76 (Amsterdam)
en: Brouwersgracht 76 in Amsterdam is a canal house on the Brouwersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument since 14 April 1970.

name: Buiten Vissersstraat 4
en: Buiten Vissersstraat 4 in Amsterdam is a building on the Buiten Vissersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a municipal monument since 5 September 2006. The street is centuries old, appearing on maps from around 1600, but all the original buildings have gone. Only two buildings remain on the even side: this one and number 6-8.

name: Buitengasthuis (Amsterdam)
en: The Buitengasthuis was a gasthuis (an early type of hospital) near the Overtoomse Vaart in Amsterdam, close to the later Wilhelmina Gasthuis. The gasthuis played an important role in the development of nursing in the Netherlands.

name: Burcht van Berlage
en: The Burcht van Berlage is the oldest trade union building in the Netherlands. Hendrik Petrus Berlage designed it for the Algemene Nederlandse Diamantbewerkersbond (ANDB) in 1899-1900. It stood in the garden of the Plantage Schouwburg, close to Artis.

name: Burgemeester Eliasstraat 72-74
en: The building at Burgemeester Eliasstraat 72-74 in Amsterdam-Slotermeer has been a municipal monument since 2011. In 1954 a new Sint-Catharinakerk was built on this site, after the old church was demolished in 1939. It was completed to a design by the firm Evers en Sarlemijn.

name: Burgemeester Röellstraat 199
en: Burgemeester Röellstraat 199 in Amsterdam is a building on the Burgemeester Röellstraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. Since 1991 it has been in use as a chapel.

name: Cabralstraat 1
en: The Cabralstraat 1/Marco Polostraat 191 complex in Amsterdam-West is also known as De Wissel. It was built as a double primary school for children of the Marco Polobuurt (Mercatorbuurt), a neighbourhood built here in the 1920s.

name: Café De Engelbewaarder
en: De Engelbewaarder is a brown café in Amsterdam, on the first floor of the building at Kloveniersburgwal 59, which is a national monument. The café, originally named Het Amsterdamsch litterair café De Engelbewaarder, is named after W.F. Hermans's novel Herinneringen van een Engelbewaarder.

name: Candida (Amsterdam)
en: Candida is an office building in Amsterdam, between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Spuistraat. The ten-storey building was completed in 1931-32 to a Cubist-Expressionist design by F.A. Warners for the N.V. Amsterdamsche Maatschappij tot Exploitatie van Etagewoningen.

name: Cartesius Lyceum
en: The Cartesius Lyceum is a secondary school offering havo and vwo education in Amsterdam. It is named after the French philosopher Cartesius (Descartes). Its motto, Cogito ergo sum ('I think, therefore I am'), was also adopted by the school. It is part of the Esprit Scholengroep.

name: Cheider
en: Joodse Kindergemeenschap Cheider is an Orthodox Jewish school for primary and secondary education in the Amsterdam district of Buitenveldert. It is the only Orthodox Jewish school in the Netherlands. Boys and girls are taught separately, in separate classes within one school.

name: Cineac (Amsterdam)
en: The Cineac in Amsterdam was a Cineac cinema where the newsreel was shown. Cineac Amsterdam was located on the Reguliersbreestraat opposite Theater Tuschinski, and was conveniently called Cineac Reguliersbreestraat.

name: Cinema Parisien
en: Cinema Parisien, a former cinema at Nieuwendijk 69 in Amsterdam, was founded on 26 March 1910. Jean Desmet was its director from 1910 to 1956, and it ran until 25 March 1987. It was Desmet's second cinema, after the Parisien in Rotterdam, founded in 1909.

name: Circa Amsterdam
en: Circa Amsterdam, known as Amsterdome between 2018 and 2023, is a congress centre with room for 2,500 visitors on the Seineweg, near the Basisweg in Amsterdam-Westpoort. Its former name combined Amsterdam with Aviodome, the Dutch aviation and space museum that occupied the building from 1971 to 2003.

name: City of Wesopa
en: City of Wesopa is a medium-sized cinema and theatre complex in the North Holland town of Weesp. The building has the status of a municipal monument.

name: Clematisstraat 25
en: Clematisstraat 25 is a building on the Clematisstraat in Amsterdam-Noord. A church of the Hersteld Apostolische Zendinggemeente (HAZEA) rose here around 1934, taken over in 1951 by the Apostolisch Genootschap. The Apostolisch Genootschap prefers to call it a place of assembly.

name: Commelinstraat 31-37
en: Commelinstraat 31-37 in Amsterdam is a group of plots on the Commelinstraat in the Dapperbuurt, Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Complex Zwanenburgwal
en: The Complex Zwanenburgwal is a relatively new complex on the corner of the Zwanenburgwal 218-230, Staalstraat 17 and 21 and Ververstraat 149-157 in Amsterdam-Centrum. The corner has been built on for centuries, since the Zwanenburgwal was dug as a canal in the early 17th century.

name: Concordia (Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal)
en: Concordia is a building on the corner of the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the St. Luciënsteeg in Amsterdam. It dates from 1859 and was substantially remodelled in 1901. It is now used as office and residential space. Concordia has the status of a national monument.

name: Condomerie
en: De Condomerie, formerly Condomerie 'Het Gulden Vlies', is a specialist shop in central Amsterdam selling only condoms. The shop, which is also linked to an online shop, a wholesale business and its own foundation, has been based on the Warmoesstraat since 1987.

name: Coöperatiehof 16
en: Coöperatiehof 16 in Amsterdam is a separate structure within the Coöperatiehof in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Corantijnschool
en: The Corantijnschool, or Corantijn, is a school building at Corantijnstraat 2-4 in Amsterdam-West. The school was initiated by the municipality of Sloten in 1921, which was absorbed by Amsterdam soon after. This double, symmetrical building, completed in 1923, housed the Corantijnschool and the Hoofdwegschool.

name: Corned beef (Feldbrugge)
en: Corned beef is an artwork by Carolien Feldbrugge. It was installed in 1989 on the Hildo Kropplein, which had been named in 1988. For a century the surrounding area served as Amsterdam's cattle market and central abattoir. Veemarkt and Slachthuisbrug still recall that use.

name: Cruquiusweg 67
en: Cruquiusweg 67 in Amsterdam is a composite building on the Cruquiusweg in the Oostelijk Havengebied of Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Crystal Court
en: Crystal Court is an apartment complex in Buitenveldert, Amsterdam-Zuid, at the end of the Willem van Weldammelaan. Hillen & Roosen, as developer and builder, was permitted to build a luxury complex near the Gelderlandplein shopping centre.

name: Damrak 70-79
en: Damrak 70-79 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum, where urban buildings had stood for centuries. Around 1900 Hendrik Petrus Berlage designed a building here for the Algemeene Maatschappij van Levensverzekering en Lijfrente. It housed offices above and shops at street level.

name: De Ark (Slotervaart)
en: De Ark is a church building in the Slotervaart district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The church was built in 1960-61 to a design by the architect Piet Zanstra. It has been on the municipal monuments list since 2008 and in the Top 100 of young monuments of Amsterdam. In 1958 the Slotervaart and Overtoomse Veld area fell under the Hervormde Gemeente Sloten N.H.

name: De Bijenkorf (Amsterdam)
en: De Bijenkorf in Amsterdam is a branch of the De Bijenkorf department store chain. The Amsterdam Bijenkorf is the chain's head store and, at 20,000 square metres, also its largest branch. The main entrance is on the Dam; secondary entrances are on the Damrak and the Beursplein.

name: De Blokhut (tankstation)
en: De Blokhut is a national monument petrol station in Diemen. De Blokhut is the oldest petrol station still in use in the Netherlands.

name: De Cuserstraat 3
en: De Cuserstraat 3 in Amsterdam is a building that was designated a national monument in 2014. It stands on the De Cuserstraat at the corner of the Buitenveldertselaan. Marius Duintjer and Dick van der Klei designed the angular building; Charles Karsten designed the 'kletsmuurtjes'.

name: De Dageraad (Amsterdam)
en: De Dageraad is a housing complex in Amsterdam-Zuid. It lies on both sides of the P.L. Takstraat and is one of the aesthetic highlights of the Amsterdam School. In 1920 the socialist housing association 'De Dageraad' commissioned Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer to build 294 homes and six shops.

name: De Drie Traancoopers
en: The building De Drie Traancoopers is a national monument corner property at Herengracht 77 and Korsjespoortsteeg 24 in central Amsterdam.

name: De Eendragt (Weesp)
en: De Eendragt is a windmill built in 1691 as a malt mill, at Utrechtseweg 13 beside the Utrechtse Vecht, in the Dutch municipality of Amsterdam (Weesp district). The mill is an octagonal grain mill of the stellingmolen type, with a stone base and a timber, reed-thatched upper section.

name: De Gooyse Boer
en: De Gooyse Boer is a monumental building at Herengracht 71 in the North Holland town of Muiden. The building is recognised as a national monument and houses a café, 'Ome Ko'.

name: De Gulden Steur
en: De Gulden Steur was a mansion built in 1601 in Amsterdam, which had to make way for the Poppenhuis in 1642. Built for Joan Poppen, it stands on the Kloveniersburgwal as a national monument. It was entered in the Monumentenregister on 25 June 1970.

name: De Hoop (Amsterdam)
en: De Hoop is a canal house and national monument at Keizersgracht 209 in central Amsterdam. A statue atop the balustrade of the façade was made possible by Ignatius van Logteren. The building, together with the houses at numbers 211 and 213, was built in 1619.

name: De Hoop (schuilkerk)
en: De Hoop is the name of a former clandestine church (schuilkerk) in Diemen, in the part that was formerly called Diemerbrug.

name: De Kandelaar (Amsterdam Nieuw-West)
en: De Kandelaar is a church building in Amsterdam, in the Nieuw-West borough, in the Slotermeer district. It stands on the Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan, between the Burgemeester Fockstraat and the Johan Herman Doornstraat. It was built to a design by the architect Geert Kliphuis.

name: De Kroon (Amsterdam)
en: De Kroon is a building in Amsterdam at Rembrandtplein 17. It has stood there since 1898 and is best known as a hospitality venue.

name: De Laurierboom (café)
en: De Laurierboom is a café in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam, at Laurierstraat 76, on the corner of the Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat. It is best known as a chess café, but other games are also played there, such as poker, klaverjassen, toepen and backgammon.

name: De Lellebel
en: De Lellebel is a café in Amsterdam known for drag performances. It opened in 1997 and is located at Utrechtsestraat 4, just around the corner from the Rembrandtplein.

name: De Nieuwe Meester
en: De Nieuwe Meester is an apartment complex built in 2019 and 2020 in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: De Opgang (Amsterdam)
en: De Opgang is a Protestant church building in an apartment complex in the Osdorp district of Amsterdam. It stands in a central spot in Osdorp, on the Tussen Meer. The first De Opgang church building was built here in 1967 for the Gereformeerde Kerk Slotervaart/Osdorp.

name: De Piramides
en: De Piramides is a building complex in Amsterdam's West borough, next to the Marcanti College and opposite Food Center Amsterdam (the former Centrale Markthallen). Its address is Jan van Galenstraat 1-29 and Marcantilaan 496-500. It consists of two pyramid-shaped apartment blocks of 55 metres, fitted into each other.

name: De Sollenburg
en: De Sollenburg was the name of a gunpowder mill in Amsterdam. It was driven by a horse mill (rosmolen).

name: De spreeuwen
en: De spreeuwen is a building and artistic work in the Houthavens district of Amsterdam-West.

name: De Standaard (Amsterdam)
en: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 56 in Amsterdam is a building on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum, running through to the Spuistraat behind it. The building is nicknamed De Standaard.

name: De Uitweg
en: De Uitweg was a Dutch Reformed church on the Tussen Meer, on the corner of the Baden Powellweg in Amsterdam-Osdorp. It was named after the Uitweg that led here onto the Osdorperweg before Osdorp was built. Around 1960 the building of Tuinstad Osdorp created a need for a church of its own.

name: De Vechthoeve
en: De Vechthoeve, locally also known as the Pippi Langkoushuis, is a former farmhouse in Muiden, North Holland, on the Vecht. The building was moved in 2013 and has been in use as a childcare centre since 2026.

name: De Vervanger
en: De Vervanger (also known as 'Verrevanger') was a windmill built in 1688 that stood on the bastion De Bocht in Amsterdam.

name: De Volharding (Artis)
en: De Volharding is a museum building opened in 1888 in Artis zoo in Amsterdam, designed by the architect Dolf van Gendt to house the ethnographic museum. The ethnographic museum had been housed in the 'Sociëteit Amicitiae', the 'Kleine Museum'.

name: De voortuinen
en: De voortuinen is a housing complex on the Haarlemmerweg in Amsterdam-West.

name: De Zwarte Ruiter (molen)
en: De Zwarte Ruiter is a former grain mill at Mr. Jac. Takkade 10 in the Dutch municipality of Aalsmeer, now in use as a house.

name: Diamantbeurs (Amsterdam)
en: The Diamantbeurs is a former diamond exchange on the Weesperplein, at the corner of the Nieuwe Achtergracht, in Amsterdam.

name: Diamantslijperij Boas
en: Diamantslijperij Boas, also called Diamantslijperij Gebroeders Boas, was a diamond cutting works located at Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 173-175 in Amsterdam.

name: Diamantstraat 134
en: Diamantstraat 134 in Amsterdam is a building on the Diamantstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Dienstwoningen De Nieuwe Ooster
en: De Dienstwoningen De Nieuwe Ooster is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost and has been a national monument since 31 October 2003. It housed the gravediggers of the cemetery De Nieuwe Ooster, opened in 1894. The structure consists of three linked houses directly beside the main entrance.

name: Dijksgracht 2
en: Dijksgracht 2 in Amsterdam is a building on the Dijksgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a striking presence within the architecture of the city centre. The building appears to have sunk on one side into Amsterdam's soft ground.

name: Dijsselhofplantsoen 10
en: Dijsselhofplantsoen 10 is a villa on the Dijsselhofplantsoen in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Dikker & Thijs
en: Dikker & Thijs is a hotel on the corner of the Prinsengracht and the Leidsestraat in the Dutch capital, Amsterdam. The hotel was previously home to a delicatessen and a top restaurant. The building it occupies is a national monument.

name: Doelenzaal
en: The Doelenzaal was housed in a building at Kloveniersburgwal 87-89 in Amsterdam. The building was erected in 1883 to replace the Blauw Jan menagerie, to a design by L. Beirer and J.J.

name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 12
en: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 12 is a building in Holysloot, Landelijk Noord, Amsterdam-Noord. The area around Holysloot was, and for centuries has been, agricultural land. With the administrative merger with Ransdorp, it came under that municipality. Ransdorp itself was one of the villages in an extensive green area.

name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 37
en: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 37 is a building in Holysloot, Landelijk Noord, Amsterdam-Noord. The Dorpsstraat only received its name in 1957; in 1959 the building was given its present address, before which it was designated Ransdorp C24.

name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 38-40
en: Dorpsstraat Holysloot 38-40 is a building in the residential centre of Holysloot, Landelijk Noord, Amsterdam-Noord. Until 1959 its address was Ransdorp C8 and C9.

name: Dr. Baumannplein 1-3
en: Dr. Baumannplein 1-3 is a building on the north side of the square, with a rear facade on the Dubbele Buurt, in the Dutch town of Halfweg (province of North Holland). It is a municipal monument. It is also known as the 'Huis ter Hart'.

name: Dr. Sarphatihuis
en: The Dr. Sarphatihuis, a nursing home on the Roetersstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum, is named after the 19th-century physician Samuel Sarphati. The building has been a national monument since 23 September 1970, registered under number 4983. It lies beside the former Wittenberg nursing home.

name: Dreesmann-museum
en: The Dreesmann-museum was a museum that displayed the Amsterdamica collection of Willem Dreesmann (1885-1954). The museum was housed in a villa dating from 1911 on the Johannes Vermeerstraat, which before the Second World War had served as the Dreesmann family home.

name: Droogbak (gebouw)
en: De Droogbak is a 19th-century office building in Neo-Renaissance style in Amsterdam, designated a national monument in 2001. It stands west of Centraal Station on the street of the same name, the Droogbak, beside the railway line.

name: Droogbak 13
en: Droogbak 13 in Amsterdam is a building on the Droogbak in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument since 11 December 2001.

name: Droogbak 1CD
en: Droogbak 1CD in Amsterdam is a building on the Droogbak street in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 115-119
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 115-119 in Amsterdam comprises three shared-stairwell houses (portiekwoningen) on the Eerste Helmersstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West. Houses of this type were built one after another as the street was developed, occasionally alternating with a block of several, as at Eerste Helmersstraat 69-83.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 17
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 17-19 in Amsterdam is a building on the Eerste Helmersstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West. A growing Amsterdam needed a new premises for the Geneeskundige en Gezondheidsdienst (Medical and Health Service).

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 208
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 208 in Amsterdam is a building on the Eerste Helmersstraat in Amsterdam-West.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 21
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 21 is a building on the Eerste Helmersstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West. It was designated a municipal monument on 14 April 2009. It was built in 1924 as a substation for the Gemeente-Energiebedrijf Amsterdam, then still abbreviated as GE.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 263-269
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 263-269 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam Oud-West. The largely symmetrical building was built around 1910 for Reformed education, to a design by Huibertus Bonda.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 271
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 271 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam Oud-West. Tendering for it, as a school, took place on 15 November 1909. The Amsterdam municipality described it as follows: 'A public school for U.L.O.'

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 69-83
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 69-83 in Amsterdam comprises a number of shared-stairwell houses on the Eerste Helmersstraat in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat 59
en: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat 59 is a building on the Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is the only municipal monument in that street, which is otherwise quite short. The building was designed by Publieke Werken, the public works department of the city of Amsterdam. The architect may have been Jacobus van Niftrik.

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 20
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 20 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3189).

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 23
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 23 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3186).

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 3
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 3 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3184).

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 5
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 5 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3185).

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 50
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 50 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3198).

name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 91
en: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 91 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (3187). Until 1989 it was registered as Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat 29.

name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 13
en: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 13 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (5057).

name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 15
en: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 15 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (5058).

name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 5
en: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat 5 in Amsterdam is a building with the status of national monument (5055).

name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat 74-76
en: Eerste Van Swindenstraat 74-76 in Amsterdam is a building on the Eerste van Swindenstraat, Dapperbuurt, Amsterdam-Oost. Original buildings dating from 1892, designed by E.F. Kruger, stood here. Judging by the construction drawings, they were shop premises with back rooms and residential floors.

name: Effectenkantoor Oudhof
en: The former headquarters of Effectenkantoor Oudhof at Rokin 99 is a building on the Rokin in Amsterdam-Centrum. Although dating from 1990, it was already designated a municipal monument in 2016, one of the youngest monuments ever.

name: Egoli-toren
en: The Egoli-toren (working title Nieuw-Echtenstein) is an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. During construction the building was named after the honeycomb block Echtenstein, which stands directly next to Nieuw-Echtenstein.

name: Eikenplein 1-5
en: Eikenplein 1-5 in Amsterdam is a building covering the whole square at the Eikenplein in Amsterdam-Oost. It was designated a municipal monument on 17 December 2013. In urban planning terms it is the counterpart of Eikenplein 2-22, built in 1911 by the Elisabeth Otter-Knoll Stichting; only two buildings stand on the square.

name: Eilandskerk
en: The Eilandskerk was a Dutch Reformed church building in Amsterdam, located on the Bickerseiland.

name: Eindgemaal Rivierenbuurt
en: The Eindgemaal Rivierenbuurt is a sewage pumping station on the President Kennedylaan in Amsterdam-Zuid. The building was completed in December 2020. The pumping station collects and pumps wastewater from the neighbourhood towards the RWZI Amsterdam West wastewater treatment plant.

name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat 2
en: Elisabeth Wolffstraat 2 and Tweede Kostverlorenkade 5 in Amsterdam-West is a building at the junction of the Elisabeth Wolffstraat and the Tweede Kostverlorenkade, part of the quay of the Kostverlorenvaart.

name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat-Van Alphenstraat
en: Elisabeth Wolffstraat 47-55 and Van Alphenstraat 6-8 is a corner building on the Elisabeth Wolffstraat and the Van Alphenstraat in Amsterdam-West.

name: Emerald Empire
en: Emerald Empire, also known as Venetiëhof, is an apartment complex on the KNSM-eiland in Amsterdam-Oost. It consists of a round residential building surrounded by a ring of waterside villas, built in 1996-97 to a design by Jo Coenen.

name: Emmakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Emmakerk, since 1999 a merger of two church communities as Kerkelijk Centrum De Bron, is a building in Amsterdam-Oost. The church is dedicated to Emma of Waldeck-Pyrmont.

name: Europarking
en: Europarking is a car park at Marnixstraat 250 in Amsterdam. The building has seven storeys with 700 parking spaces in total and was designed by the Dutch architect Piet Zanstra. Because of its spiral ramps it has been nicknamed “de billen van Zanstra” (Zanstra's buttocks).

name: Ferdinand Bolstraat 8
en: Ferdinand Bolstraat 8 is a building on the Ferdinand Bolstraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is the only municipal monument in that street (number 8E not counted). It was built to a design by the Public Works Department in Amsterdam. From its completion it housed fire station “F” and a police station.

name: Flesseman
en: Flesseman, the main building at Nieuwmarkt 75-249 in Amsterdam, is a building on the Nieuwmarkt in the Dutch capital Amsterdam. It is named after the merchant Isaac Levie Flesseman.

name: Flevopark 11-12
en: Flevopark 11 and 12, Amsterdam, are a number of small buildings in the Flevopark, Amsterdam-Oost. Seven numbered buildings stand in the park, including Flevopark 13, the former pumping station building. While almost everything is known about building 13, this is not true of the three wooden huts that go by numbers 11 and 12.

name: Flevopark 13
en: Flevopark 13 in Amsterdam is a building in the Flevopark, Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the seven buildings in the park with an address. Since about 1631 the Oetewalermolen stood here, a wind and water mill with a scoop-wheel mill.

name: Fons Vitae Lyceum
en: The Fons Vitae Lyceum is a secondary school in Amsterdam.

name: Fort Bijlmer
en: Fort Bijlmer (also Fort Duivendrecht, officially Fort in den Laander- en Westbijlmerpolder) was built in 1868 as a military fortification to protect the capital Amsterdam. It formed part of the Ouderkerk military sector of the so-called Posten van Krayenhoff, a precursor of the later Stelling van Amsterdam.

name: Frederik Hendrikstraat 200-220
en: Frederik Hendrikstraat 200-220 in Amsterdam is a complex of dwellings on the corner of the Frederik Hendrikstraat and the Hugo de Grootgracht (quay) in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Gabriël Metsustraat 16
en: Gabriël Metsustraat 16 in Amsterdam is a building on the Gabriël Metsustraat, Museumkwartier, Amsterdam Oud-Zuid. The street, which received its name in 1899, was built up over the following decade, in effect plot by plot.

name: Gabriël Metsustraat 2-6
en: De Gabriël Metsustraat 2-6 in Amsterdam is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam-Zuid, Museumkwartier.

name: Gabriël Metsustraat 7
en: Gabriël Metsustraat 7 in Amsterdam is a detached building dating from 1911 on the Gabriël Metsustraat, Museumkwartier, in Amsterdam-Zuid. It stands between the American embassy on the Museumplein and the entrance to the Van Miereveldstraat.

name: GAK-gebouw (Amsterdam)
en: The GAK building is a former office building on the Bos en Lommerplantsoen in Amsterdam-West. It was built for the Gemeenschappelijk Administratiekantoor (GAK), which moved in during 1960 and left the building in 2005. Colloquially, however, it is still known by the name of its first user.

name: Garage West
en: Garage West is a garage built for and used by the GVB at Jan Tooropstraat 647 in Amsterdam-West. The complex, the first part of which came into use in November 1956, lies between the Jan Evertsenstraat, Jan van Galenstraat and the Ringspoorbaan in the Overtoomse Veld, Amsterdam-West.

name: Gebouw Industria
en: Gebouw Industria is a club building dating from 1916 in the Dutch capital Amsterdam. It stands on the south-east side of the Dam, on the corner of the Rokin (address: Dam 25).

name: Gebouw Kosmos
en: Het Gebouw Kosmos stands at Koningsplein 1 in Amsterdam's city centre. It occupies the corner of the Singel (by the Bloemenmarkt) and the Koningsplein (in line with the Leidsestraat), a busy site in the middle of the Stadslus. The building originally housed the life insurance company Kosmos.

name: Gebouw Mercurius
en: The Gebouw Mercurius (also called the Mercurius Gebouw) is a monumental 19th-century building at Prins Hendrikkade 20-21 in Amsterdam. It is a national monument (no. 518505) and has entrances on both the Prins Hendrikkade and the Nieuwendijk.

name: Gebouw Vivaldi
en: Gebouw Vivaldi is a building in Amsterdam-Zuid. It dates from 1967/1968 and was designed by Peter de Clercq Zubli and Piet Zanstra (Bureau Zanstra, Ab Gmelig Meyling & De Clercq Zubli). The former office and warehouse of Philips-Duphar Nederland NV and Phonogram Records was built at Drentestraat 11.

name: Gemaal De Lynden
en: The Gemaal Lynden, also known as De Lynden, in the village of the same name, Lijnden, is a pumping station in the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Gemaal Schipholdijk
en: The Gemaal Schipholdijk is a polder pumping station on the western edge of the Amsterdamse Bos. In 1939 the municipality of Amsterdam released 75,000 guilders for a new pumping station for the Rietwijkeroorderpolder. The old one no longer sufficed and had to be adapted, but it proved cheaper to build a new pumping station with a machinist's house.

name: Gemaal Stadwijck
en: The Gemaal Stadwijck is a polder pumping station dating from 1921, on the Amsteldijk and the Kleine Wetering in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is named after the farmstead Stadwyck that stood here and was demolished in 1915-'16 on the orders of the municipality of Amsterdam. Stadwijck replaced the old steam pumping station that stood where the Meerhuizenstraat now runs.

name: Gemaal Zeeburg
en: The Gemaal Zeeburg is a pumping station that lifts water from the Lozingskanaal, part of Amsterdam's stadsboezem (urban water-retention system), up to a Voorboezem. From there it is discharged into the IJmeer through the Syphonsluis, an underflow passing beneath the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal.

name: Gemeentebadhuis aan de Polanenstraat/Zaanstraat
en: The Gemeentebadhuis aan de Polanenstraat/Zaanstraat is a former public bath house in Amsterdam.

name: Gerard Doustraat 220
en: Gerard Doustraat 220 is a building on the Gerard Doustraat in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It is one of five municipal monuments in that street. The building was designed by Publieke Werken, the public works department of the city of Amsterdam.

name: Goslerhuisje
en: The Goslerhuisje, or Huisje van Gosler, is a national monument in Amsterdam-Centrum and has been one since 1973. The detached building is the only surviving building of the Amsterdam street Joden Houttuinen, which was otherwise demolished in the late 1960s so that the Maupoleum could be erected there.

name: Graaf Floris V van Muiden
en: Graaf Floris V van Muiden is a monumental building at Herengracht 72 in the North Holland town of Muiden.

name: Gran Vista
en: Gran Vista is the (nick)name of an apartment complex in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building forms the northern façade wall of the Houtkopersdwarsstraat and wraps around the corner on both sides, from the Jodenbreestraat in the east to the Waterlooplein in the west. It owes its name to a British investor.

name: Grimburgwal 1-5
en: Grimburgwal 1-5 is a building on the corner of the Grimburgwal and the Nes in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a municipal monument since 1995.

name: Groot Laboratorium
en: The Groot Laboratorium (or simply Groot Lab) is a building in Amsterdam that housed the laboratory of the Bataafsche Petroleum Maatschappij (BPM), later Shell. It lies in the Overhoeks district of Amsterdam-Noord, next to the Toren Overhoeks, and is separated by a footbridge from the Tolhuistuin.

name: Groote Keijser
en: De Groote Keijser was the collective name for six houses on the Keizersgracht in Amsterdam, numbers 242 to 252. The houses were built between 1620 and 1730 and have national monument status. In the late 1970s and early 1980s they became nationally known as a stronghold of the Amsterdam squatting movement.

name: Grote en Kleine Verfdoos
en: De Grote en Kleine Verfdoos are two apartment buildings in the garden suburb of Slotermeer in the Amsterdam borough of Nieuw-West. They were designed by the architect Allert Warners, built between 1954 and 1956 and renovated in 2008-2009. The two blocks cost about 1.7 million guilders to build. The buildings contain dwellings.

name: Grote Kerk (Halfweg)
en: De Grote Kerk was a Protestant church on the Amsterdamsestraatweg in Halfweg. Its originally Gereformeerde (GKN) congregation was founded in 1881. Until 1890 a wooden temporary building was used, after which a small stone church was built, with room for 300 worshippers.

name: Grote of Sint-Nicolaaskerk (Muiden)
en: The Grote of Sint-Nicolaaskerk is a church at Kerkstraat 1 in the North Holland town of Muiden. It is a late-Gothic pseudo-basilica from the early 15th century, though its tower dates from the 12th century. The tower is 28 metres high, built of tufa in a late-Romanesque style. It also served as a lookout tower and lighthouse.

name: H. Nicolaas van Myrakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Tichelkerk, or Tichel, is a church building on the corner of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Tichelstraat in the Amsterdam Jordaan. It was built in 1912 as the Roman Catholic Sint-Antoniuskerk. In 2005 it became the Russian Orthodox Heilige Nikolaas van Myrakerk, and in the same year the building was designated a municipal monument.

name: H.H. Engelbewaarderskerk (Badhoevedorp)
en: The H.H. Engelbewaarderskerk is a Roman Catholic church on the Pa Verkuijllaan in Badhoevedorp. It was built between 1937 and 1939 to a design by Jan van Hardeveld. The priest in charge of construction was F.H.J.M. Cornet from Lijnden. The church is dedicated to the holy guardian angels.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 37
en: Haarlemmerdijk 37 is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designated a municipal monument in November 2004. The Haarlemmerdijk, a continuation of the Haarlemmerstraat, is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 39
en: Haarlemmerdijk 39, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designated a municipal monument in November 2004. The Haarlemmerdijk, a continuation of the Haarlemmerstraat, is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.

name: Haarlemmerdijk 43
en: Haarlemmerdijk 43, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerdijk in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 2004 it was designated a municipal monument. The Haarlemmerdijk, a continuation of the Haarlemmerstraat, is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.

name: Haarlemmerplein 2
en: Haarlemmerplein 2 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum, on the corner of the Haarlemmerplein and the Haarlemmerdijk. It replaced several older houses, was designed by Arthur Staal in the late 1960s and has housed various businesses.

name: Haarlemmerplein 23
en: Haarlemmerplein 23 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerplein in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Haarlemmerplein 4
en: Haarlemmerplein 4, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerplein in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 132-136 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 132-136 in Amsterdam is a school building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 150 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 150 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The house number belongs to a shop unit; the flats above were given an address on the Korte Prinsengracht 25. In 1938 there were still three plots, two of them on the Korte Prinsengracht (25-27).

name: Haarlemmerstraat 2 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 2 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum, Netherlands.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 4 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 4 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat, Amsterdam-Centrum. The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the Amsterdam canal belt. The original buildings have mostly been replaced by new construction, and then by further new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 51 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 51 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. That Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt. Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 60 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 60 in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. That Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt. Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 65-67 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 65-67, Binnen Wieringerstraat 2, in Amsterdam is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.
