Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 77 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 77, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt. Over the centuries the original buildings have largely been replaced by new construction, or new construction on new construction.

name: Haarlemmerstraat 83 (Amsterdam)
en: Haarlemmerstraat 83, Amsterdam, is a building on the Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 2004 it was given the protected status of municipal monument (no. 204019). The Haarlemmerstraat is an age-old street just north of the canal belt.

name: Hallen van Stork
en: The Hallen van Stork, Van Gendthallen or Werkspoorhallen are five interconnected halls of the former Werkspoor-Stork factory on Oostenburg in Amsterdam.

name: Halte Aalsmeerderweg
en: Halte Aalsmeerderweg (telegraphic code: amw) is a former halt on the Dutch Aalsmeer–Haarlem railway line. It was built and operated by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij (HESM) as part of the Haarlemmermeer railway lines.

name: Hamer en Bouwershofje
en: The Hamer en Bouwershofje is a building at Marnixstraat 281 in Amsterdam-Centrum. As the front and back are identical, the building can also be approached from Westerkade 21 on the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Hangbrugmaisonettes
en: The Hangbrugmaisonettes is a block of flats dating from 1970 on the Dijkgraafplein in Amsterdam Osdorp. Until the 1950s there were horticultural businesses here. Amsterdam was bursting at the seams, and in 1958 construction began on the new garden suburb of Osdorp. In 1962 tram line 17 received the Dijkgraafplein as its terminus.

name: Havengebouw (Amsterdam)
en: The Havengebouw is an office building on the De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam. It stands in a prominent position on the IJ. The head office of the Havenbedrijf Amsterdam is based here. Other businesses, institutions and dwellings are also housed in the building.

name: Heilige Nicolaaskerk (Muiden)
en: The Heilige Nicolaaskerk in Muiden is a Roman Catholic church at Herengracht 83 in the municipality of Gooise Meren and is a national monument.

name: Heilige-Familiekerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Heilige-Familiekerk is a church building in Amsterdam-Oost. It stands on the northern edge of the garden village of Betondorp in Watergraafsmeer. This Roman Catholic church rose from 22 May 1951 at the end of the Zaaiersweg, where it connects via a bend to the Rozenburglaan.

name: Heineken Hoek
en: Heineken Hoek was a hospitality establishment in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Hemkade
en: The Hemkade is a street and event venue in Zaandam. It is the northern bank of the North Sea Canal and runs from just beyond the Nieuwe Zeehaven to Zijkanaal G, where the street becomes the Havenstraat. The name derives from the address, Hemkade 48.

name: Hemonystraat 4
en: Hemonystraat 4 is a small building on the Hemonystraat in Amsterdam's De Pijp district.

name: Herberg Zeeburg
en: Herberg Zeeburg is a former inn in Amsterdam-Oost. The inn was built in 1675 on what was then still Diemen territory, near Fort Zeeburg. Ships could moor at the inn at the so-called “Mosselsteiger”. A lively trade developed in livestock, which was unloaded there and sometimes fattened, and in fish.

name: Herengracht 107
en: Herengracht 107 is a building on the Herengracht (107) and Blauwburgwal (17-19) in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Hervormd Lyceum West
en: The Hervormd Lyceum West, or HLW, is a secondary school on the Hemsterhuisstraat and the Johan Huizingalaan in the Slotervaart district of Amsterdam (Nieuw-West). The school is a lyceum with a shared bridging year and the vwo, havo and vmbo (theoretical pathway) streams. In 2015 the school had about 850 pupils.

name: Hervormd Lyceum Zuid
en: The HLZ, also known as Hervormd Lyceum Zuid, is a secondary school on the Brahmsstraat in Amsterdam. The school is a lyceum with a shared bridging year and the vwo and havo streams. In 2026 the school is undergoing a major renovation and is using the school building on the Dongestraat.

name: Het Atelier (Rozengracht)
en: Het Atelier is a building on the Rozengracht in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam. It was formerly called “De Harmonie” and later “Lückner”, and is best known as one of the flashpoints of the Jordaan riot of 1934. It takes its current name from the fact that various clothing-company studios (in the 1960s) were housed in the building.

name: Het Sieraad
en: Het Sieraad is a multifunctional school building on the Postjesweg in Amsterdam. It is owned by the housing association Ymere. It is largely surrounded by water from the Admiralengracht, the Postjeswetering and the Kostverlorenvaart, and was built on a pentagonal plot. Since 20 January 2003 the building has been a national monument.

name: Het Wapen van Riga
en: Het Wapen van Riga is a house in Amsterdam, located at Oudezijds Voorburgwal 14. The house has a stepped gable. Houses of this type were built between about 1600 and 1665. The earliest stepped gables were in a style not yet typical of Amsterdam, the Dutch Renaissance, which is also common in Haarlem, for example.

name: Het Werkteater (theater)
en: Het Werkteater was a theatre in Amsterdam. Its address was Oostenburgergracht 75. Originally Het Werkteater was the home of the theatre company of the same name. From 1997 the building was increasingly rented out for other theatre productions and for television recordings.

name: Het witte dijkhuis
en: Het witte dijkhuis is a building on the Ringdijk in Amsterdam. The street name Ringdijk refers to a street at the foot of the dyke belonging to the centuries-old Ringvaart Watergraafsmeer. The Watergraafsmeer was agricultural land for centuries, with scattered settlements and buildings made up of farmhouses and country estates.

name: Het Zandkasteel (gebouw)
en: Het Zandkasteel is a landmark building in the Amsterdamse Poort district of Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It stands on the Bijlmerplein, enclosed by the Bijlmerdreef, the Anton de Komplein, the Hoogoorddreef and the Foppingadreef. For a long time it served as the head office of ING. Since 2017 it has been a municipal monument.

name: Hillehuis
en: Het Hillehuis is a building on the Gabriël Metsustraat, Museumkwartier, in Amsterdam Oud-Zuid.

name: Hirschgebouw
en: The Hirschgebouw is a monumental building on the Leidseplein and the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies on the south side of the Leidseplein with house numbers 23-31, and on the west side of the small park with numbers 2-2a. It also has a side entrance on the Hirschpassage.

name: Holiday Inn Amsterdam
en: The Holiday Inn Amsterdam (formerly the Esso Motor Hotel Amsterdam, and from 1975 the Amsterdam Crest Hotel) was a hotel on the De Boelelaan in the Zuid borough of Amsterdam. The building still stands and is used as a shelter for refugees.

name: Holland Casino Amsterdam
en: The Holland Casino Amsterdam is a casino on the Max Euweplein in Amsterdam. The building came into use in 1991. The casino is operated by Holland Casino.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 12
en: Hondecoeterstraat 12 in Amsterdam is a building on the corner of the Hondecoeterstraat and the Nicolaas Maesstraat in the Museumkwartier.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 14
en: Hondecoeterstraat 14 in Amsterdam is a building on the Hondecoeterstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has wings on the Frans van Mierisstraat 90-94 and the Nicolaas Maesstraat 111.

name: Hondecoeterstraat 4-8
en: Hondecoeterstraat 4-8 in Amsterdam is a building complex on the Hondecoeterstraat, Amsterdam-Zuid, Museumkwartier.

name: Hoofdkantoor Amsterdamsche Bank
en: The Hoofdkantoor Amsterdamsche Bank is a building on the Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam, built as the head office of the former Amsterdamsche Bank. The Amsterdamse Bank was later merged into the Amro Bank, which in turn merged into ABN Amro.

name: Hoogduitse Schouwburg
en: The Hoogduitse Schouwburg, also known as the Deutsches Theater, was a theatre building in Amsterdam. Performances in this theatre, one of the first in the city, acted as a catalyst for Dutch theatre life. The Hoogduitse Schouwburg was built on the Amstelstraat, number 21, for the Hoogduitsche Tooneelsociëteit.

name: Hotel Boat & Co
en: Hotel Boat & Co, also known as Revaleiland 500, is a hotel on the Revaleiland in the Houthaven district of Amsterdam-West.

name: Hourglass (kantoorgebouw)
en: Hourglass is an office building in the Zuidas business district of Amsterdam. It is built against the office building NoMA House and lies next to the A10 ring road (Zuidasdok project), with its main entrance on the Parnassusweg and its west side on the Clara Schumannstraat.

name: Hugo de Vries-laboratorium
en: The Hugo de Vries-laboratorium is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Plantagebuurt, designed by the architect J.M. van der Mey and built in 1910-1912. It was commissioned by the University of Amsterdam for botany, and in 1948 it was named after Hugo de Vries.

name: Huis De Vicq
en: Huis De Vicq is a mansion on the Gouden Bocht of the Herengracht in Amsterdam, at house number 476. It was built in 1670 and was the national office of the Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds until 12 December 2022.

name: Huis Fuld
en: Huis Fuld is a monumental canal house with a rich interior at Keizersgracht 452 in Amsterdam, on the corner with the Molenpad. It was given national monument status in 1970. The building is rented out as office space, and a number of businesses are housed in it.

name: Huis met de Kolommen
en: The Huis met de Kolommen, also known as the Deutzhuis, has been the official residence of the Amsterdam mayor since 1927. The building was constructed by Paulus Godin in 1672 and lies at Herengracht 502.

name: Huis van Bewaring II (Amstelveenseweg)
en: The Huis van Bewaring II by the Amstelveenseweg (Havenstraat 6) in Amsterdam-Zuid was a penitentiary built in 1890. At the time of construction the prison lay outside the city, in the then still rural municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel. Around 1910 it came to lie within the urban area.

name: Huis Van Brienen
en: Huis Van Brienen (or Huize Van Brienen) is a building at Herengracht 284 in Amsterdam, with an exceptionally rich and well-preserved 18th-century interior. It is among the top 100 most important interiors in the Netherlands. The building has been a national monument since 1970 (no. 1795).

name: Huiszittenweduwenhof
en: The Huiszittenweduwenhof, better known as the Karthuizerhofje, is a hofje (almshouse courtyard) on the Karthuizersstraat in the Amsterdam district of the Jordaan, built in 1650. The design for the hofje, with 104 small ground-floor and upper-floor dwellings, came from city architect Daniël Stalpaert, commissioned by the so-called Huiszittenmeesters.

name: IJburg College
en: The IJburg College is a secondary school in the IJburg residential district of Amsterdam. Pupils can follow vmbo, havo and vwo courses there.

name: IJpromenade 2
en: IJpromenade 2 in Amsterdam is a building on the IJpromenade in Amsterdam-Noord. Since 25 January 2022, on the initiative of the heritage association Heemschut, it has been a municipal monument (200957). It is known as the “Paviljoen Tolhuistuin”.

name: Ir. Lely Lyceum
en: The Ir. Lely Lyceum is a public lyceum for secondary education in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. Pupils are evenly divided across the streams (a third mavo, a third havo and a third vwo). In the early 2020s the school was one of the fastest-growing secondary schools in Amsterdam.

name: James Wattstraat 56-58 (Amsterdam)
en: James Wattstraat 56-58 in Amsterdam is a former church building. It was built as a votive church and used by the Christus Koningparochie in Amsterdam. The original church, with an area of 47 by 27.5 metres, was built by Roman Catholics in 1957-1959.

name: Jan Maijenstraat 11-17
en: Jan Maijenstraat 11-17 is a complex on the Jan Maijenstraat in Amsterdam-West.

name: Jan Swammerdam Instituut
en: The Jan Swammerdam Instituut (JSI), named after Jan Swammerdam, was originally a medical laboratory located in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Jan van Eijckstraat 47
en: Jan van Eijckstraat 47 is a school building from 1956 in Amsterdam, designed by the architectural firm of Cees van der Bom and Commer de Geus. The building lies between the Jan van Eijckstraat (at number 47), the Rubensstraat (15), the Adama van Scheltemaplein (1) and the Memlingstraat in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Johan Huizingalaan 803
en: Johan Huizingalaan 803 is an industrial building in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Justus (gebouw)
en: Justus is a residential tower in the Sluisbuurt on Zeeburgereiland in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Kadijksplein 4
en: Kadijksplein 4, also known as the Koffiehuis van den Volksbond, is a building on the Kadijksplein in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been designated a municipal monument.

name: Kalverstraat 1
en: Kalverstraat 1 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Kalverstraat in Amsterdam. The building extends through to the closed-off Kromelleboogsteeg.

name: Kalverstraat 3-5
en: Kalverstraat 3-5 in Amsterdam-Centrum is a building on the Kalverstraat in Amsterdam. The building extends through to the closed-off Kromelleboogsteeg 5-7.

name: Kanaalstraat 102 (Amsterdam)
en: Kanaalstraat 102 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kanaalstraat in Amsterdam-West. It has been a municipal monument since 14 April 2009.

name: Kanaalstraat 147-149 (Amsterdam)
en: Kanaalstraat 147-149 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kanaalstraat in Amsterdam-West. It has been a municipal monument since 14 April 2009.

name: Kattengat 1
en: Kattengat 1 is the only building with an odd house number on the Kattengat in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Kazerne Muiden
en: The Kazerne in Muiden was built after the adoption of the Vestingwet (Fortress Act) of 1874. The whole Muiden fortification was adapted to modern military thinking on fortress construction. Part of this plan was the building of a bombproof barracks, also known as Fort D.

name: Keesmanblokken
en: The Keesmanblokken is a municipal monument in Amsterdam-West. It lies on the Kijkduinstraat (house numbers 36-64) and the Solebaystraat (numbers 1 to 19a and 21 to 47), both named after naval battles. Space was kept free for schools when the neighbourhood was built, as a district with many children was expected.

name: Keizer Karel College
en: The Keizer Karel College is a school community in Amstelveen offering gymnasium, Technasium at vwo and havo level, atheneum and havo, with a one-year bridging period. The school is generally abbreviated to KKC and is named after Charles the Great (Karel de Grote). The school was originally Catholic and still celebrates Christmas, for example.

name: Keizersgracht 316
en: Keizersgracht 316, Berenstraat 1-3 is a corner building on the south-western side of the junction of the Keizergracht and the Berenstraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. The building bears the name Groote en Kleine Beer, but was initially called the Gebouw William Koch.

name: Keizersgracht 318
en: Keizersgracht 318 in Amsterdam is a building on the south-western side of the Keizergracht, Amsterdam-Centrum, in the section between the Berenstraat and the Runstraat. The area is known as De 9 Straatjes (the Nine Streets).

name: Keizersgracht 554
en: Keizersgracht 554 in Amsterdam is a building on the Keizersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. On 17 June 1970 it was entered in the monuments register with the description: house with a bell gable (also called an inward-curving neck gable) from the second half of the 17th century.

name: Kerk van Holysloot
en: The Kerk van Holysloot, also known as the Holyslootkerk or Het Witte Kerkje, is a Hervormde (Dutch Reformed) church at Dorpsstraat 30 in Holysloot, in the rural area of Amsterdam-Noord. Since 2006 the church has been used by the Protestantse Gemeente Ransdorp-Holysloot.

name: Kerk van Ransdorp
en: The Kerk van Ransdorp is the Dutch Reformed church of Ransdorp in Amsterdam-Noord. The original church was lost to fire in 1715 following a lightning strike.

name: Klarenbeek (Amstel)
en: Klarenbeek is a 17th-century farm in the Groot-Duivendrechtse Polder, on the Ouderkerkerdijk on the east (right) bank of the River Amstel. Up to and including 1921 the whole of the Ouderkerkerdijk and the Groot-Duivendrechtse Polder belonged to the municipality of Ouder-Amstel.

name: Kleine Kerk (Halfweg)
en: De Kleine Kerk in Halfweg is a church building at Wilhelminastraat 15 in Halfweg. Originally a Dutch Reformed church, it received its nickname to distinguish it from the Grote Kerk on the Amsterdamsestraatweg.

name: Klokkenhof
en: Klokkenhof is a block of flats in Amsterdam-Zuid. It lies on the south-east corner of the Surinameplein and the Haarlemmermeerstraat, a street that still just belongs to Amsterdam-Zuid; the boundary lies on the Cornelis Lelylaan. Since its completion it has been an eye-catcher on the square.

name: Kloveniersburgwal 22-24
en: Kloveniersburgwal 22-24 is a national monument on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam, opposite the Trippenhuis. The two houses were built in the course of the 18th century and later merged. On the bel-étage, which has been altered several times, a travel agency has been based since 1986.

name: Kloveniersburgwal 26
en: Kloveniersburgwal 26 in Amsterdam is a building on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is known as the Klein Trippenhuis, as it stands diagonally opposite the Trippenhuis at number 29. Both buildings are national monuments. Number 26 is one of the narrowest buildings in Amsterdam, only about 2.40 metres wide.

name: Koningin Máximakazerne
en: The Koningin Máximakazerne is a barracks of the Dutch armed forces on the Sloterweg in Badhoevedorp. Units of the Koninklijke Marechaussee (KMar) are based there and are responsible for security at Schiphol Airport.

name: Koninginneweg 1
en: Koninginneweg 1 is a building in the Oud-Zuid district of Amsterdam that has been extended over time. It lies on the Van Eeghenstraat and the Koninginneweg, beside the entrance to the Vondelpark on that street. The foundation stone was laid in September 1896 by a granddaughter of the chairman of the Luthersche Diaconessenvereeniging, J.G.

name: Koningsplein 10
en: Koningsplein 10 in Amsterdam is a building on the Koningsplein in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Korenmetershuisje (Amsterdam)
en: The Korenmetershuisje, or Korenmeestershuis, on the Nieuwezijds Kolk in Amsterdam is a former guild house, built in 1620 for the guild of corn measurers to replace an earlier guild house on the same spot.

name: Korte Marnixkade 4
en: Korte Marnixkade 4 is a building in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Kouwenoord
en: Kouwenoord is a residential tower and former honeycomb block, and the Kouwenoordweg is a street, in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The honeycomb block was named on 25 June 1969 after various farms in the Netherlands, including one in Kesteren. In the Rotterdam borough of IJsselmonde, in the Reyeroord district, there is also a street called Kouwenoord.

name: Kraaiennest (winkelcentrum)
en: Kraaiennest was a shopping centre in the south-eastern part of the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It lay below the Karspeldreef, east of the Kraaiennest metro station, and beneath the car park of Kleiburg.

name: Krelis Louwenstraat 4
en: De Krelis Louwenstraat 4 is a building in Amsterdam-West. In the period after the Second World War, housing construction was pursued vigorously through the implementation of Cor van Eesteren's Algemeen Uitbreidingsplan (General Extension Plan).

name: Kruiskerk (Amstelveen)
en: The Kruiskerk in Amstelveen, on the Van der Veerelaan 30a, was designed by architect Ir. Marius Duintjer. The church was built in 1949-1950 on the commission of the Hervormde Gemeente and was put into use on 11 May 1951.

name: Langestraat 61
en: Langestraat 61 is a building on the corner of the Langestraat and the Blauwburgwal in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Langestraat 78
en: Langestraat 78 in Amsterdam is a building on the Langestraat in Amsterdam-Centrum. It has been a national monument since 1970. The history of the building and the gable stone set into it is recorded in the book Gevelstenen van Amsterdam (2007) by researchers Onno Broers (author) and Hans Brandenburg, with photographs by Pancras van de Vlist.

name: Lauriergracht 107
en: Lauriergracht 107 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 109
en: Lauriergracht 109 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 11
en: Lauriergracht 11 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 111
en: Lauriergracht 111 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 112
en: Lauriergracht 112 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 114
en: Lauriergracht 114 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 116
en: Lauriergracht 116 is a national monument on the Lauriergracht in the centre of Amsterdam.

name: Lauriergracht 118
en: Lauriergracht 118 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 12
en: Lauriergracht 12 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 123
en: Lauriergracht 123 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 130-132
en: Lauriergracht 130-132 in Amsterdam is an apartment building on the Lauriergracht in the Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a former church.

name: Lauriergracht 136
en: Lauriergracht 136 is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 138
en: Lauriergracht 138 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Lauriergracht 148
en: Lauriergracht 148 in Amsterdam is a building on the Lauriergracht in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Armeens-Apostolische Kerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Armenian Apostolic Church in Amsterdam is located at Kromboomssloot 22 in the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood of Amsterdam-Centrum. From the beginning of the 17th century, Armenian merchants settled in Amsterdam, mainly in the then-new Lastage district east of the Nieuwmarkt.

name: ABN AMRO-hoofdkantoor
en: The ABN AMRO head office is located in Amsterdam at the Zuidas. At 105 metres and 24 storeys, it is one of the ten tallest buildings in the capital. As its name suggests, it is the head office of the Dutch bank ABN AMRO.

name: Augustanakerk (Amsterdam)
en: The Augustanakerk, also called the Augustanahof (after the new functions the building now houses), is a Lutheran church building in the Amsterdam district of Bos en Lommer.

name: Brouwersgracht 51 (Amsterdam)
en: Brouwersgracht 51 in Amsterdam is a house on the Brouwersgracht in Amsterdam-Centrum. The Brouwersgracht is a centuries-old canal. Much of its original building stock has disappeared, including the building that stood at number 51, which was built at the request of J.J.F.

name: De Ark (Slotervaart)
en: De Ark is a church building in the Slotervaart district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The church was built in 1960-61 to a design by the architect Piet Zanstra. It has been on the municipal monuments list since 2008 and in the Top 100 of young monuments of Amsterdam.

name: Doelenzaal
en: The Doelenzaal was housed in a building at Kloveniersburgwal 87-89 in Amsterdam.

name: Eerste Helmersstraat 271
en: Eerste Helmersstraat 271 in Amsterdam is a building in Amsterdam Oud-West. Tendering for it, as a school, took place on 15 November 1909.

name: Koninginneweg 1
en: Koninginneweg 1 is a building in the Oud-Zuid district of Amsterdam that has been extended over time. It lies on the Van Eeghenstraat and the Koninginneweg, beside the entrance to the Vondelpark on that street.

name: Museum Het Broekerhuis
en: Museum Het Broekerhuis was a museum from 1882 to 1887 at Amstelveenseweg 122 in Amsterdam, showing the contents of the Broekerhuis in Broek in Waterland, collected by Aaltje Fregeres (1810-1900).

name: Sint-Rosaklooster
en: The Sint-Rosaklooster was a Roman Catholic sisters' house at Wingerdweg 4 in Amsterdam-Noord. It was built in 1926-27 to a design by A.J. Kropholler in a traditionalist style.

name: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46
en: Bijdorpstraat 1-29, 46 is a building on the southern edge of the Bijdorpplantsoen in Amsterdam-Oost. Staff housing once stood here, belonging to the Bijlmerbajes prison, which stood just to the north of the small complex.

name: Overtoom 13-17 (Amsterdam)
en: Overtoom 13-17 in Amsterdam is a building on the Overtoom in Amsterdam-West. When the building was erected in 1890/1891 there was still plenty of commercial activity along the Overtoomse Vaart with its Vondelkade.

name: Reynders (café)
en: Reynders (also spelled Reijnders) is a café at Leidseplein 6 in Amsterdam. It is the oldest surviving café on this square and was particularly known in the 1950s and 1960s as an artists' café.

name: Stadhouderskade 129
en: Stadhouderskade 129 is a building on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in De Pijp, Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built to a design by Nicolaas Vos, an estate agent by background but also an architect.

name: Stadhouderskade 74
en: The building Stadhouderskade 74 was a mansion on the Stadhouderskade/Singelgracht in Amsterdam-Zuid. The mansion originally served only as a residence and was designated Stadhouderskade 51N.

name: Station Aalsmeer
en: Station Aalsmeer is a former terminus station on the Haarlemmermeer railway lines: Aalsmeer - Amsterdam Willemspark, Aalsmeer - Haarlem and Aalsmeer - Nieuwersluis-Loenen, built by the Hollandsche Electrische-Spoorweg-Maatschappij (HESM).

name: West-End (Amsterdam)
en: The West-End, later the Ambassade, was a cinema in the Amsterdam district of De Baarsjes. The cinema opened in 1933 on the Jan Evertsenstraat near the Krommert, at what was then the far western edge of the city. It is not known whether the name West-End refers to the London nightlife district of the same name.

name: Kantoorgebouw Van Leer
en: The former office building of Van Leer's Vatenfabrieken lies on the Amsterdamseweg in Amstelveen. It was built in 1958 to a design by Marcel Breuer as the headquarters of the company Van Leer.
